meta.blurb_uz: Manor fermasining hayvonlari ichkilikboz egasi janob Jonsni haydab chiqarib, fermani o'zlari boshqara boshlaydi: «Barcha hayvonlar tengdir». Ammo hokimiyat asta-sekin cho'chqalar qo'liga o'tadi, qoidalar tunda jimgina o'zgartiriladi, va oxir-oqibat ozod hayvonlar avvalgisidan ham og'irroq ahvolga tushadi.
meta.why_uz: Orwellning bu qisqa «ertak»i — hokimiyat, targ'ibot va inqilob qanday qilib o'z g'oyalariga xiyonat qilishi haqidagi eng mashhur asarlardan biri. Tili sodda va aniq, jumlalari qisqa — B2 darajasida ingliz tilini o'rganuvchilar uchun to'liq asl matnni o'qishga eng yaxshi boshlang'ich kitoblardan biri.
meta.author_uz: Jorj Oruell (asl ismi Erik Artur Bler, 1903–1950) — ingliz yozuvchisi va jurnalisti. Hindistonda tug'ilgan, Birmada politsiyachi bo'lib xizmat qilgan, Ispaniya fuqarolar urushida qatnashgan. Har qanday totalitarizmning ashaddiy tanqidchisi; «Hayvonlar fermasi» (1945) va «1984» (1949) romanlari bilan dunyoga mashhur.

chapters.title: Old Major's dream

paras.en: Mr. Jones, of the Manor Farm, had locked the hen-houses for the night, but was too drunk to remember to shut the popholes. With the ring of light from his lantern dancing from side to side, he lurched across the yard, kicked off his boots at the back door, drew himself a last glass of beer from the barrel in the scullery, and made his way up to bed, where Mrs. Jones was already snoring.
paras.uz: «Manor» fermasining egasi janob Jons kechqurun tovuqxonalarni qulflab qo'ydi, lekin shunchalik mast ediki, tuynukchalarni yopishni esdan chiqardi. Fonusining nur halqasi u yoqdan-bu yoqqa raqs tushar ekan, u hovli bo'ylab gandiraklab o'tdi, orqa eshik oldida etiklarini tepib yechdi, yordamchi xonadagi bochkadan o'ziga oxirgi qadah pivo quydi va yotoqqa chiqdi — u yerda Jons xonim allaqachon xurrak otayotgan edi.

paras.en: As soon as the light in the bedroom went out there was a stirring and a fluttering all through the farm buildings. Word had gone round during the day that old Major, the prize Middle White boar, had had a strange dream on the previous night and wished to communicate it to the other animals. It had been agreed that they should all meet in the big barn as soon as Mr. Jones was safely out of the way. Old Major (so he was always called, though the name under which he had been exhibited was Willingdon Beauty) was so highly regarded on the farm that everyone was quite ready to lose an hour’s sleep in order to hear what he had to say.
paras.uz: Yotoqxonadagi chiroq o'chishi bilanoq butun ferma binolarida qimirlash va qanot qoqish boshlandi. Kun bo'yi ferma bo'ylab xabar tarqalgan edi: sovrindor Middl Uayt zotli to'ng'iz keksa Mayor o'tgan kecha g'alati tush ko'ribdi va uni boshqa hayvonlarga aytib bermoqchi ekan. Janob Jons yo'ldan butunlay chiqishi bilanoq hammalari katta molxonada yig'ilishga kelishib olishgan edi. Keksa Mayor (uni doim shunday atashardi, garchi ko'rgazmalarda «Uillingdon go'zali» nomi bilan qatnashgan bo'lsa ham) fermada shunchalik hurmatga sazovor ediki, uning gapini eshitish uchun hamma bir soatlik uyqusidan voz kechishga tayyor edi.

paras.en: At one end of the big barn, on a sort of raised platform, Major was already ensconced on his bed of straw, under a lantern which hung from a beam. He was twelve years old and had lately grown rather stout, but he was still a majestic-looking pig, with a wise and benevolent appearance in spite of the fact that his tushes had never been cut. Before long the other animals began to arrive and make themselves comfortable after their different fashions. First came the three dogs, Bluebell, Jessie, and Pincher, and then the pigs, who settled down in the straw immediately in front of the platform. The hens perched themselves on the window-sills, the pigeons fluttered up to the rafters, the sheep and cows lay down behind the pigs and began to chew the cud.
paras.uz: Katta molxonaning bir chetida, qandaydir baland supada Mayor allaqachon somon to'shagiga qulay joylashib olgan, tepasida to'sinda fonus osilib turardi. U o'n ikki yoshda edi, so'nggi paytlarda ancha semirib qolgandi, lekin hali ham viqorli ko'rinishli cho'chqa edi, so'yloq tishlari hech qachon kesilmaganiga qaramay, dono va mehribon qiyofaga ega edi. Ko'p o'tmay boshqa hayvonlar ham kela boshladi va har biri o'zicha qulay joylashib oldi. Avval uchta it — Blyubell, Jessi va Pincher keldi, keyin cho'chqalar kelib, supaning naq ro'parasidagi somonga cho'zilishdi. Tovuqlar deraza tokchalariga qo'ndi, kaptarlar uchib to'sinlarga chiqdi, qo'ylar va sigirlar cho'chqalarning orqasiga yotib, kavsh qaytara boshladi.

paras.en: The two cart-horses, Boxer and Clover, came in together, walking very slowly and setting down their vast hairy hoofs with great care lest there should be some small animal concealed in the straw. Clover was a stout motherly mare approaching middle life, who had never quite got her figure back after her fourth foal. Boxer was an enormous beast, nearly eighteen hands high, and as strong as any two ordinary horses put together. A white stripe down his nose gave him a somewhat stupid appearance, and in fact he was not of first-rate intelligence, but he was universally respected for his steadiness of character and tremendous powers of work. After the horses came Muriel, the white goat, and Benjamin, the donkey. Benjamin was the oldest animal on the farm, and the worst tempered.
paras.uz: Ikki arava oti — Bokser va Klover birga kirib kelishdi. Ular juda sekin yurishar, somon orasida biror kichik hayvon yashirinib qolmasin deb ulkan, junli tuyoqlarini katta ehtiyotkorlik bilan qo'yishardi. Klover o'rta yoshga yaqinlashib qolgan, to'rtinchi qulunidan keyin qomatini hech tiklay olmagan, to'lagina, onalarcha mehribon biya edi. Bokser esa deyarli o'n sakkiz qarich bo'yli ulkan jonivor bo'lib, har qanday ikki oddiy otni qo'shganda ham ulardan kuchli edi. Burni bo'ylab tushgan oq chiziq unga biroz ahmoqona tus berardi, aslida ham u o'tkir aql egasi emasdi, lekin xarakterining barqarorligi va ulkan mehnat qobiliyati uchun hamma uni hurmat qilardi. Otlardan keyin oq echki Muriel va eshak Benjamin kirib keldi. Benjamin fermadagi eng keksa va eng jahldor hayvon edi.

paras.en: He seldom talked, and when he did, it was usually to make some cynical remark – for instance, he would say that God had given him a tail to keep the flies off, but that he would sooner have had no tail and no flies. Alone among the animals on the farm he never laughed. If asked why, he would say that he saw nothing to laugh at. Nevertheless, without openly admitting it, he was devoted to Boxer; the two of them usually spent their Sundays together in the small paddock beyond the orchard, grazing side by side and never speaking.
paras.uz: U kamdan-kam gapirar, gapirganda ham odatda qandaydir kinoyali gap qilardi — masalan, Xudo unga pashshalarni haydash uchun dum beribdi, lekin u dum ham, pashsha ham bo'lmaganini afzal ko'rardi, derdi. Fermadagi hayvonlar orasida faqat u hech qachon kulmasdi. Nega deb so'rashsa, kuladigan hech narsa ko'rmayapman, derdi. Shunga qaramay, ochiq tan olmasa ham, u Bokserga chin dildan bog'langan edi; ikkovi odatda yakshanbalarni bog'ning narigi tomonidagi kichik o'tloqda birga o'tkazishar, yonma-yon o't yeyishar va hech gaplashishmasdi.

paras.en: The two horses had just lain down when a brood of ducklings, which had lost their mother, filed into the barn, cheeping feebly and wandering from side to side to find some place where they would not be trodden on. Clover made a sort of wall round them with her great foreleg, and the ducklings nestled down inside it and promptly fell asleep. At the last moment Mollie, the foolish, pretty white mare who drew Mr. Jones’s trap, came mincing daintily in, chewing at a lump of sugar. She took a place near the front and began flirting her white mane, hoping to draw attention to the red ribbons it was plaited with. Last of all came the cat, who looked round, as usual, for the warmest place, and finally squeezed herself in between Boxer and Clover; there she purred contentedly throughout Major’s speech without listening to a word of what he was saying.
paras.uz: Ikki ot endigina yotganda, onasidan ajralib qolgan bir to'da o'rdakcha bir qatorda molxonaga kirib keldi; ular zaif chiyillab, oyoq ostida qolib ketmaydigan joy izlab u yoqdan-bu yoqqa sarson bo'lishardi. Klover ulkan oldingi oyog'i bilan ularning atrofini devorday o'rab oldi, o'rdakchalar uning ichiga tiqilib, darhol uxlab qolishdi. So'nggi daqiqada janob Jonsning yengil aravasini tortadigan ahmoqqina, chiroyli oq biya Molli bir parcha qandni chaynagancha nozik qadam tashlab kirib keldi. U oldinroqdan joy oldi va oq yolini silkitib noz qila boshladi — yoliga o'rilgan qizil lentalarga e'tibor tortmoqchi edi. Eng oxirida mushuk keldi; u odatdagidek eng issiq joyni qidirib atrofga qaradi va oxiri Bokser bilan Kloverning o'rtasiga suqilib kirdi; u yerda Mayorning nutqi davomida bir og'iz so'zini ham tinglamasdan mamnun xurillab yotdi.

paras.en: All the animals were now present except Moses, the tame raven, who slept on a perch behind the back door. When Major saw that they had all made themselves comfortable and were waiting attentively, he cleared his throat and began: ‘Comrades, you have heard already about the strange dream that I had last night. But I will come to the dream later. I have something else to say first. I do not think, comrades, that I shall be with you for many months longer, and before I die, I feel it my duty to pass on to you such wisdom as I have acquired. I have had a long life, I have had much time for thought as I lay alone in my stall, and I think I may say that I understand the nature of life on this earth as well as any animal now living. It is about this that I wish to speak to you.
paras.uz: Orqa eshik ortidagi qo'nimda uxlaydigan qo'lga o'rgatilgan qarg'a Mozesdan boshqa barcha hayvonlar endi shu yerda edi. Hammasi qulay joylashib, diqqat bilan kutib turganini ko'rgan Mayor tomog'ini qirib, gap boshladi: «O'rtoqlar, kecha ko'rgan g'alati tushim haqida allaqachon eshitgansizlar. Lekin tushimga keyinroq kelaman. Avval aytadigan boshqa gapim bor. O'rtoqlar, men sizlar bilan yana ko'p oylar birga bo'lmayman deb o'ylayman, va o'lishimdan oldin orttirgan donoligimni sizlarga yetkazishni burchim deb bilaman. Men uzoq umr ko'rdim, qo'rada yolg'iz yotib o'ylash uchun ko'p vaqtim bo'ldi, va menimcha, yer yuzidagi hayotning mohiyatini hozir tirik bo'lgan har qanday hayvon kabi yaxshi tushunaman deyishim mumkin. Sizlarga aynan shu haqda gapirmoqchiman.

paras.en: ‘Now, comrades, what is the nature of this life of ours? Let us face it: our lives are miserable, laborious, and short. We are born, we are given just so much food as will keep the breath in our bodies, and those of us who are capable of it are forced to work to the last atom of our strength; and the very instant that our usefulness has come to an end we are slaughtered with hideous cruelty. No animal in England knows the meaning of happiness or leisure after he is a year old. No animal in England is free. The life of an animal is misery and slavery: that is the plain truth.
paras.uz: Xo'sh, o'rtoqlar, bu hayotimizning mohiyati nima? Keling, tan olaylik: hayotimiz baxtsiz, mashaqqatli va qisqa. Biz tug'ilamiz, bizga faqat jonimiz tanamizda qolishiga yetadigan miqdorda ovqat beriladi, qodir bo'lganlarimiz esa kuchimizning so'nggi zarrasigacha ishlashga majbur qilinadi; va foydamiz tugagan o'sha lahzadayoq bizni dahshatli shafqatsizlik bilan so'yishadi. Angliyada bir yoshdan oshgan biror hayvon baxt yoki dam olish nimaligini bilmaydi. Angliyada biror hayvon ozod emas. Hayvonning hayoti — azob va qullik: bu oddiy haqiqat.

paras.en: ‘But is this simply part of the order of nature? Is it because this land of ours is so poor that it cannot afford a decent life to those who dwell upon it? No, comrades, a thousand times no! The soil of England is fertile, its climate is good, it is capable of affording food in abundance to an enormously greater number of animals than now inhabit it. This single farm of ours would support a dozen horses, twenty cows, hundreds of sheep – and all of them living in a comfort and a dignity that are now almost beyond our imagining. Why then do we continue in this miserable condition? Because nearly the whole of the produce of our labour is stolen from us by human beings. There, comrades, is the answer to all our problems. It is summed up in a single word – Man. Man is the only real enemy we have. Remove Man from the scene, and the root cause of hunger and overwork is abolished for ever.
paras.uz: Lekin bu shunchaki tabiat tartibining bir qismimi? Yerimiz shunchalik kambag'alki, unda yashovchilarga munosib hayot bera olmaydimi? Yo'q, o'rtoqlar, ming marta yo'q! Angliyaning tuprog'i serhosil, iqlimi yaxshi, u hozir unda yashayotganlardan ancha ko'p hayvonni mo'l-ko'l ovqat bilan ta'minlay oladi. Birgina shu fermamiz o'nlab otni, yigirmata sigirni, yuzlab qo'yni boqa olardi — va ularning hammasi hozir biz tasavvur ham qila olmaydigan farovonlik va qadr-qimmat bilan yashardi. Unda nega biz bu baxtsiz ahvolda qolyapmiz? Chunki mehnatimiz mahsulining deyarli hammasini insonlar bizdan o'g'irlaydi. Mana, o'rtoqlar, barcha muammolarimizning javobi. U bitta so'zda jamlangan — Inson. Inson — bizning yagona haqiqiy dushmanimiz. Insonni sahnadan olib tashlang — ochlik va haddan tashqari mehnatning tub sababi abadiy yo'qoladi.

paras.en: ‘Man is the only creature that consumes without producing. He does not give milk, he does not lay eggs, he is too weak to pull the plough, he cannot run fast enough to catch rabbits. Yet he is lord of all the animals. He sets them to work, he gives back to them the bare minimum that will prevent them from starving, and the rest he keeps for himself. Our labour tills the soil, our dung fertilises it, and yet there is not one of us that owns more than his bare skin. You cows that I see before me, how many thousands of gallons of milk have you given during this last year? And what has happened to that milk which should have been breeding up sturdy calves? Every drop of it has gone down the throats of our enemies.
paras.uz: Inson — ishlab chiqarmasdan iste'mol qiladigan yagona mavjudot. U sut bermaydi, tuxum qo'ymaydi, omoch tortishga kuchi yetmaydi, quyon tutish uchun yetarlicha tez yugura olmaydi. Shunga qaramay u barcha hayvonlarning hukmdori. U ularni ishlatadi, ochlikdan o'lmasliklari uchun eng kam narsani qaytarib beradi, qolganini esa o'ziga oladi. Bizning mehnatimiz yerni haydaydi, go'ngimiz uni o'g'itlaydi, lekin oramizda yalang'och terisidan boshqa narsaga ega bo'lgan birortamiz yo'q. Oldimda ko'rib turgan sigirlar, o'tgan yili necha ming gallon sut berdingiz? Mustahkam buzoqlarni boqishi kerak bo'lgan o'sha sut qayerga ketdi? Uning har bir tomchisi dushmanlarimizning tomog'idan o'tib ketdi.

paras.en: And you hens, how many eggs have you laid in this last year, and how many of those eggs ever hatched into chickens? The rest have all gone to market to bring in money for Jones and his men. And you, Clover, where are those four foals you bore, who should have been the support and pleasure of your old age? Each was sold at a year old – you will never see one of them again. In return for your four confinements and all your labour in the fields, what have you ever had except your bare rations and a stall?
paras.uz: Sizlar-chi, tovuqlar, o'tgan yili qancha tuxum qo'ydingiz va ulardan nechtasi jo'jaga aylandi? Qolganlari Jons va uning odamlariga pul keltirish uchun bozorga ketdi. Sen-chi, Klover, qariganingda suyanching va quvonching bo'lishi kerak bo'lgan to'rtta quluning qani? Har biri bir yoshida sotib yuborildi — ularning birortasini hech qachon boshqa ko'rmaysan. To'rt marta tug'ishing va dalalardagi butun mehnating evaziga senga qorningni zo'rg'a to'yg'azadigan ulush va bir qo'radan boshqa nima berildi?

paras.en: ‘And even the miserable lives we lead are not allowed to reach their natural span. For myself I do not grumble, for I am one of the lucky ones. I am twelve years old and have had over four hundred children. Such is the natural life of a pig. But no animal escapes the cruel knife in the end. You young porkers who are sitting in front of me, every one of you will scream your lives out at the block within a year. To that horror we all must come – cows, pigs, hens, sheep, everyone. Even the horses and the dogs have no better fate. You, Boxer, the very day that those great muscles of yours lose their power, Jones will sell you to the knacker, who will cut your throat and boil you down for the foxhounds. As for the dogs, when they grow old and toothless, Jones ties a brick round their necks and drowns them in the nearest pond.
paras.uz: Bundan tashqari, kechirayotgan bu baxtsiz hayotimiz ham tabiiy muddatiga yetishiga yo'l qo'yilmaydi. O'zim uchun nolimayman, chunki men omadlilardanman. Men o'n ikki yoshdaman va to'rt yuzdan ortiq bolam bor. Cho'chqaning tabiiy hayoti shunday. Lekin oxir-oqibat hech bir hayvon shafqatsiz pichoqdan qutulolmaydi. Oldimda o'tirgan yosh cho'chqachalar, bir yil ichida har biringiz kunda ustida jon talvasasida chinqirib o'lasiz. Bu dahshatga hammamiz yetib boramiz — sigirlar, cho'chqalar, tovuqlar, qo'ylar, hamma. Hatto otlar va itlarning taqdiri ham bundan yaxshi emas. Sen, Bokser, o'sha ulkan mushaklaring kuchdan qolgan kuniyoq Jons seni o'lakso qassobiga sotadi, u esa tomog'ingni kesib, tozi itlar uchun qaynatib yuboradi. Itlarga kelsak, ular qarib, tishsiz qolganda Jons bo'yinlariga g'isht bog'lab, eng yaqin hovuzga cho'ktiradi.

paras.en: ‘Is it not crystal clear, then, comrades, that all the evils of this life of ours spring from the tyranny of human beings? Only get rid of Man, and the produce of our labour would be our own. Almost overnight we could become rich and free. What then must we do? Why, work night and day, body and soul, for the overthrow of the human race! That is my message to you, comrades: Rebellion! I do not know when that Rebellion will come, it might be in a week or in a hundred years, but I know, as surely as I see this straw beneath my feet, that sooner or later justice will be done. Fix your eyes on that, comrades, throughout the short remainder of your lives! And above all, pass on this message of mine to those who come after you, so that future generations shall carry on the struggle until it is victorious.
paras.uz: Demak, o'rtoqlar, hayotimizdagi barcha yovuzliklar insonlarning zulmidan kelib chiqishi billurdek ravshan emasmi? Faqat Insondan qutulsak bas, mehnatimiz mahsuli o'zimizniki bo'lardi. Deyarli bir kechada boy va ozod bo'lishimiz mumkin edi. Unda nima qilishimiz kerak? Albatta, inson zotini ag'darish uchun kechayu kunduz, jonu dil bilan mehnat qilish! O'rtoqlar, sizlarga aytadigan gapim shu: Qo'zg'olon! O'sha Qo'zg'olon qachon bo'lishini bilmayman, bir haftadan keyinmi yoki yuz yildanmi, lekin oyog'im ostidagi bu somonni ko'rib turganimdek aniq bilamanki, ertami-kechmi adolat qaror topadi. O'rtoqlar, qisqa umringizning qolgan qismi davomida nigohingizni shunga qadab turing! Va eng muhimi, bu xabarimni sizdan keyin keladiganlarga yetkazing, toki kelajak avlodlar kurashni g'alabaga qadar davom ettirsin.

paras.en: ‘And remember, comrades, your resolution must never falter. No argument must lead you astray. Never listen when they tell you that Man and the animals have a common interest, that the prosperity of the one is the prosperity of the others. It is all lies. Man serves the interests of no creature except himself. And among us animals let there be perfect unity, perfect comradeship in the struggle. All men are enemies. All animals are comrades.’
paras.uz: Va unutmang, o'rtoqlar, qat'iyatingiz hech qachon bo'shashmasligi kerak. Hech qanday dalil sizni yo'ldan ozdirmasin. Inson bilan hayvonlarning manfaati umumiy, birining farovonligi boshqasining farovonligi degan gaplarga hech qachon quloq solmang. Bularning hammasi yolg'on. Inson o'zidan boshqa hech bir mavjudotning manfaatiga xizmat qilmaydi. Biz hayvonlar orasida esa kurashda to'liq birlik, to'liq o'rtoqlik bo'lsin. Barcha odamlar — dushman. Barcha hayvonlar — o'rtoq.»

paras.en: At this moment there was a tremendous uproar. While Major was speaking four large rats had crept out of their holes and were sitting on their hindquarters, listening to him. The dogs had suddenly caught sight of them, and it was only by a swift dash for their holes that the rats saved their lives. Major raised his trotter for silence.
paras.uz: Shu payt dahshatli shovqin ko'tarildi. Mayor gapirayotganda to'rtta katta kalamush inlaridan chiqib, orqa oyoqlarida o'tirgancha uni tinglayotgan edi. Itlar birdan ularni ko'rib qolishdi va kalamushlar faqat inlariga chaqqon otilib, jonlarini saqlab qolishdi. Mayor jimlik so'rab tuyog'ini ko'tardi.

paras.en: ‘Comrades,’ he said, ‘here is a point that must be settled. The wild creatures, such as rats and rabbits – are they our friends or our enemies? Let us put it to the vote. I propose this question to the meeting: Are rats comrades?’
paras.uz: «O'rtoqlar, — dedi u, — mana hal qilinishi kerak bo'lgan bir masala. Kalamushlar va quyonlar kabi yovvoyi jonivorlar — ular bizning do'stlarimizmi yoki dushmanlarimizmi? Keling, ovozga qo'yaylik. Yig'ilishga shu savolni taklif qilaman: Kalamushlar o'rtoqmi?»

paras.en: The vote was taken at once, and it was agreed by an overwhelming majority that rats were comrades. There were only four dissentients, the three dogs and the cat, who was afterwards discovered to have voted on both sides. Major continued: ‘I have little more to say. I merely repeat, remember always your duty of enmity towards Man and all his ways. Whatever goes upon two legs is an enemy. Whatever goes upon four legs, or has wings, is a friend. And remember also that in fighting against Man, we must not come to resemble him. Even when you have conquered him, do not adopt his vices. No animal must ever live in a house, or sleep in a bed, or wear clothes, or drink alcohol, or smoke tobacco, or touch money, or engage in trade. All the habits of Man are evil. And, above all, no animal must ever tyrannise over his own kind. Weak or strong, clever or simple, we are all brothers. No animal must ever kill any other animal. All animals are equal.
paras.uz: Darhol ovoz berildi va mutlaq ko'pchilik ovoz bilan kalamushlar o'rtoq deb kelishildi. Faqat to'rtta qarshi ovoz bo'ldi — uchta it va mushuk, keyinroq ma'lum bo'lishicha, mushuk ikkala tomonga ham ovoz bergan ekan. Mayor davom etdi: «Aytadigan gapim kam qoldi. Faqat takrorlayman: Insonga va uning barcha yo'llariga dushmanlik burchingizni doim yodda tuting. Ikki oyoqda yuradigan har qanday narsa — dushman. To'rt oyoqda yuradigan yoki qanoti bor har qanday narsa — do'st. Va yana shuni yodda tutingki, Insonga qarshi kurashda biz unga o'xshab qolmasligimiz kerak. Hatto uni yenggan taqdiringizda ham uning illatlarini qabul qilmang. Hech bir hayvon hech qachon uyda yashamasligi, karavotda uxlamasligi, kiyim kiymasligi, spirtli ichimlik ichmasligi, tamaki chekmasligi, pulga tegmasligi yoki savdo bilan shug'ullanmasligi kerak. Insonning barcha odatlari yovuz. Va eng muhimi, hech bir hayvon hech qachon o'z jinsdoshlari ustidan zulm qilmasligi kerak. Zaifmi yoki kuchli, aqllimi yoki sodda — hammamiz birodarmiz. Hech bir hayvon boshqa hayvonni hech qachon o'ldirmasligi kerak. Barcha hayvonlar teng.

paras.en: ‘And now, comrades, I will tell you about my dream of last night. I cannot describe that dream to you. It was a dream of the earth as it will be when Man has vanished. But it reminded me of something that I had long forgotten. Many years ago, when I was a little pig, my mother and the other sows used to sing an old song of which they knew only the tune and the first three words. I had known that tune in my infancy, but it had long since passed out of my mind. Last night, however, it came back to me in my dream. And what is more, the words of the song also came back – words, I am certain, which were sung by the animals of long ago and have been lost to memory for generations. I will sing you that song now, comrades. I am old and my voice is hoarse, but when I have taught you the tune, you can sing it better for yourselves. It is called Beasts of England.’
paras.uz: Endi, o'rtoqlar, sizlarga kechagi tushimni aytib beraman. U tushni sizlarga ta'riflab berolmayman. Bu Inson yo'qolgandan keyingi yer haqidagi tush edi. Lekin u menga allaqachon unutib yuborgan bir narsani eslatdi. Ko'p yillar oldin, men kichkina cho'chqacha bo'lganimda, onam va boshqa ona cho'chqalar bir eski qo'shiqni kuylashardi, ular uning faqat kuyini va dastlabki uchta so'zini bilishardi. Men u kuyni go'dakligimda bilardim, lekin u allaqachon xotiramdan chiqib ketgan edi. Biroq kecha u tushimda menga qaytib keldi. Bundan tashqari, qo'shiqning so'zlari ham qaytib keldi — ishonchim komilki, bu so'zlarni qadim zamonlar hayvonlari kuylagan va ular avlodlar davomida xotiradan yo'qolgan. Hozir o'sha qo'shiqni sizlarga kuylab beraman, o'rtoqlar. Men qariman, ovozim xirillaydi, lekin sizlarga kuyni o'rgatganimdan keyin uni o'zingiz yaxshiroq kuylay olasiz. U «Angliya hayvonlari» deb ataladi.»

paras.en: Old Major cleared his throat and began to sing. As he had said, his voice was hoarse, but he sang well enough, and it was a stirring tune, something between Clementine and La Cucaracha. The words ran:
paras.uz: Keksa Mayor tomog'ini qirib, kuylay boshladi. O'zi aytganidek, ovozi xirillardi, lekin u yetarlicha yaxshi kuyladi, kuy esa jo'shqin bo'lib, «Klementina» bilan «La Kukaracha» o'rtasidagi narsaga o'xshardi. So'zlari shunday edi:

paras.en: Beasts of England, beasts of Ireland, / Beasts of every land and clime, / Hearken to my joyful tidings / Of the golden future time.
paras.uz: Angliya va Irlandiya hayvonlari, / Har bir yurt, har iqlim jonzoti, / Quloq soling quvonchli xabarga — / Oltin kelajak saodati.

paras.en: Soon or late the day is coming, / Tyrant Man shall be o’erthrown, / And the fruitful fields of England / Shall be trod by beasts alone.
paras.uz: Ertami-kechmi kun kelur, / Zolim Inson ag'darilur, / Angliyaning serhosil dalalarini / Faqat hayvonlar oyog'i bosur.

paras.en: Rings shall vanish from our noses, / And the harness from our back, / Bit and spur shall rust forever, / Cruel whips no more shall crack.
paras.uz: Burnimizdan halqalar yo'qolur, / Belimizdan egar-jabduq ketar, / Suvliq-u shpor abadiy zanglar, / Qamchilar endi chirsillamas.

paras.en: Riches more than mind can picture, / Wheat and barley, oats and hay, / Clover, beans, and mangel-wurzels / Shall be ours upon that day.
paras.uz: Aql bovar qilmas boylik — / Bug'doy, arpa, suli, pichan, / Beda, dukkak va xashaki lavlagi / O'sha kuni bizniki bo'lur hamon.

paras.en: Bright will shine the fields of England, / Purer shall its waters be, / Sweeter yet shall blow its breezes / On the day that sets us free.
paras.uz: Angliya dalalari porlar yorqin, / Suvlari bo'lur yanada toza, / Shabadasi esar yanada shirin / Bizni ozod qilgan o'sha kunda.

paras.en: For that day we all must labour, / Though we die before it break; / Cows and horses, geese and turkeys, / All must toil for freedom’s sake.
paras.uz: O'sha kun uchun mehnat qilmog'imiz kerak, / Garchi u tong otmasdan o'lsak ham; / Sigir-u ot, g'oz-u kurka, / Hamma ozodlik uchun tortsin zahmat.

paras.en: Beasts of England, beasts of Ireland, / Beasts of every land and clime, / Hearken well and spread my tidings / Of the golden future time.
paras.uz: Angliya va Irlandiya hayvonlari, / Har bir yurt, har iqlim jonzoti, / Yaxshi tinglang, tarqating xabarimni — / Oltin kelajak saodati.

paras.en: The singing of this song threw the animals into the wildest excitement. Almost before Major had reached the end, they had begun singing it for themselves. Even the stupidest of them had already picked up the tune and a few of the words, and as for the clever ones, such as the pigs and dogs, they had the entire song by heart within a few minutes. And then, after a few preliminary tries, the whole farm burst out into 'Beasts of England' in tremendous unison. The cows lowed it, the dogs whined it, the sheep bleated it, the horses whinnied it, the ducks quacked it. They were so delighted with the song that they sang it right through five times in succession, and might have continued singing it all night if they had not been interrupted.
paras.uz: Bu qo'shiq hayvonlarni eng kuchli hayajonga soldi. Mayor oxiriga yetmasidanoq ular uni o'zlari kuylay boshlashdi. Hatto eng ahmoqlari ham kuyni va bir nechta so'zni ilib olgan edi, cho'chqalar va itlar kabi aqllilari esa bir necha daqiqa ichida qo'shiqni to'liq yod olishdi. Keyin bir necha dastlabki urinishlardan so'ng butun ferma bir ovozdan ulkan «Angliya hayvonlari»ni boshlab yubordi. Sigirlar uni mo'radi, itlar g'ingshidi, qo'ylar ma'radi, otlar kishnadi, o'rdaklar g'oqilladi. Qo'shiq ularga shunchalik yoqdiki, uni ketma-ket besh marta boshidan oxirigacha kuylashdi va agar xalaqit berilmaganida tun bo'yi kuylashda davom etishlari mumkin edi.

paras.en: Unfortunately, the uproar awoke Mr. Jones, who sprang out of bed, making sure that there was a fox in the yard. He seized the gun which always stood in a corner of his bedroom, and let fly a charge of number 6 shot into the darkness. The pellets buried themselves in the wall of the barn and the meeting broke up hurriedly. Everyone fled to his own sleeping-place. The birds jumped on to their perches, the animals settled down in the straw, and the whole farm was asleep in a moment.
paras.uz: Afsuski, shovqin janob Jonsni uyg'otib yubordi; u hovliga tulki kirdi, deb ishonib, karavotidan sakrab turdi. Yotoqxonasining burchagida doim turadigan miltiqni olib, qorong'ilikka oltinchi raqamli o'q bilan o'q uzdi. Sochma o'qlar molxona devoriga qadaldi va yig'ilish shosha-pisha tarqaldi. Har kim o'z uyqu joyiga qochdi. Qushlar qo'nimlariga sakrab chiqdi, hayvonlar somonga cho'zildi va bir lahzada butun ferma uyquga ketdi.

quiz.q: Who is the only real enemy of the animals, according to Major?
How were the rats classified by the vote?
quiz.why_uz: Ko'pchilik ovoz bilan kalamushlar o'rtoq deb topildi.

chapters.recap_uz: Manor fermasida keksa to'ng'iz Mayor hayvonlarni yig'ib, ularning hayoti baxtsiz, mashaqqatli va qisqa ekanini, buning yagona sababi Inson ekanini aytadi. U qo'zg'olonga chaqiradi, «Barcha hayvonlar teng» deydi va ularga «Angliya hayvonlari» qo'shig'ini o'rgatadi.

chapters.title: The Rebellion

paras.en: Three nights later old Major died peacefully in his sleep. His body was buried at the foot of the orchard.
paras.uz: Uch kechadan keyin keksa Mayor uyqusida osoyishta jon berdi. Uning jasadi bog'ning etagiga dafn etildi.

paras.en: This was early in March. During the next three months there was much secret activity. Major’s speech had given to the more intelligent animals on the farm a completely new outlook on life. They did not know when the Rebellion predicted by Major would take place, they had no reason for thinking that it would be within their own lifetime, but they saw clearly that it was their duty to prepare for it. The work of teaching and organising the others fell naturally upon the pigs, who were generally recognised as being the cleverest of the animals. Pre-eminent among the pigs were two young boars named Snowball and Napoleon, whom Mr. Jones was breeding up for sale. Napoleon was a large, rather fierce-looking Berkshire boar, the only Berkshire on the farm, not much of a talker, but with a reputation for getting his own way.
paras.uz: Bu mart oyining boshida edi. Keyingi uch oy davomida ko'p yashirin harakatlar bo'ldi. Mayorning nutqi fermadagi aqlliroq hayvonlarga hayotga butunlay yangi nigoh bergan edi. Ular Mayor bashorat qilgan Qo'zg'olon qachon bo'lishini bilishmasdi, uning o'z umrlari davomida bo'lishiga ishonish uchun hech qanday asos yo'q edi, lekin unga tayyorlanish o'z burchlari ekanini aniq ko'rishardi. Boshqalarni o'qitish va tashkil etish ishi tabiiy ravishda hayvonlarning eng aqllisi deb tan olingan cho'chqalar zimmasiga tushdi. Cho'chqalar orasida janob Jons sotish uchun boqayotgan Snoubol va Napoleon ismli ikki yosh erkak cho'chqa ajralib turardi. Napoleon yirik, ancha shafqatsiz ko'rinishli berkshir zotli erkak cho'chqa edi — fermadagi yagona berkshir, ko'p gapirmasdi, lekin har doim aytganini qildirishi bilan nom chiqargan edi.

paras.en: Snowball was a more vivacious pig than Napoleon, quicker in speech and more inventive, but was not considered to have the same depth of character. All the other male pigs on the farm were porkers. The best known among them was a small fat pig named Squealer, with very round cheeks, twinkling eyes, nimble movements, and a shrill voice. He was a brilliant talker, and when he was arguing some difficult point he had a way of skipping from side to side and whisking his tail which was somehow very persuasive. The others said of Squealer that he could turn black into white.
paras.uz: Snoubol Napoleondan ko'ra jonliroq cho'chqa edi, gapga chaqqonroq va ixtirochiroq edi, lekin xarakteri unchalik chuqur emas deb hisoblanardi. Fermadagi qolgan barcha erkak cho'chqalar go'shtga boqilayotgan cho'chqachalar edi. Ular orasida eng mashhuri Skviler ismli kichkina semiz cho'chqa edi — yuzi juda dumaloq, ko'zlari chaqnab turadigan, harakatlari epchil va ovozi chiyildoq. U ajoyib notiq edi va qandaydir qiyin masalani isbotlayotganda u yoqdan-bu yoqqa sakrab, dumini silkitib qo'yish odati bor edi, bu esa qandaydir juda ishonarli tuyulardi. Boshqalar Skviler haqida u qorani oq qilib ko'rsata oladi, deyishardi.

paras.en: These three had elaborated old Major’s teachings into a complete system of thought, to which they gave the name of Animalism. Several nights a week, after Mr. Jones was asleep, they held secret meetings in the barn and expounded the principles of Animalism to the others. At the beginning they met with much stupidity and apathy. Some of the animals talked of the duty of loyalty to Mr. Jones, whom they referred to as ‘Master,’ or made elementary remarks such as ‘Mr. Jones feeds us. If he were gone, we should starve to death.’ Others asked such questions as ‘Why should we care what happens after we are dead?’ or ‘If this Rebellion is to happen anyway, what difference does it make whether we work for it or not?’, and the pigs had great difficulty in making them see that this was contrary to the spirit of Animalism. The stupidest questions of all were asked by Mollie, the white mare. The very first question she asked Snowball was: ‘Will there still be sugar after the Rebellion? ’
paras.uz: Bu uchovi keksa Mayorning ta'limotini to'liq fikr tizimiga aylantirib, unga Hayvonizm deb nom berishdi. Haftada bir necha kecha, janob Jons uxlab qolgandan keyin, ular molxonada yashirin yig'ilishlar o'tkazib, boshqalarga Hayvonizm tamoyillarini tushuntirishardi. Boshida ular ko'p ahmoqlik va befarqlikka duch kelishdi. Ba'zi hayvonlar «Xo'jayin» deb ataydigan janob Jonsga sodiqlik burchi haqida gapirishar yoki «Janob Jons bizni boqadi. U ketsa, ochdan o'lamiz» kabi oddiy gaplarni aytishardi. Boshqalar «O'lganimizdan keyin nima bo'lishi bizga nima?» yoki «Agar bu Qo'zg'olon baribir bo'ladigan bo'lsa, uning uchun ishlashimiz yoki ishlamasligimizning nima farqi bor?» kabi savollarni berishar, cho'chqalar esa bu Hayvonizm ruhiga zid ekanini tushuntirishda katta qiyinchilik tortishardi. Eng ahmoqona savollarni oq biya Molli berardi. U Snouboldan bergan eng birinchi savol shu edi: «Qo'zg'olondan keyin ham qand bo'ladimi?»

paras.en: ‘No,’ said Snowball firmly. ‘We have no means of making sugar on this farm. Besides, you do not need sugar. You will have all the oats and hay you want.’
paras.uz: «Yo'q, — dedi Snoubol qat'iy ohangda. — Bu fermada qand ishlab chiqarishga imkoniyatimiz yo'q. Bundan tashqari, senga qandning keragi yo'q. Xohlaganingcha suli va pichaning bo'ladi.»

paras.en: ‘And shall I still be allowed to wear ribbons in my mane?’ asked Mollie.
paras.uz: «Yolimga lenta taqishimga ruxsat beriladimi?» — so'radi Molli.

paras.en: ‘Comrade,’ said Snowball, ‘those ribbons that you are so devoted to are the badge of slavery. Can you not understand that liberty is worth more than ribbons?’
paras.uz: «O'rtoq, — dedi Snoubol, — sen shunchalik yaxshi ko'radigan o'sha lentalar qullik belgisi. Ozodlik lentadan qimmatroq ekanini tushunolmaysanmi?»

paras.en: Mollie agreed, but she did not sound very convinced.
paras.uz: Molli rozi bo'ldi, lekin ovozi unchalik ishonchli eshitilmadi.

paras.en: The pigs had an even harder struggle to counteract the lies put about by Moses, the tame raven. Moses, who was Mr. Jones’s especial pet, was a spy and a tale-bearer, but he was also a clever talker. He claimed to know of the existence of a mysterious country called Sugarcandy Mountain, to which all animals went when they died. It was situated somewhere up in the sky, a little distance beyond the clouds, Moses said. In Sugarcandy Mountain it was Sunday seven days a week, clover was in season all the year round, and lump sugar and linseed cake grew on the hedges. The animals hated Moses because he told tales and did no work, but some of them believed in Sugarcandy Mountain, and the pigs had to argue very hard to persuade them that there was no such place.
paras.uz: Cho'chqalar qo'lga o'rgatilgan qarg'a Mozes tarqatgan yolg'onlarga qarshi kurashda yana ham qiyinroq ahvolga tushishdi. Janob Jonsning alohida erkatoyi bo'lgan Mozes ayg'oqchi va chaqimchi edi, lekin ayni paytda gapga usta ham edi. U barcha hayvonlar o'lganda boradigan Qandtog' degan sirli mamlakat borligini bilaman, deb da'vo qilardi. Mozesning aytishicha, u osmonda, bulutlardan sal narida joylashgan ekan. Qandtog'da haftaning yetti kuni ham yakshanba, beda yil bo'yi pishib turadi, to'siqlarda esa bo'lak qand va zig'ir kunjarasi o'sadi. Hayvonlar Mozesni chaqimchilik qilgani va hech ish qilmagani uchun yomon ko'rishardi, lekin ba'zilari Qandtog'ga ishonishardi va cho'chqalar bunday joy yo'qligiga ularni ishontirish uchun juda qattiq bahslashishga majbur bo'lishardi.

paras.en: Their most faithful disciples were the two cart-horses, Boxer and Clover. These two had great difficulty in thinking anything out for themselves, but having once accepted the pigs as their teachers, they absorbed everything that they were told, and passed it on to the other animals by simple arguments. They were unfailing in their attendance at the secret meetings in the barn, and led the singing of 'Beasts of England', with which the meetings always ended.
paras.uz: Ularning eng sodiq shogirdlari ikki arava oti — Bokser va Klover edi. Bu ikkovi biror narsani o'zicha o'ylab topishda juda qiynalishardi, lekin bir marta cho'chqalarni ustoz deb qabul qilgach, aytilgan hamma narsani singdirib olishar va oddiy dalillar bilan boshqa hayvonlarga yetkazishardi. Ular molxonadagi yashirin yig'ilishlarni hech qachon qoldirishmas, yig'ilishlar doim u bilan tugaydigan «Angliya hayvonlari» qo'shig'ini boshlab berishardi.

paras.en: Now, as it turned out, the Rebellion was achieved much earlier and more easily than anyone had expected. In past years Mr. Jones, although a hard master, had been a capable farmer, but of late he had fallen on evil days. He had become much disheartened after losing money in a lawsuit, and had taken to drinking more than was good for him. For whole days at a time he would lounge in his Windsor chair in the kitchen, reading the newspapers, drinking, and occasionally feeding Moses on crusts of bread soaked in beer. His men were idle and dishonest, the fields were full of weeds, the buildings wanted roofing, the hedges were neglected, and the animals were underfed.
paras.uz: Ma'lum bo'lishicha, Qo'zg'olon hamma kutganidan ancha erta va osonroq amalga oshdi. O'tgan yillarda janob Jons qattiqqo'l xo'jayin bo'lsa ham, uddaburon fermer edi, lekin so'nggi paytlarda boshiga og'ir kunlar tushgan edi. Sud ishida pul yutqazgach, u juda tushkunlikka tushdi va me'yoridan ko'p icha boshladi. U kun bo'yi oshxonadagi Vindzor kursisida yonboshlab, gazeta o'qir, ichar va vaqti-vaqti bilan Mozesni pivoga botirilgan non qotganlari bilan boqardi. Uning odamlari dangasa va insofsiz edi, dalalarni begona o't bosgan, binolarning tomini yopish kerak edi, to'siqlar qarovsiz qolgan, hayvonlar esa to'yib ovqat yemasdi.

paras.en: June came and the hay was almost ready for cutting. On Midsummer’s Eve, which was a Saturday, Mr. Jones went into Willingdon and got so drunk at the Red Lion that he did not come back till midday on Sunday. The men had milked the cows in the early morning and then had gone out rabbiting, without bothering to feed the animals. When Mr. Jones got back he immediately went to sleep on the drawing-room sofa with the 'News of the World' over his face, so that when evening came, the animals were still unfed. At last they could stand it no longer. One of the cows broke in the door of the store-shed with her horn and all the animals began to help themselves from the bins. It was just then that Mr. Jones woke up.
paras.uz: Iyun keldi va pichan o'rishga deyarli tayyor bo'ldi. Shanba kuniga to'g'ri kelgan Yoz o'rtasi arafasida janob Jons Uillingdonga borib, «Qizil Sher»da shunchalik mast bo'ldiki, yakshanba tushgacha qaytmadi. Odamlar erta tongda sigirlarni sog'ib, keyin hayvonlarni boqishni ham o'ylamay, quyon oviga ketishdi. Janob Jons qaytib kelgach, darhol mehmonxonadagi divanda yuziga «News of the World» gazetasini yopib uxlab qoldi, shuning uchun kech tushganda ham hayvonlar hali och edi. Nihoyat ular boshqa chiday olmadi. Sigirlardan biri shoxi bilan omborxona eshigini sindirdi va barcha hayvonlar qutilardan o'zlari ovqat ola boshlashdi. Aynan shu payt janob Jons uyg'onib qoldi.

paras.en: The next moment he and his four men were in the store-shed with whips in their hands, lashing out in all directions. This was more than the hungry animals could bear. With one accord, though nothing of the kind had been planned beforehand, they flung themselves upon their tormentors. Jones and his men suddenly found themselves being butted and kicked from all sides. The situation was quite out of their control. They had never seen animals behave like this before, and this sudden uprising of creatures whom they were used to thrashing and maltreating just as they chose, frightened them almost out of their wits. After only a moment or two they gave up trying to defend themselves and took to their heels. A minute later all five of them were in full flight down the cart-track that led to the main road, with the animals pursuing them in triumph.
paras.uz: Keyingi lahzada u va uning to'rtta odami qo'llarida qamchi bilan omborxonada paydo bo'lib, har tomonga savalay boshlashdi. Bu och hayvonlar chiday oladigan narsadan ortiq edi. Oldindan hech narsa rejalashtirilmagan bo'lsa ham, ular bir ovozdan o'z qiynoqchilariga tashlanishdi. Jons va uning odamlari birdan har tomondan suzilayotgan va tepilayotganlarini ko'rishdi. Vaziyat butunlay ular nazoratidan chiqdi. Ular ilgari hech qachon hayvonlarning bunday qilganini ko'rmagan edilar, va o'zlari xohlaganicha urib, qiynashga odatlangan jonivorlarning bu to'satdan isyoni ularni es-hushidan ayirgudek qo'rqitib yubordi. Bir-ikki lahzadan keyin ular himoyalanishga urinishni tashlab, qochib qolishdi. Bir daqiqadan so'ng beshovi ham katta yo'lga olib boradigan arava yo'li bo'ylab jon holatda qochib borar, hayvonlar esa g'alaba bilan ularni quvib borardi.

paras.en: Mrs. Jones looked out of the bedroom window, saw what was happening, hurriedly flung a few possessions into a carpet bag, and slipped out of the farm by another way. Moses sprang off his perch and flapped after her, croaking loudly. Meanwhile the animals had chased Jones and his men out on to the road and slammed the five-barred gate behind them. And so, almost before they knew what was happening, the Rebellion had been successfully carried through: Jones was expelled, and the Manor Farm was theirs.
paras.uz: Jons xonim yotoqxona derazasidan qarab, nima bo'layotganini ko'rdi, shosha-pisha bir nechta buyumni gilam xaltaga tashladi va fermadan boshqa yo'l bilan sirg'alib chiqib ketdi. Mozes qo'nimidan sakrab tushib, baland qag'illagancha qanot qoqib uning ortidan uchdi. Bu orada hayvonlar Jons va uning odamlarini yo'lga quvib chiqarib, ularning orqasidan besh to'sinli darvozani qarsillatib yopishdi. Shunday qilib, nima bo'layotganini deyarli anglab ulgurmasdan, Qo'zg'olon muvaffaqiyatli amalga oshdi: Jons haydaldi va «Manor» fermasi ularniki bo'ldi.

paras.en: For the first few minutes the animals could hardly believe in their good fortune. Their first act was to gallop in a body right round the boundaries of the farm, as though to make quite sure that no human being was hiding anywhere upon it; then they raced back to the farm buildings to wipe out the last traces of Jones’s hated reign. The harness-room at the end of the stables was broken open; the bits, the nose-rings, the dog-chains, the cruel knives with which Mr. Jones had been used to castrate the pigs and lambs, were all flung down the well. The reins, the halters, the blinkers, the degrading nosebags, were thrown on to the rubbish fire which was burning in the yard. So were the whips. All the animals capered with joy when they saw the whips going up in flames. Snowball also threw on to the fire the ribbons with which the horses’ manes and tails had usually been decorated on market days.
paras.uz: Dastlabki bir necha daqiqa davomida hayvonlar o'z omadlariga deyarli ishona olmadilar. Ularning birinchi ishi — go'yo fermaning biror joyida biror inson yashirinib qolmaganiga to'liq ishonch hosil qilmoqchidek, to'da bo'lib fermaning chegaralari bo'ylab aylanib chopish bo'ldi; keyin ular Jonsning nafratli hukmronligining so'nggi izlarini yo'q qilish uchun ferma binolariga yugurib qaytishdi. Otxonalarning oxiridagi egar-jabduq xonasi buzib ochildi; suvliqlar, burun halqalari, it zanjirlari, janob Jons cho'chqa va qo'zilarni bichishda ishlatadigan shafqatsiz pichoqlar — hammasi quduqqa uloqtirildi. Jilovlar, nuqtalar, ko'z to'siqlari, xo'rlovchi yem xaltalari hovlida yonayotgan axlat gulxaniga tashlandi. Qamchilar ham. Qamchilarning alangada yonib ketayotganini ko'rib, barcha hayvonlar quvonchdan sakrab o'ynashdi. Snoubol bozor kunlari otlarning yoli va dumini bezash uchun ishlatiladigan lentalarni ham olovga tashladi.

paras.en: ‘Ribbons,’ he said, ‘should be considered as clothes, which are the mark of a human being. All animals should go naked.’
paras.uz: «Lentalarni, — dedi u, — kiyim deb hisoblash kerak, kiyim esa inson belgisi. Barcha hayvonlar yalang'och yurishi kerak.»

paras.en: When Boxer heard this he fetched the small straw hat which he wore in summer to keep the flies out of his ears, and flung it on to the fire with the rest.
paras.uz: Bokser buni eshitib, yozda qulog'iga pashsha kirmasligi uchun kiyadigan kichkina somon shlyapasini olib keldi va uni boshqa narsalar bilan birga olovga tashladi.

paras.en: In a very little while the animals had destroyed everything that reminded them of Mr. Jones. Napoleon then led them back to the store-shed and served out a double ration of corn to everybody, with two biscuits for each dog. Then they sang 'Beasts of England' from end to end seven times running, and after that they settled down for the night and slept as they had never slept before.
paras.uz: Juda qisqa vaqt ichida hayvonlar ularga janob Jonsni eslatadigan hamma narsani yo'q qilishdi. Keyin Napoleon ularni omborxonaga qaytarib olib bordi va hammaga ikki hissa don, har bir itga esa ikkitadan pechenye tarqatdi. So'ngra ular «Angliya hayvonlari»ni boshidan oxirigacha ketma-ket yetti marta kuylashdi, keyin tunashga joylashib, hech qachon uxlamagandek uxlashdi.

paras.en: But they woke at dawn as usual, and suddenly remembering the glorious thing that had happened, they all raced out into the pasture together. A little way down the pasture there was a knoll that commanded a view of most of the farm. The animals rushed to the top of it and gazed round them in the clear morning light. Yes, it was theirs – everything that they could see was theirs! In the ecstasy of that thought they gambolled round and round, they hurled themselves into the air in great leaps of excitement. They rolled in the dew, they cropped mouthfuls of the sweet summer grass, they kicked up clods of the black earth and snuffed its rich scent. Then they made a tour of inspection of the whole farm and surveyed with speechless admiration the ploughland, the hayfield, the orchard, the pool, the spinney. It was as though they had never seen these things before, and even now they could hardly believe that it was all their own.
paras.uz: Lekin ular odatdagidek tong saharda uyg'onishdi va birdan sodir bo'lgan ajoyib voqeani eslab, hammasi birgalikda yaylovga yugurib chiqishdi. Yaylovdan sal pastda fermaning katta qismi ko'rinib turadigan tepalik bor edi. Hayvonlar uning cho'qqisiga otilib chiqib, tiniq tong nurida atrofga tikilishdi. Ha, bu ularniki edi — ko'rib turgan hamma narsa ularniki edi! Bu fikrdan vajdga tushib, ular aylana-aylana o'ynashdi, hayajondan katta-katta sakrab havoga otilishdi. Shudringda ag'nashdi, shirin yozgi o'tdan og'iz to'la yulib yeyishdi, qora tuproq kesaklarini tepib, uning to'yimli hidini hidlashdi. Keyin butun fermani aylanib ko'zdan kechirishdi va haydalgan yerga, pichanzorga, bog'ga, hovuzga, butazorga so'zsiz hayrat bilan qarashdi. Go'yo ular bu narsalarni ilgari hech qachon ko'rmagandek edi, hatto hozir ham hammasi o'zlariniki ekaniga deyarli ishona olishmasdi.

paras.en: Then they filed back to the farm buildings and halted in silence outside the door of the farmhouse. That was theirs too, but they were frightened to go inside. After a moment, however, Snowball and Napoleon butted the door open with their shoulders and the animals entered in single file, walking with the utmost care for fear of disturbing anything. They tiptoed from room to room, afraid to speak above a whisper and gazing with a kind of awe at the unbelievable luxury, at the beds with their feather mattresses, the looking-glasses, the horsehair sofa, the Brussels carpet, the lithograph of Queen Victoria over the drawing-room mantelpiece. They were just coming down the stairs when Mollie was discovered to be missing. Going back, the others found that she had remained behind in the best bedroom.
paras.uz: Keyin ular bir qatorda ferma binolariga qaytib, ferma uyining eshigi oldida jimgina to'xtashdi. U ham ularniki edi, lekin ichkariga kirishga qo'rqishardi. Biroq bir lahzadan keyin Snoubol va Napoleon yelkalari bilan eshikni itarib ochishdi va hayvonlar biror narsani buzib qo'yishdan qo'rqib, nihoyatda ehtiyotkorlik bilan bir qatorda ichkariga kirishdi. Ular oyoq uchida xonama-xona yurishar, shivirlashdan balandroq gapirishga qo'rqishar va aql bovar qilmas hashamatga — par to'shakli karavotlarga, ko'zgularga, ot yolidan to'qilgan divanga, Bryussel gilamiga, mehmonxona kamini ustidagi Qirolicha Viktoriyaning litografiyasiga qandaydir hurmat aralash qo'rquv bilan tikilishardi. Ular endigina zinadan tushib kelayotganlarida Molli yo'qligi ma'lum bo'lib qoldi. Ortga qaytgan boshqalar uning eng yaxshi yotoqxonada qolib ketganini ko'rishdi.

paras.en: She had taken a piece of blue ribbon from Mrs. Jones’s dressing-table, and was holding it against her shoulder and admiring herself in the glass in a very foolish manner. The others reproached her sharply, and they went outside. Some hams hanging in the kitchen were taken out for burial, and the barrel of beer in the scullery was stove in with a kick from Boxer’s hoof, – otherwise nothing in the house was touched. A unanimous resolution was passed on the spot that the farmhouse should be preserved as a museum. All were agreed that no animal must ever live there.
paras.uz: U Jons xonimning pardoz stolidan bir parcha ko'k lenta olib, uni yelkasiga tutgancha ko'zguda o'zini juda ahmoqona tomosha qilib turardi. Boshqalar uni qattiq koyishdi va tashqariga chiqishdi. Oshxonada osilib turgan bir nechta dudlangan son ko'mish uchun olib chiqildi, yordamchi xonadagi pivo bochkasi esa Bokserning tuyog'i bilan tepib teshildi, — bundan boshqa uydagi hech narsaga tegilmadi. Joyning o'zidayoq ferma uyini muzey sifatida saqlash haqida bir ovozdan qaror qabul qilindi. Hech bir hayvon u yerda hech qachon yashamasligi kerakligiga hamma rozi bo'ldi.

paras.en: The animals had their breakfast, and then Snowball and Napoleon called them together again.
paras.uz: Hayvonlar nonushta qilishdi, keyin Snoubol va Napoleon ularni yana yig'ishdi.

paras.en: ‘Comrades,’ said Snowball, ‘it is half-past six and we have a long day before us. Today we begin the hay harvest. But there is another matter that must be attended to first.’
paras.uz: «O'rtoqlar, — dedi Snoubol, — soat olti yarim, oldimizda uzun kun turibdi. Bugun pichan o'rimini boshlaymiz. Lekin avval hal qilinishi kerak bo'lgan yana bir masala bor.»

paras.en: The pigs now revealed that during the past three months they had taught themselves to read and write from an old spelling book which had belonged to Mr. Jones’s children and which had been thrown on the rubbish heap. Napoleon sent for pots of black and white paint and led the way down to the five-barred gate that gave on to the main road. Then Snowball (for it was Snowball who was best at writing) took a brush between the two knuckles of his trotter, painted out MANOR FARM from the top bar of the gate and in its place painted ANIMAL FARM. This was to be the name of the farm from now onwards. After this they went back to the farm buildings, where Snowball and Napoleon sent for a ladder which they caused to be set against the end wall of the big barn.
paras.uz: Endi cho'chqalar o'tgan uch oy davomida janob Jonsning bolalariga tegishli bo'lgan va axlatxonaga tashlab yuborilgan eski alifbe kitobidan o'zlari o'qish va yozishni o'rganganliklarini ma'lum qilishdi. Napoleon qora va oq bo'yoq solingan idishlarni keltirishni buyurdi va katta yo'lga chiqadigan besh to'sinli darvozaga boshlab bordi. Keyin Snoubol (chunki eng yaxshi yozadigan Snoubol edi) cho'tkani tuyog'ining ikki bo'g'imi orasiga olib, darvozaning ustki to'sinidagi MANOR FERMASI yozuvini bo'yab tashladi va uning o'rniga HAYVONLAR FERMASI deb yozdi. Bundan buyon fermaning nomi shu bo'lishi kerak edi. Shundan keyin ular ferma binolariga qaytishdi, u yerda Snoubol va Napoleon narvon keltirishni buyurib, uni katta molxonaning yon devoriga qo'ydirishdi.

paras.en: They explained that by their studies of the past three months the pigs had succeeded in reducing the principles of Animalism to Seven Commandments. These Seven Commandments would now be inscribed on the wall; they would form an unalterable law by which all the animals on Animal Farm must live for ever after. With some difficulty (for it is not easy for a pig to balance himself on a ladder) Snowball climbed up and set to work, with Squealer a few rungs below him holding the paint-pot. The Commandments were written on the tarred wall in great white letters that could be read thirty yards away. They ran thus:
paras.uz: Ular tushuntirishlaricha, o'tgan uch oydagi izlanishlari natijasida cho'chqalar Hayvonizm tamoyillarini Yetti Amrga jamlashga muvaffaq bo'lishgan ekan. Bu Yetti Amr endi devorga yozib qo'yiladi; ular Hayvonlar fermasidagi barcha hayvonlar bundan buyon abadiy amal qilishi kerak bo'lgan o'zgarmas qonunni tashkil etadi. Biroz qiynalib (chunki cho'chqa uchun narvonda muvozanatni saqlash oson emas) Snoubol tepaga chiqib ishga kirishdi, Skviler esa undan bir necha pog'ona pastda bo'yoq idishini ushlab turdi. Amrlar qatron surtilgan devorga o'ttiz yard naridan o'qish mumkin bo'lgan katta oq harflar bilan yozildi. Ular shunday edi:

paras.en: THE SEVEN COMMANDMENTS
paras.uz: YETTI AMR

paras.en: 1. Whatever goes upon two legs is an enemy.
paras.uz: 1. Ikki oyoqda yuradigan har qanday narsa — dushman.

paras.en: 2. Whatever goes upon four legs, or has wings, is a friend.
paras.uz: 2. To'rt oyoqda yuradigan yoki qanoti bor har qanday narsa — do'st.

paras.en: 3. No animal shall wear clothes.
paras.uz: 3. Hech bir hayvon kiyim kiymaydi.

paras.en: 4. No animal shall sleep in a bed.
paras.uz: 4. Hech bir hayvon karavotda uxlamaydi.

paras.en: 5. No animal shall drink alcohol.
paras.uz: 5. Hech bir hayvon spirtli ichimlik ichmaydi.

paras.en: 6. No animal shall kill any other animal.
paras.uz: 6. Hech bir hayvon boshqa hayvonni o'ldirmaydi.

paras.en: 7. All animals are equal.
paras.uz: 7. Barcha hayvonlar teng.

paras.en: It was very neatly written, and except that ‘friend’ was written ‘freind’ and one of the ‘S’s’ was the wrong way round, the spelling was correct all the way through. Snowball read it aloud for the benefit of the others. All the animals nodded in complete agreement, and the cleverer ones at once began to learn the Commandments by heart.
paras.uz: Juda chiroyli yozilgan edi va «friend» (do'st) so'zi «freind» deb yozilgani hamda «S» harflaridan biri teskari turgani hisobga olinmasa, imlo boshidan oxirigacha to'g'ri edi. Snoubol boshqalar uchun uni ovoz chiqarib o'qib berdi. Barcha hayvonlar to'liq rozilik bilan bosh irg'ashdi, aqlliroqlari esa darhol Amrlarni yod ola boshlashdi.

paras.en: ‘Now, comrades,’ cried Snowball, throwing down the paint-brush, ‘to the hayfield! Let us make it a point of honour to get in the harvest more quickly than Jones and his men could do.’
paras.uz: «Endi, o'rtoqlar, — deb qichqirdi Snoubol bo'yoq cho'tkasini tashlab, — pichanzorga! Hosilni Jons va uning odamlari qila olganidan tezroq yig'ib olishni sharaf ishi qilaylik.»

paras.en: But at this moment the three cows, who had seemed uneasy for some time past, set up a loud lowing. They had not been milked for twenty-four hours, and their udders were almost bursting. After a little thought, the pigs sent for buckets and milked the cows fairly successfully, their trotters being well adapted to this task. Soon there were five buckets of frothing creamy milk at which many of the animals looked with considerable interest.
paras.uz: Lekin shu payt anchadan beri bezovta ko'rinayotgan uchta sigir baland ovozda mo'ray boshladi. Ular yigirma to'rt soatdan beri sog'ilmagan edi va yelinlari yorilib ketay deb turardi. Biroz o'ylab, cho'chqalar chelaklar keltirishni buyurishdi va sigirlarni ancha muvaffaqiyatli sog'ishdi — ularning tuyoqlari bu ishga juda moslashgan ekan. Tez orada ko'pirib turgan quyuq sut to'la beshta chelak paydo bo'ldi va ko'p hayvonlar ularga katta qiziqish bilan qarashdi.

paras.en: ‘What is going to happen to all that milk?’ said someone.
paras.uz: «Shuncha sut nima bo'ladi?» — dedi kimdir.

paras.en: ‘Jones used sometimes to mix some of it in our mash,’ said one of the hens.
paras.uz: «Jons ba'zan uning bir qismini yemimizga aralashtirardi», — dedi tovuqlardan biri.

paras.en: ‘Never mind the milk, comrades!’ cried Napoleon, placing himself in front of the buckets. ‘That will be attended to. The harvest is more important. Comrade Snowball will lead the way. I shall follow in a few minutes. Forward, comrades! The hay is waiting.’
paras.uz: «Sutni qo'yinglar, o'rtoqlar! — deb qichqirdi Napoleon chelaklarning oldiga turib olib. — Unga qaraladi. Hosil muhimroq. O'rtoq Snoubol boshlab boradi. Men bir necha daqiqadan keyin ortidan boraman. Oldinga, o'rtoqlar! Pichan kutyapti.»

paras.en: So the animals trooped down to the hayfield to begin the harvest, and when they came back in the evening it was noticed that the milk had disappeared.
paras.uz: Shunday qilib, hayvonlar hosilni boshlash uchun to'da bo'lib pichanzorga tushishdi, kechqurun qaytib kelishganda esa sut g'oyib bo'lgani ma'lum bo'ldi.
