…Moses, the tame raven. Moses, who was Mr. Jones’s especial pet, was a spy and a tale-bearer, but he was also a clever talker. He claimed to know of the existenc…
…e pigs had succeeded in reducing the principles of Animalism to Seven Commandments. These Seven Commandments would now be inscribed on the wall; they would form…
…arm buildings to wipe out the last traces of Jones’s hated reign. The harness-room at the end of the stables was broken open; the bits, the nose-rings, the dog-…
…Red Lion that he did not come back till midday on Sunday. The men had milked the cows in the early morning and then had gone out rabbiting, without bothering to…

quiz.q: What did the pigs call their system of thought?
What happened to the milk at the end of the chapter?

chapters.recap_uz: Mayor o'ladi; cho'chqalar uning g'oyalarini «Hayvonizm»ga aylantiradi. Bir kuni och qolgan hayvonlar Jonsni haydab chiqaradi. Ferma «Hayvonlar fermasi» deb nomlanadi, devorga Yetti Amr yoziladi — lekin oqshomga borib sut g'oyib bo'ladi.

chapters.title: Four legs good, two legs bad
chapters.title_uz: To'rt oyoq — yaxshi, ikki oyoq — yomon

paras.en: How they toiled and sweated to get the hay in! But their efforts were rewarded, for the harvest was an even bigger success than they had hoped.
paras.uz: Pichanni yig'ib olish uchun ular qanchalik mehnat qilib, ter to'kishdi! Lekin harakatlari mukofotlandi, chunki hosil ular umid qilganidan ham zo'r chiqdi.

paras.en: Sometimes the work was hard; the implements had been designed for human beings and not for animals, and it was a great drawback that no animal was able to use any tool that involved standing on his hind legs. But the pigs were so clever that they could think of a way round every difficulty. As for the horses, they knew every inch of the field, and in fact understood the business of mowing and raking far better than Jones and his men had ever done. The pigs did not actually work, but directed and supervised the others. With their superior knowledge it was natural that they should assume the leadership.
paras.uz: Ba'zan ish og'ir bo'lardi; asbob-uskunalar hayvonlar uchun emas, insonlar uchun yasalgan edi va hech bir hayvon orqa oyoqlarida turishni talab qiladigan asbobni ishlata olmasligi katta noqulaylik edi. Lekin cho'chqalar shunchalik aqlli ediki, har qanday qiyinchilikni aylanib o'tish yo'lini topa olishardi. Otlarga kelsak, ular dalaning har bir qarichini bilishardi va aslida o'rish va pichan yig'ish ishini Jons va uning odamlaridan ancha yaxshiroq tushunishardi. Cho'chqalar aslida ishlamasdi, balki boshqalarga yo'l-yo'riq ko'rsatib, nazorat qilishardi. Bilimlari ustun bo'lgani uchun rahbarlikni o'z zimmalariga olishlari tabiiy edi.

paras.en: Boxer and Clover would harness themselves to the cutter or the horse-rake (no bits or reins were needed in these days, of course) and tramp steadily round and round the field with a pig walking behind and calling out ‘Gee up, comrade!’ or ‘Whoa back, comrade!’ as the case might be. And every animal down to the humblest worked at turning the hay and gathering it. Even the ducks and hens toiled to and fro all day in the sun, carrying tiny wisps of hay in their beaks. In the end they finished the harvest in two days’ less time than it had usually taken Jones and his men. Moreover, it was the biggest harvest that the farm had ever seen. There was no wastage whatever; the hens and ducks with their sharp eyes had gathered up the very last stalk. And not an animal on the farm had stolen so much as a mouthful.
paras.uz: Bokser va Klover o'roq mashinasiga yoki ot xaskashiga o'zlarini qo'shishar (bu kunlarda, albatta, suvliq ham, jilov ham kerak emasdi) va orqalaridan yurayotgan cho'chqaning vaziyatga qarab «Chuh, o'rtoq!» yoki «Tirr, o'rtoq!» degan hayqiriqlari ostida dala atrofida tinimsiz aylanib yurishardi. Eng kamtarinigacha har bir hayvon pichanni ag'darish va yig'ishda ishladi. Hatto o'rdaklar va tovuqlar ham kun bo'yi quyosh ostida tumshuqlarida mitti pichan tolalarini tashib, u yoqdan-bu yoqqa yugurishdi. Oxir-oqibat ular hosilni odatda Jons va uning odamlariga ketadigan vaqtdan ikki kun tezroq tugatishdi. Bundan tashqari, bu fermaning hozirgacha ko'rgan eng katta hosili edi. Hech qanday isrof bo'lmadi; o'tkir ko'zli tovuqlar va o'rdaklar eng oxirgi poyagacha terib olishdi. Fermadagi biror hayvon bir og'iz ham o'g'irlamadi.

paras.en: All through that summer the work of the farm went like clockwork. The animals were happy as they had never conceived it possible to be. Every mouthful of food was an acute positive pleasure, now that it was truly their own food, produced by themselves and for themselves, not doled out to them by a grudging master. With the worthless parasitical human beings gone, there was more for everyone to eat. There was more leisure too, inexperienced though the animals were. They met with many difficulties – for instance, later in the year, when they harvested the corn, they had to tread it out in the ancient style and blow away the chaff with their breath, since the farm possessed no threshing machine – but the pigs with their cleverness and Boxer with his tremendous muscles always pulled them through. Boxer was the admiration of everybody.
paras.uz: O'sha yoz bo'yi ferma ishlari soatdek aniq yurdi. Hayvonlar ilgari mumkin deb tasavvur ham qilmagan darajada baxtli edi. Har bir luqma ovqat endi o'tkir, haqiqiy lazzat edi, chunki u chindan ham o'z ovqatlari — xasis xo'jayin ulashib bergan emas, balki o'zlari, o'zlari uchun yetishtirgan ovqat edi. Befoyda, tekinxo'r insonlar ketgach, hammaga yeyish uchun ko'proq narsa qoldi. Hayvonlar tajribasiz bo'lsa ham, dam olish vaqti ham ko'paydi. Ular ko'p qiyinchiliklarga duch kelishdi — masalan, yilning oxirroq qismida don o'rganlarida, fermada xirmon mashinasi yo'qligi sababli uni qadimiy usulda oyoq bilan yanchishga va somonini nafas bilan puflab uchirishga majbur bo'lishdi — lekin cho'chqalar aqli bilan, Bokser esa ulkan mushaklari bilan ularni doim qiyinchilikdan olib chiqishardi. Bokserga hamma qoyil qolardi.

paras.en: He had been a hard worker even in Jones’s time, but now he seemed more like three horses than one; there were days when the entire work of the farm seemed to rest on his mighty shoulders. From morning to night he was pushing and pulling, always at the spot where the work was hardest. He had made an arrangement with one of the cockerels to call him in the mornings half an hour earlier than anyone else, and would put in some volunteer labour at whatever seemed to be most needed, before the regular day’s work began. His answer to every problem, every setback, was ‘I will work harder!’ – which he had adopted as his personal motto.
paras.uz: U Jons davrida ham mehnatkash edi, lekin endi bitta ot emas, uchta otga o'xshab qolgandi; ba'zi kunlari fermaning butun ishi uning qudratli yelkalariga tayanganday tuyulardi. Ertalabdan kechgacha u itarar va tortar, doim ish eng og'ir bo'lgan joyda bo'lardi. U xo'rozlardan biri bilan kelishib olgan edi — u ertalab uni hammadan yarim soat oldin uyg'otardi, va Bokser odatdagi ish kuni boshlanishidan oldin eng zarur ko'ringan joyda ixtiyoriy mehnat qilardi. Har bir muammo, har bir muvaffaqiyatsizlikka uning javobi «Men yanada ko'proq ishlayman!» edi — u buni o'zining shaxsiy shiori qilib olgan edi.

paras.en: But everyone worked according to his capacity. The hens and ducks, for instance, saved five bushels of corn at the harvest by gathering up the stray grains. Nobody stole, nobody grumbled over his rations, the quarrelling and biting and jealousy which had been normal features of life in the old days had almost disappeared. Nobody shirked – or almost nobody. Mollie, it was true, was not good at getting up in the mornings, and had a way of leaving work early on the ground that there was a stone in her hoof. And the behaviour of the cat was somewhat peculiar. It was soon noticed that when there was work to be done the cat could never be found. She would vanish for hours on end, and then reappear at meal-times, or in the evening after work was over, as though nothing had happened.
paras.uz: Lekin har kim o'z qobiliyatiga yarasha ishlardi. Masalan, tovuqlar va o'rdaklar hosil paytida sochilib qolgan donlarni terib, besh bushel donni tejab qolishdi. Hech kim o'g'irlamas, hech kim o'z ulushidan nolimas, eski kunlarda hayotning odatiy qismi bo'lgan janjal, tishlash va hasad deyarli yo'qolgan edi. Hech kim ishdan qochmasdi — yoki deyarli hech kim. To'g'ri, Molli ertalab turishga no'noq edi va tuyog'imga tosh kirdi, degan bahona bilan ishdan erta ketish odati bor edi. Mushukning xatti-harakati ham biroz g'alati edi. Tez orada payqaldiki, qilinadigan ish bo'lganda mushukni hech qachon topib bo'lmasdi. U soatlab g'oyib bo'lib, keyin ovqat paytida yoki kechqurun ish tugagandan keyin hech narsa bo'lmagandek yana paydo bo'lardi.

paras.en: But she always made such excellent excuses, and purred so affectionately, that it was impossible not to believe in her good intentions. Old Benjamin, the donkey, seemed quite unchanged since the Rebellion. He did his work in the same slow obstinate way as he had done it in Jones’s time, never shirking and never volunteering for extra work either. About the Rebellion and its results he would express no opinion. When asked whether he was not happier now that Jones was gone, he would say only ‘Donkeys live a long time. None of you has ever seen a dead donkey,’ and the others had to be content with this cryptic answer.
paras.uz: Lekin u doim shunchalik zo'r bahonalar topar va shunchalik mehr bilan xurillardiki, uning yaxshi niyatlariga ishonmaslik mumkin emasdi. Keksa eshak Benjamin Qo'zg'olondan keyin ham hech o'zgarmaganday edi. U ishini Jons davridagidek sekin va qaysarlik bilan qilardi — hech qachon ishdan qochmas, qo'shimcha ishga ham hech qachon o'zi ko'ngilli bo'lmasdi. Qo'zg'olon va uning natijalari haqida hech qanday fikr bildirmasdi. Jons ketganidan keyin endi baxtliroq emasmisan, deb so'rashsa, faqat: «Eshaklar uzoq yashaydi. Hech biringiz o'lik eshakni ko'rmagansiz», derdi, va boshqalar bu sirli javob bilan qanoatlanishga majbur bo'lishardi.

paras.en: On Sundays there was no work. Breakfast was an hour later than usual, and after breakfast there was a ceremony which was observed every week without fail. First came the hoisting of the flag. Snowball had found in the harness-room an old green tablecloth of Mrs. Jones’s and had painted on it a hoof and a horn in white. This was run up the flagstaff in the farmhouse garden every Sunday morning. The flag was green, Snowball explained, to represent the green fields of England, while the hoof and horn signified the future Republic of the Animals which would arise when the human race had been finally overthrown. After the hoisting of the flag all the animals trooped into the big barn for a general assembly which was known as the Meeting. Here the work of the coming week was planned out and resolutions were put forward and debated.
paras.uz: Yakshanba kunlari ish bo'lmasdi. Nonushta odatdagidan bir soat kechroq bo'lar, nonushtadan keyin esa har hafta kanda qilinmaydigan marosim o'tkazilardi. Avval bayroq ko'tarilardi. Snoubol egar-jabduq xonasidan Jons xonimning eski yashil dasturxonini topib, unga oq bo'yoq bilan tuyoq va shox chizgan edi. Har yakshanba ertalab u ferma uyi bog'idagi bayroq ustuniga ko'tarilardi. Snoubol tushuntirishicha, bayroq Angliyaning yashil dalalarini anglatish uchun yashil, tuyoq va shox esa inson zoti butunlay ag'darilgandan keyin vujudga keladigan kelajakdagi Hayvonlar Respublikasini bildirardi. Bayroq ko'tarilgandan keyin barcha hayvonlar Yig'ilish deb ataladigan umumiy majlis uchun katta molxonaga to'da bo'lib kirishardi. Bu yerda kelgusi haftaning ishi rejalashtirilar, takliflar kiritilib, muhokama qilinardi.

paras.en: It was always the pigs who put forward the resolutions. The other animals understood how to vote, but could never think of any resolutions of their own. Snowball and Napoleon were by far the most active in the debates. But it was noticed that these two were never in agreement: whatever suggestion either of them made, the other could be counted on to oppose it. Even when it was resolved – a thing no one could object to in itself – to set aside the small paddock behind the orchard as a home of rest for animals who were past work, there was a stormy debate over the correct retiring age for each class of animal. The Meeting always ended with the singing of 'Beasts of England', and the afternoon was given up to recreation.
paras.uz: Takliflarni har doim cho'chqalar kiritardi. Boshqa hayvonlar qanday ovoz berishni tushunishardi, lekin o'zlaricha hech qanday taklif o'ylab topa olishmasdi. Munozaralarda eng faollar Snoubol va Napoleon edi. Lekin bu ikkovi hech qachon kelishmasligi payqaldi: biri qanday taklif qilmasin, ikkinchisi albatta unga qarshi chiqardi. Hatto o'z-o'zidan hech kim e'tiroz bildira olmaydigan qaror — bog' ortidagi kichik o'tloqni ishlashdan qolgan hayvonlar uchun dam olish maskani sifatida ajratish to'g'risida qaror qabul qilinganda ham, har bir hayvon toifasi uchun to'g'ri nafaqa yoshi haqida qizg'in bahs bo'ldi. Yig'ilish har doim «Angliya hayvonlari»ni kuylash bilan tugar, tushdan keyin esa dam olishga bag'ishlanardi.

paras.en: The pigs had set aside the harness-room as a headquarters for themselves. Here, in the evenings, they studied blacksmithing, carpentering, and other necessary arts from books which they had brought out of the farmhouse. Snowball also busied himself with organising the other animals into what he called Animal Committees. He was indefatigable at this. He formed the Egg Production Committee for the hens, the Clean Tails League for the cows, the Wild Comrades’ Re-education Committee (the object of this was to tame the rats and rabbits), the Whiter Wool Movement for the sheep, and various others, besides instituting classes in reading and writing. On the whole, these projects were a failure. The attempt to tame the wild creatures, for instance, broke down almost immediately. They continued to behave very much as before, and when treated with generosity, simply took advantage of it.
paras.uz: Cho'chqalar egar-jabduq xonasini o'zlari uchun qarorgoh qilib ajratib olgan edi. Bu yerda kechqurunlari ular ferma uyidan olib chiqqan kitoblardan temirchilik, duradgorlik va boshqa zarur hunarlarni o'rganishardi. Snoubol boshqa hayvonlarni o'zi Hayvonlar Qo'mitalari deb atagan tuzilmalarga birlashtirish bilan ham band edi. Bu ishda u charchoq bilmasdi. U tovuqlar uchun Tuxum Ishlab Chiqarish Qo'mitasini, sigirlar uchun Toza Dumlar Ittifoqini, Yovvoyi O'rtoqlarni Qayta Tarbiyalash Qo'mitasini (uning maqsadi kalamushlar va quyonlarni qo'lga o'rgatish edi), qo'ylar uchun Oppoqroq Jun Harakatini va boshqa turli tashkilotlarni tuzdi, buning ustiga o'qish va yozish darslarini ham ochdi. Umuman olganda, bu loyihalar muvaffaqiyatsiz chiqdi. Masalan, yovvoyi jonivorlarni qo'lga o'rgatish urinishi deyarli darhol barbod bo'ldi. Ular avvalgidek o'zini tutishda davom etishdi va ularga saxiylik qilinsa, shunchaki undan foydalanib qolishdi.

paras.en: The cat joined the Re-education Committee and was very active in it for some days. She was seen one day sitting on a roof and talking to some sparrows who were just out of her reach. She was telling them that all animals were now comrades and that any sparrow who chose could come and perch on her paw; but the sparrows kept their distance.
paras.uz: Mushuk Qayta Tarbiyalash Qo'mitasiga qo'shildi va bir necha kun unda juda faol bo'ldi. Bir kuni uni tomda o'tirib, panjasi yetmaydigan joydagi chumchuqlar bilan gaplashayotganini ko'rishdi. U ularga endi barcha hayvonlar o'rtoq ekanini va xohlagan chumchuq kelib uning panjasiga qo'nishi mumkinligini aytayotgan edi; lekin chumchuqlar masofani saqlashdi.

paras.en: The reading and writing classes, however, were a great success. By the autumn almost every animal on the farm was literate in some degree.
paras.uz: Biroq o'qish va yozish darslari katta muvaffaqiyat qozondi. Kuzga kelib fermadagi deyarli har bir hayvon ozmi-ko'pmi savodli bo'lib qoldi.

paras.en: As for the pigs, they could already read and write perfectly. The dogs learned to read fairly well, but were not interested in reading anything except the Seven Commandments. Muriel, the goat, could read somewhat better than the dogs, and sometimes used to read to the others in the evenings from scraps of newspaper which she found on the rubbish heap. Benjamin could read as well as any pig, but never exercised his faculty. So far as he knew, he said, there was nothing worth reading. Clover learnt the whole alphabet, but could not put words together. Boxer could not get beyond the letter D. He would trace out A, B, C, D, in the dust with his great hoof, and then would stand staring at the letters with his ears back, sometimes shaking his forelock, trying with all his might to remember what came next and never succeeding.
paras.uz: Cho'chqalarga kelsak, ular allaqachon mukammal o'qib-yoza olishardi. Itlar ancha yaxshi o'qishni o'rganishdi, lekin Yetti Amrdan boshqa hech narsani o'qishga qiziqishmasdi. Echki Muriel itlardan biroz yaxshiroq o'qiy olardi va ba'zan kechqurunlari axlatxonadan topgan gazeta parchalaridan boshqalarga o'qib berardi. Benjamin har qanday cho'chqa kabi yaxshi o'qiy olardi, lekin bu qobiliyatini hech qachon ishlatmasdi. Uning aytishicha, bilishicha, o'qishga arziydigan hech narsa yo'q edi. Klover butun alifboni o'rgandi, lekin so'zlarni birlashtira olmasdi. Bokser D harfidan nariga o'ta olmasdi. U ulkan tuyog'i bilan changda A, B, C, D harflarini chizib, keyin quloqlarini orqaga qayirgancha harflarga tikilib turar, ba'zan peshona yolini silkitib, keyin nima kelishini butun kuchi bilan eslashga urinar, lekin hech qachon eslay olmasdi.

paras.en: On several occasions, indeed, he did learn E, F, G, H, but by the time he knew them, it was always discovered that he had forgotten A, B, C, and D. Finally he decided to be content with the first four letters, and used to write them out once or twice every day to refresh his memory. Mollie refused to learn any but the six letters which spelt her own name. She would form these very neatly out of pieces of twig, and would then decorate them with a flower or two and walk round them admiring them.
paras.uz: To'g'ri, bir necha marta u E, F, G, H ni o'rgandi, lekin ularni bilib olganida har doim A, B, C va D ni unutib qo'ygani ma'lum bo'lardi. Nihoyat u dastlabki to'rt harf bilan qanoatlanishga qaror qildi va xotirasini yangilash uchun ularni har kuni bir-ikki marta yozib qo'yardi. Molli o'z ismini tashkil etuvchi oltita harfdan boshqasini o'rganishdan bosh tortdi. U ularni shox parchalaridan juda chiroyli qilib terar, keyin bir-ikkita gul bilan bezab, ularga qoyil qolgancha atrofida aylanib yurardi.

paras.en: None of the other animals on the farm could get further than the letter A. It was also found that the stupider animals, such as the sheep, hens, and ducks, were unable to learn the Seven Commandments by heart. After much thought Snowball declared that the Seven Commandments could in effect be reduced to a single maxim, namely: ‘Four legs good, two legs bad.’ This, he said, contained the essential principle of Animalism. Whoever had thoroughly grasped it would be safe from human influences. The birds at first objected, since it seemed to them that they also had two legs, but Snowball proved to them that this was not so.
paras.uz: Fermadagi boshqa hayvonlarning hech biri A harfidan nariga o'ta olmadi. Bundan tashqari, qo'ylar, tovuqlar va o'rdaklar kabi ahmoqroq hayvonlar Yetti Amrni yod ola olmasligi ma'lum bo'ldi. Uzoq o'ylab, Snoubol Yetti Amrni amalda bitta hikmatga qisqartirish mumkin, deb e'lon qildi, ya'ni: «To'rt oyoq — yaxshi, ikki oyoq — yomon». Uning aytishicha, bunda Hayvonizmning asosiy tamoyili mujassam edi. Uni puxta tushungan har kim insonlar ta'siridan xavfsiz bo'ladi. Qushlar dastlab e'tiroz bildirishdi, chunki ularga o'zlarining ham ikki oyog'i borday tuyuldi, lekin Snoubol ularga bunday emasligini isbotlab berdi.

paras.en: ‘A bird’s wing, comrades,’ he said, ‘is an organ of propulsion and not of manipulation. It should therefore be regarded as a leg. The distinguishing mark of man is the hand, the instrument with which he does all his mischief.’
paras.uz: «Qushning qanoti, o'rtoqlar, — dedi u, — boshqarish emas, harakatlantirish a'zosidir. Shuning uchun uni oyoq deb hisoblash kerak. Insonning ajralib turuvchi belgisi — qo'l, u barcha yovuzliklarini shu asbob bilan qiladi.»

paras.en: The birds did not understand Snowball’s long words, but they accepted his explanation, and all the humbler animals set to work to learn the new maxim by heart. FOUR LEGS GOOD, TWO LEGS BAD, was inscribed on the end wall of the barn, above the Seven Commandments and in bigger letters. When they had once got it by heart, the sheep developed a great liking for this maxim, and often as they lay in the field they would all start bleating ‘Four legs good, two legs bad! Four legs good, two legs bad!’ and keep it up for hours on end, never growing tired of it.
paras.uz: Qushlar Snoubolning uzun-uzun so'zlarini tushunishmadi, lekin uning izohini qabul qilishdi va barcha kamtarinroq hayvonlar yangi hikmatni yod olishga kirishishdi. TO'RT OYOQ — YAXSHI, IKKI OYOQ — YOMON degan yozuv molxonaning yon devoriga, Yetti Amrdan tepaga, kattaroq harflar bilan yozildi. Uni yod olgach, qo'ylarga bu hikmat juda yoqib qoldi va ko'pincha dalada yotganlarida hammalari birdan «To'rt oyoq — yaxshi, ikki oyoq — yomon! To'rt oyoq — yaxshi, ikki oyoq — yomon!» deb ma'rashni boshlab, hech charchamasdan soatlab davom ettirishardi.

paras.en: Napoleon took no interest in Snowball’s committees. He said that the education of the young was more important than anything that could be done for those who were already grown up. It happened that Jessie and Bluebell had both whelped soon after the hay harvest, giving birth between them to nine sturdy puppies. As soon as they were weaned, Napoleon took them away from their mothers, saying that he would make himself responsible for their education. He took them up into a loft which could only be reached by a ladder from the harness-room, and there kept them in such seclusion that the rest of the farm soon forgot their existence.
paras.uz: Napoleon Snoubolning qo'mitalariga hech qiziqmasdi. U yoshlarni tarbiyalash allaqachon voyaga yetganlar uchun qilinadigan har qanday ishdan muhimroq, derdi. Shunday bo'ldiki, Jessi va Blyubell pichan o'rimidan keyin ko'p o'tmay tug'ishdi va ikkovi to'qqizta baquvvat kuchukcha tug'ishdi. Ular sutdan ajratilishi bilanoq Napoleon ularni onalaridan olib qo'ydi va ularning tarbiyasini o'z zimmasiga olishini aytdi. U ularni faqat egar-jabduq xonasidan narvon orqali chiqish mumkin bo'lgan chordoqqa olib chiqdi va u yerda shunchalik yashirin saqladiki, fermaning qolgan qismi tez orada ularning borligini unutib yubordi.

paras.en: The mystery of where the milk went to was soon cleared up. It was mixed every day into the pigs’ mash. The early apples were now ripening, and the grass of the orchard was littered with windfalls. The animals had assumed as a matter of course that these would be shared out equally; one day, however, the order went forth that all the windfalls were to be collected and brought to the harness-room for the use of the pigs. At this some of the other animals murmured, but it was no use. All the pigs were in full agreement on this point, even Snowball and Napoleon. Squealer was sent to make the necessary explanations to the others.
paras.uz: Sut qayerga ketgani haqidagi sir tez orada ochildi. U har kuni cho'chqalarning yemiga aralashtirilardi. Ertapishar olmalar endi pishayotgan edi va bog'dagi o't ustida shamol qoqqan olmalar sochilib yotardi. Hayvonlar, albatta, ular teng taqsimlanadi deb o'ylashgan edi; biroq bir kuni barcha to'kilgan olmalar yig'ilib, cho'chqalar foydalanishi uchun egar-jabduq xonasiga olib kelinsin, degan buyruq chiqdi. Bunga ba'zi boshqa hayvonlar g'o'ldirashdi, lekin foydasi yo'q edi. Bu masalada barcha cho'chqalar, hatto Snoubol va Napoleon ham to'liq hamfikr edi. Boshqalarga zarur tushuntirishlarni berish uchun Skviler yuborildi.

paras.en: ‘Comrades!’ he cried. ‘You do not imagine, I hope, that we pigs are doing this in a spirit of selfishness and privilege? Many of us actually dislike milk and apples. I dislike them myself. Our sole object in taking these things is to preserve our health. Milk and apples (this has been proved by Science, comrades) contain substances absolutely necessary to the well-being of a pig. We pigs are brainworkers. The whole management and organisation of this farm depend on us. Day and night we are watching over your welfare. It is for your sake that we drink that milk and eat those apples. Do you know what would happen if we pigs failed in our duty? Jones would come back! Yes, Jones would come back! Surely, comrades,’ cried Squealer almost pleadingly, skipping from side to side and whisking his tail, ‘surely there is no one among you who wants to see Jones come back?’
paras.uz: «O'rtoqlar! — deb qichqirdi u. — Umid qilamanki, biz cho'chqalar buni xudbinlik va imtiyoz ruhida qilyapmiz deb o'ylamaysizlar? Ko'pchiligimiz aslida sut va olmani yoqtirmaymiz. Men o'zim ham yoqtirmayman. Bularni olishdan yagona maqsadimiz — sog'lig'imizni saqlash. Sut va olmada (buni Ilm isbotlagan, o'rtoqlar) cho'chqaning farovonligi uchun mutlaqo zarur moddalar bor. Biz cho'chqalar — aqliy mehnat ahlimiz. Bu fermaning butun boshqaruvi va tashkiloti bizga bog'liq. Kechayu kunduz biz sizning farovonligingizni kuzatib turamiz. O'sha sutni ichib, o'sha olmalarni yeyishimiz sizlar uchun. Agar biz cho'chqalar burchimizni bajara olmasak, nima bo'lishini bilasizlarmi? Jons qaytib keladi! Ha, Jons qaytib keladi! Axir, o'rtoqlar, — deb qichqirdi Skviler deyarli yalinib, u yoqdan-bu yoqqa sakrab, dumini silkitarkan, — axir orangizda Jonsning qaytib kelishini istaydigan hech kim yo'q-ku?»

paras.en: Now if there was one thing that the animals were completely certain of, it was that they did not want Jones back. When it was put to them in this light, they had no more to say. The importance of keeping the pigs in good health was all too obvious. So it was agreed without further argument that the milk and the windfall apples (and also the main crop of apples when they ripened) should be reserved for the pigs alone.
paras.uz: Agar hayvonlar biror narsaga mutlaqo amin bo'lsa, bu Jonsning qaytishini istamasliklari edi. Masala ularga shu nuqtai nazardan qo'yilganda, boshqa aytadigan gaplari qolmadi. Cho'chqalarning sog'lig'ini saqlash muhimligi juda ham ravshan edi. Shunday qilib, sut va to'kilgan olmalar (shuningdek, asosiy olma hosili ham pishganda) faqat cho'chqalar uchun ajratib qo'yilishi boshqa bahssiz kelishib olindi.

chapters.recap_uz: Birinchi hosil muvaffaqiyatli; Bokserning shiori — «Men yanada ko'proq ishlayman!». Snoubol qo'mitalar tuzadi va Amrlarni bitta shiorga qisqartiradi. Napoleon kuchukchalarni yashirincha o'zi tarbiyalaydi, sut va olmalar esa cho'chqalarga ajratiladi.

chapters.title: The Battle of the Cowshed

paras.en: By the late summer the news of what had happened on Animal Farm had spread across half the county. Every day Snowball and Napoleon sent out flights of pigeons whose instructions were to mingle with the animals on neighbouring farms, tell them the story of the Rebellion, and teach them the tune of Beasts of England.
paras.uz: Yozning oxiriga kelib Hayvonlar fermasida nima bo'lgani haqidagi xabar grafligining yarmiga tarqalib ketdi. Snoubol va Napoleon har kuni kaptarlar galasini jo'natishardi; ularga qo'shni fermalardagi hayvonlar orasiga aralashib, ularga Qo'zg'olon tarixini aytib berish va «Angliya hayvonlari» kuyini o'rgatish topshirilgan edi.

paras.en: Most of this time Mr. Jones had spent sitting in the taproom of the Red Lion at Willingdon, complaining to anyone who would listen of the monstrous injustice he had suffered in being turned out of his property by a pack of good-for-nothing animals. The other farmers sympathised in principle, but they did not at first give him much help. At heart, each of them was secretly wondering whether he could not somehow turn Jones’s misfortune to his own advantage. It was lucky that the owners of the two farms which adjoined Animal Farm were on permanently bad terms. One of them, which was named Foxwood, was a large, neglected, old-fashioned farm, much overgrown by woodland, with all its pastures worn out and its hedges in a disgraceful condition.
paras.uz: Bu vaqtning ko'p qismini janob Jons Uillingdondagi «Qizil Sher»ning mayxonasida o'tirib, tinglashga rozi bo'lgan har kimga bir to'da yaramas hayvonlar tomonidan o'z mulkidan haydab chiqarilib, boshiga tushgan dahshatli adolatsizlikdan shikoyat qilib o'tkazdi. Boshqa fermerlar printsipial jihatdan unga hamdardlik bildirishdi, lekin dastlab unchalik yordam berishmadi. Ichida har biri yashirincha Jonsning baxtsizligini qandaydir yo'l bilan o'z foydasiga aylantira olmasmikan, deb o'ylardi. Hayvonlar fermasiga tutash ikki fermaning egalari doimo bir-biri bilan yomon munosabatda bo'lgani omad edi. Ulardan biri — Foksvud deb atalgan ferma katta, qarovsiz, eski usuldagi xo'jalik bo'lib, uni o'rmon bosib ketgan, barcha yaylovlari tugab bitgan, to'siqlari esa sharmandali ahvolda edi.

paras.en: Its owner, Mr. Pilkington, was an easy-going gentleman farmer who spent most of his time in fishing or hunting according to the season. The other farm, which was called Pinchfield, was smaller and better kept. Its owner was a Mr. Frederick, a tough, shrewd man, perpetually involved in lawsuits and with a name for driving hard bargains. These two disliked each other so much that it was difficult for them to come to any agreement, even in defence of their own interests.
paras.uz: Uning egasi janob Pilkington beg'am janob-fermer bo'lib, vaqtining ko'p qismini mavsumga qarab baliq ovlash yoki ov qilish bilan o'tkazardi. Pinchfild deb atalgan ikkinchi ferma kichikroq va yaxshiroq qaralgan edi. Uning egasi qandaydir janob Frederik edi — qattiqqo'l, ayyor odam, doimo sud ishlariga aralashib yurar va savdolashganda qattiq turishi bilan nom chiqargan edi. Bu ikkovi bir-birini shunchalik yomon ko'rardiki, hatto o'z manfaatlarini himoya qilishda ham biror kelishuvga kelishlari qiyin edi.

paras.en: Nevertheless, they were both thoroughly frightened by the rebellion on Animal Farm, and very anxious to prevent their own animals from learning too much about it. At first they pretended to laugh to scorn the idea of animals managing a farm for themselves. The whole thing would be over in a fortnight, they said. They put it about that the animals on the Manor Farm (they insisted on calling it the Manor Farm; they would not tolerate the name ‘Animal Farm’) were perpetually fighting among themselves and were also rapidly starving to death. When time passed and the animals had evidently not starved to death, Frederick and Pilkington changed their tune and began to talk of the terrible wickedness that now flourished on Animal Farm. It was given out that the animals there practised cannibalism, tortured one another with red-hot horseshoes, and had their females in common. This was what came of rebelling against the laws of Nature, Frederick and Pilkington said.
paras.uz: Shunga qaramay, ularning ikkalasi ham Hayvonlar fermasidagi qo'zg'olondan qattiq qo'rqib ketishgan va o'z hayvonlarining bu haqda ko'p narsa bilib olishiga yo'l qo'ymaslikka juda intilishardi. Dastlab ular hayvonlarning o'zlari fermani boshqarishi degan fikr ustidan kulgandek bo'lishdi. Hammasi ikki hafta ichida tugaydi, deyishdi ular. Ular «Manor» fermasidagi (ular uni «Manor» fermasi deb atashda qat'iy turishardi; «Hayvonlar fermasi» nomiga toqat qilishmasdi) hayvonlar doimo o'zaro urishayotgani va tezda ochlikdan o'lib borayotgani haqida mish-mish tarqatishdi. Vaqt o'tib, hayvonlar ochdan o'lmagani ma'lum bo'lgach, Frederik va Pilkington ohanglarini o'zgartirib, endi Hayvonlar fermasida gullab-yashnayotgan dahshatli yovuzlik haqida gapira boshlashdi. U yerdagi hayvonlar bir-birini yeyishadi, bir-birini cho'g'dek qizdirilgan taqalar bilan qiynashadi va urg'ochilari umumiy, degan gaplar tarqatildi. Tabiat qonunlariga qarshi isyon ko'tarishning oqibati shu, deyishdi Frederik va Pilkington.

paras.en: However, these stories were never fully believed. Rumours of a wonderful farm, where the human beings had been turned out and the animals managed their own affairs, continued to circulate in vague and distorted forms, and throughout that year a wave of rebelliousness ran through the countryside. Bulls which had always been tractable suddenly turned savage, sheep broke down hedges and devoured the clover, cows kicked the pail over, hunters refused their fences and shot their riders on to the other side. Above all, the tune and even the words of Beasts of England were known everywhere. It had spread with astonishing speed. The human beings could not contain their rage when they heard this song, though they pretended to think it merely ridiculous. They could not understand, they said, how even animals could bring themselves to sing such contemptible rubbish.
paras.uz: Biroq bu hikoyalarga hech qachon to'liq ishonishmadi. Insonlar haydab chiqarilgan va hayvonlar o'z ishlarini o'zlari boshqarayotgan ajoyib ferma haqidagi mish-mishlar noaniq va buzilgan shakllarda tarqalishda davom etdi va o'sha yil bo'yi qishloqlar bo'ylab isyonkorlik to'lqini yurib o'tdi. Doim yuvosh bo'lgan buqalar birdan yovvoyilashib ketdi, qo'ylar to'siqlarni buzib, bedani yeb bitirdi, sigirlar chelakni tepib ag'dardi, ov otlari to'siqlardan sakrashdan bosh tortib, chavandozlarini narigi tomonga uloqtirdi. Eng muhimi, «Angliya hayvonlari»ning kuyi va hatto so'zlari hamma joyda ma'lum edi. U hayratlanarli tezlikda tarqalgan edi. Insonlar bu qo'shiqni eshitganda g'azablarini bosa olmasdilar, garchi uni shunchaki kulgili deb hisoblagandek ko'rinsalar ham. Ularning aytishicha, hatto hayvonlar ham qanday qilib bunday jirkanch bema'nilikni kuylashga o'zlarini majbur qila olishini tushuna olmasdilar.

paras.en: Any animal caught singing it was given a flogging on the spot. And yet the song was irrepressible. The blackbirds whistled it in the hedges, the pigeons cooed it in the elms, it got into the din of the smithies and the tune of the church bells. And when the human beings listened to it, they secretly trembled, hearing in it a prophecy of their future doom.
paras.uz: Uni kuylayotganda qo'lga tushgan har qanday hayvon joyida kaltaklanardi. Shunga qaramay qo'shiqni to'xtatib bo'lmasdi. Qoraqushlar uni to'siqlarda hushtak bilan chalardi, kaptarlar qayrag'ochlarda uni g'u-g'ulab kuylardi, u temirchilik ustaxonalarining taqir-tuqurlariga va cherkov qo'ng'iroqlarining kuyiga kirib ketdi. Insonlar uni tinglaganlarida, unda o'zlarining kelajakdagi halokatlari bashoratini eshitib, ichdan titrab ketishardi.

paras.en: Early in October, when the corn was cut and stacked and some of it was already threshed, a flight of pigeons came whirling through the air and alighted in the yard of Animal Farm in the wildest excitement. Jones and all his men, with half a dozen others from Foxwood and Pinchfield, had entered the five-barred gate and were coming up the cart-track that led to the farm. They were all carrying sticks, except Jones, who was marching ahead with a gun in his hands. Obviously they were going to attempt the recapture of the farm.
paras.uz: Oktyabr boshida, don o'rilib, g'aram qilingan va bir qismi allaqachon yanchilgan paytda, bir gala kaptar havoda charx urib uchib kelib, eng kuchli hayajonda Hayvonlar fermasining hovlisiga qo'ndi. Jons va uning barcha odamlari Foksvud va Pinchfilddan kelgan yarim o'nlab boshqalar bilan birga besh to'sinli darvozadan kirib, fermaga olib boradigan arava yo'li bo'ylab kelishayotgan edi. Qo'lida miltiq bilan oldinda borayotgan Jonsdan tashqari hammasi tayoq ko'tarib olgan edi. Ravshanki, ular fermani qayta egallashga urinmoqchi edi.

paras.en: This had long been expected, and all preparations had been made. Snowball, who had studied an old book of Julius Caesar’s campaigns which he had found in the farmhouse, was in charge of the defensive operations. He gave his orders quickly, and in a couple of minutes every animal was at his post.
paras.uz: Bu anchadan beri kutilgan edi va barcha tayyorgarliklar ko'rilgan edi. Ferma uyidan topilgan Yuliy Sezarning yurishlari haqidagi eski kitobni o'rgangan Snoubol mudofaa harakatlariga mas'ul edi. U buyruqlarini tez berdi va bir-ikki daqiqada har bir hayvon o'z joyida edi.

paras.en: As the human beings approached the farm buildings, Snowball launched his first attack. All the pigeons, to the number of thirty-five, flew to and fro over the men’s heads and muted upon them from mid-air; and while the men were dealing with this, the geese, who had been hiding behind the hedge, rushed out and pecked viciously at the calves of their legs. However, this was only a light skirmishing manoeuvre, intended to create a little disorder, and the men easily drove the geese off with their sticks. Snowball now launched his second line of attack. Muriel, Benjamin, and all the sheep, with Snowball at the head of them, rushed forward and prodded and butted the men from every side, while Benjamin turned around and lashed at them with his small hoofs. But once again the men, with their sticks and their hobnailed boots, were too strong for them; and suddenly, at a squeal from Snowball, which was the signal for retreat, all the animals turned and fled through the gateway into the yard.
paras.uz: Insonlar ferma binolariga yaqinlashganda, Snoubol birinchi hujumini boshladi. O'ttiz beshta kaptarning hammasi odamlarning boshi ustida u yoqdan-bu yoqqa uchib, havodan ularning ustiga axlat tashladi; odamlar bu bilan ovora bo'lib turganda, to'siq ortida yashirinib turgan g'ozlar otilib chiqib, ularning boldirlarini ayovsiz cho'qishdi. Biroq bu faqat biroz tartibsizlik yaratish uchun mo'ljallangan yengil to'qnashuv edi va odamlar g'ozlarni tayoqlari bilan osongina haydab yuborishdi. Endi Snoubol ikkinchi hujum safini ishga soldi. Muriel, Benjamin va barcha qo'ylar, boshida Snoubol bilan, oldinga otilib, odamlarni har tomondan turtib, suzishdi, Benjamin esa orqasiga o'girilib, kichkina tuyoqlari bilan ularni tepdi. Lekin yana tayoqlar va mixli etiklar bilan qurollangan odamlar ulardan kuchli chiqdi; va birdan Snoubolning chinqirig'i bilan — bu chekinish ishorasi edi — barcha hayvonlar orqaga o'girilib, darvoza orqali hovliga qochishdi.

paras.en: The men gave a shout of triumph. They saw, as they imagined, their enemies in flight, and they rushed after them in disorder. This was just what Snowball had intended. As soon as they were well inside the yard, the three horses, the three cows, and the rest of the pigs, who had been lying in ambush in the cowshed, suddenly emerged in their rear, cutting them off. Snowball now gave the signal for the charge. He himself dashed straight for Jones. Jones saw him coming, raised his gun and fired. The pellets scored bloody streaks along Snowball’s back, and a sheep dropped dead. Without halting for an instant, Snowball flung his fifteen stone against Jones’s legs. Jones was hurled into a pile of dung and his gun flew out of his hands.
paras.uz: Odamlar g'alaba hayqirig'ini ko'tarishdi. Ular o'ylaganlaridek, dushmanlarini qochayotgan holda ko'rishdi va tartibsiz holda ularning ortidan yugurishdi. Snoubol aynan shuni ko'zlagan edi. Ular hovliga yaxshigina kirib olishlari bilanoq, molxonada pistirmada yotgan uchta ot, uchta sigir va qolgan cho'chqalar birdan ularning orqasida paydo bo'lib, yo'llarini to'sishdi. Endi Snoubol hujum ishorasini berdi. Uning o'zi to'g'ri Jonsga tashlandi. Jons uning kelayotganini ko'rib, miltig'ini ko'tarib o'q uzdi. Sochma o'qlar Snoubolning orqasi bo'ylab qonli izlar qoldirdi va bir qo'y o'lib yiqildi. Bir lahza ham to'xtamasdan, Snoubol o'zining o'n besh stounlik vaznini Jonsning oyoqlariga otdi. Jons go'ng uyumiga uloqtirildi va miltig'i qo'lidan uchib ketdi.

paras.en: But the most terrifying spectacle of all was Boxer, rearing up on his hind legs and striking out with his great iron-shod hoofs like a stallion. His very first blow took a stable-lad from Foxwood on the skull and stretched him lifeless in the mud. At the sight, several men dropped their sticks and tried to run. Panic overtook them, and the next moment all the animals together were chasing them round and round the yard. They were gored, kicked, bitten, trampled on. There was not an animal on the farm that did not take vengeance on them after his own fashion. Even the cat suddenly leapt off a roof onto a cowman’s shoulders and sank her claws in his neck, at which he yelled horribly.
paras.uz: Lekin eng dahshatli manzara Bokser edi — u orqa oyoqlarida tikka turib, ulkan temir taqali tuyoqlari bilan ayg'irdek urardi. Uning birinchi zarbasi Foksvuddan kelgan otxona bolasining boshiga tegib, uni loyga jonsiz cho'zib qo'ydi. Buni ko'rib bir nechta odam tayog'ini tashlab qochishga urindi. Ularni vahima bosdi va keyingi lahzada barcha hayvonlar birgalikda ularni hovli bo'ylab aylantirib quvishardi. Ularni shox bilan sanchishdi, tepishdi, tishlashdi, oyoq osti qilishdi. Fermada o'zicha ulardan o'ch olmagan birorta hayvon qolmadi. Hatto mushuk ham birdan tomdan bir podachining yelkasiga sakrab, tirnoqlarini uning bo'yniga botirdi, u esa dahshatli baqirib yubordi.

paras.en: At a moment when the opening was clear, the men were glad enough to rush out of the yard and make a bolt for the main road. And so within five minutes of their invasion they were in ignominious retreat by the same way as they had come, with a flock of geese hissing after them and pecking at their calves all the way.
paras.uz: Yo'l ochilgan bir lahzada odamlar hovlidan otilib chiqib, katta yo'lga qochishdan juda xursand bo'lishdi. Shunday qilib, bosqindan besh daqiqa o'tmay ular kelgan yo'llaridan sharmandalarcha chekinib borishar, bir gala g'oz esa butun yo'l bo'yi vishillab, boldirlarini cho'qib, ularning ortidan quvardi.

paras.en: All the men were gone except one. Back in the yard Boxer was pawing with his hoof at the stable-lad who lay face down in the mud, trying to turn him over. The boy did not stir.
paras.uz: Bittasidan boshqa barcha odamlar ketib bo'lgan edi. Hovlida Bokser loyda yuztuban yotgan otxona bolasini ag'darishga urinib, uni tuyog'i bilan turtkilardi. Bola qimirlamasdi.

paras.en: ‘He is dead,’ said Boxer sorrowfully. ‘I had no intention of doing that. I forgot that I was wearing iron shoes. Who will believe that I did not do this on purpose?’
paras.uz: «U o'libdi, — dedi Bokser qayg'u bilan. — Men bunday qilishni niyat qilmagan edim. Temir taqa kiyib olganimni unutibman. Kim men buni ataylab qilmaganimga ishonadi?»

paras.en: ‘No sentimentality, comrade!’ cried Snowball from whose wounds the blood was still dripping. ‘War is war. The only good human being is a dead one.’
paras.uz: «Ko'ngilchanlik kerak emas, o'rtoq! — deb qichqirdi yaralaridan hali ham qon tomayotgan Snoubol. — Urush — urush. Yagona yaxshi inson — o'lik inson.»

paras.en: ‘I have no wish to take life, not even human life,’ repeated Boxer, and his eyes were full of tears.
paras.uz: «Men hech kimning jonini olishni istamayman, hatto insonning ham», — deb takrorladi Bokser, uning ko'zlari yoshga to'la edi.

paras.en: ‘Where is Mollie?’ exclaimed somebody.
paras.uz: «Molli qani?» — deb xitob qildi kimdir.

paras.en: Mollie in fact was missing. For a moment there was great alarm; it was feared that the men might have harmed her in some way, or even carried her off with them. In the end, however, she was found hiding in her stall with her head buried among the hay in the manger. She had taken to flight as soon as the gun went off. And when the others came back from looking for her, it was to find that the stable-lad, who in fact was only stunned, had already recovered and made off.
paras.uz: Haqiqatan ham Molli yo'q edi. Bir lahza katta xavotir ko'tarildi; odamlar unga qandaydir zarar yetkazgan yoki hatto o'zlari bilan olib ketgan bo'lishi mumkin, deb qo'rqishdi. Biroq oxir-oqibat uni o'z qo'rasida boshini oxurdagi pichanga tiqib yashirinib yotgan holda topishdi. U miltiq otilishi bilanoq qochib qolgan edi. Boshqalar uni qidirib qaytib kelishganda esa aslida faqat hushidan ketgan otxona bolasi o'ziga kelib, allaqachon qochib ketganini ko'rishdi.

paras.en: The animals had now reassembled in the wildest excitement, each recounting his own exploits in the battle at the top of his voice. An impromptu celebration of the victory was held immediately. The flag was run up and Beasts of England was sung a number of times, then the sheep who had been killed was given a solemn funeral, a hawthorn bush being planted on her grave. At the graveside Snowball made a little speech, emphasising the need for all animals to be ready to die for Animal Farm if need be.
paras.uz: Hayvonlar endi eng kuchli hayajonda yana yig'ilishdi, har biri jangdagi o'z qahramonliklarini baland ovozda hikoya qilardi. Darhol g'alabaning kutilmagan bayrami o'tkazildi. Bayroq ko'tarildi va «Angliya hayvonlari» bir necha marta kuylandi, keyin o'ldirilgan qo'yga tantanali dafn marosimi o'tkazilib, qabriga do'lana butasi ekildi. Qabr yonida Snoubol kichik nutq so'zlab, barcha hayvonlar zarur bo'lsa Hayvonlar fermasi uchun o'lishga tayyor bo'lishi kerakligini ta'kidladi.

paras.en: The animals decided unanimously to create a military decoration, ‘Animal Hero, First Class,’ which was conferred there and then on Snowball and Boxer. It consisted of a brass medal (they were really some old horse-brasses which had been found in the harness-room), to be worn on Sundays and holidays. There was also ‘Animal Hero, Second Class,’ which was conferred posthumously on the dead sheep.
paras.uz: Hayvonlar bir ovozdan «Birinchi darajali Hayvon Qahramoni» harbiy mukofotini ta'sis etishga qaror qilishdi va uni o'sha yerning o'zida Snoubol va Bokserga topshirishdi. U yakshanba va bayram kunlari taqiladigan jez medaldan iborat edi (aslida bular egar-jabduq xonasidan topilgan eski ot bezaklari edi). Shuningdek «Ikkinchi darajali Hayvon Qahramoni» mukofoti ham bo'lib, u o'lgan qo'yga vafotidan keyin berildi.

paras.en: There was much discussion as to what the battle should be called. In the end, it was named the Battle of the Cowshed, since that was where the ambush had been sprung. Mr. Jones’s gun had been found lying in the mud, and it was known that there was a supply of cartridges in the farmhouse. It was decided to set the gun up at the foot of the Flagstaff, like a piece of artillery, and to fire it twice a year – once on October the twelfth, the anniversary of the Battle of the Cowshed, and once on Midsummer Day, the anniversary of the Rebellion.
paras.uz: Jangni qanday atash kerakligi haqida ko'p bahs bo'ldi. Oxir-oqibat unga Molxona jangi deb nom berildi, chunki pistirma aynan o'sha yerdan ochilgan edi. Janob Jonsning miltig'i loyda yotgan holda topilgan edi va ferma uyida o'q-dori zaxirasi borligi ma'lum edi. Miltiqni to'p kabi bayroq ustunining tagiga o'rnatib, yiliga ikki marta — bir marta o'n ikkinchi oktyabrda, Molxona jangi yilligida, bir marta Yoz o'rtasi kunida, Qo'zg'olon yilligida otishga qaror qilindi.
