Uchta yosh qora minorka zotli makiyon boshchiligida tovuqlar Napoleonning xohishini barbod qilish uchun qat'iy harakat qilishdi. Ularning usuli to'sinlarga uchib chiqib, tuxumlarini o'sha yerda qo'yish edi, tuxumlar esa polga tushib chil-chil bo'lardi. Napoleon tez va shafqatsiz harakat qildi. U tovuqlarning ulushini to'xtatishni buyurdi va tovuqqa bir dona don bergan har qanday hayvon o'lim bilan jazolanishi haqida farmon chiqardi.

paras.en: The dogs saw to it that these orders were carried out. For five days the hens held out, then they capitulated and went back to their nesting boxes. Nine hens had died in the meantime. Their bodies were buried in the orchard, and it was given out that they had died of coccidiosis. Whymper heard nothing of this affair, and the eggs were duly delivered, a grocer's van driving up to the farm once a week to take them away.
paras.uz: Itlar bu buyruqlarning bajarilishini nazorat qilishdi. Tovuqlar besh kun chidashdi, keyin taslim bo'lib, in qutilariga qaytishdi. Bu orada to'qqizta tovuq o'ldi. Ularning jasadlari bog'ga ko'mildi va ular koktsidiozdan o'ldi, deb e'lon qilindi. Uimper bu voqea haqida hech narsa eshitmadi va tuxumlar o'z vaqtida yetkazib berildi — haftasiga bir marta baqqolning furgoni ularni olib ketish uchun fermaga kelardi.

paras.en: All this while no more had been seen of Snowball. He was rumoured to be hiding on one of the neighbouring farms, either Foxwood or Pinchfield. Napoleon was by this time on slightly better terms with the other farmers than before. It happened that there was in the yard a pile of timber which had been stacked there ten years earlier when a beech spinney was cleared. It was well seasoned, and Whymper had advised Napoleon to sell it; both Mr Pilkington and Mr Frederick were anxious to buy it. Napoleon was hesitating between the two, unable to make up his mind. It was noticed that whenever he seemed on the point of coming to an agreement with Frederick, Snowball was declared to be in hiding at Foxwood, while when he inclined towards Pilkington, Snowball was said to be at Pinchfield.
paras.uz: Bu vaqt davomida Snoubol boshqa ko'rinmadi. Mish-mishlarga ko'ra u qo'shni fermalardan birida — yo Foksvudda, yo Pinchfildda yashirinib yurgan ekan. Bu vaqtga kelib Napoleon boshqa fermerlar bilan avvalgidan biroz yaxshiroq munosabatda edi. Shunday bo'ldiki, hovlida o'n yil oldin qoraqayin butazori kesilganda taxlab qo'yilgan bir g'aram yog'och bor edi. U yaxshi qurigan edi va Uimper Napoleonga uni sotishni maslahat bergan edi; janob Pilkington ham, janob Frederik ham uni sotib olishni juda xohlashardi. Napoleon ikkovi o'rtasida ikkilanib, qaror qabul qila olmasdi. Payqalishicha, u Frederik bilan kelishuvga kelishga yaqinlashgandek ko'rinsa, Snoubol Foksvudda yashirinib yurgani e'lon qilinardi, Pilkingtonga moyil bo'lganda esa Snoubol Pinchfildda ekani aytilardi.

paras.en: Suddenly, early in the spring, an alarming thing was discovered. Snowball was secretly frequenting the farm by night! The animals were so disturbed that they could hardly sleep in their stalls. Every night, it was said, he came creeping in under cover of darkness and performed all kinds of mischief. He stole the corn, he upset the milk-pails, he broke the eggs, he trampled the seed-beds, he gnawed the bark off the fruit trees. Whenever anything went wrong it became usual to attribute it to Snowball. If a window was broken or a drain was blocked up, someone was certain to say that Snowball had come in the night and done it, and when the key of the stores-shed was lost the whole farm was convinced that Snowball had thrown it down the well. Curiously enough they went on believing this even after the mislaid key was found under a sack of meal. The cows declared unanimously that Snowball crept into their stalls and milked them in their sleep. The rats, which had been troublesome that winter, were also said to be in league with Snowball.
paras.uz: Erta bahorda birdan xavotirli narsa aniqlandi. Snoubol kechalari yashirincha fermaga kelib yurgan ekan! Hayvonlar shunchalik bezovtalandiki, qo'ralarida zo'rg'a uxlashardi. Aytishlaricha, u har kecha zulmat pardasi ostida o'rmalab kirib, har xil yovuzliklar qilardi. U donni o'g'irlar, sut chelaklarini ag'darar, tuxumlarni sindirar, ko'chat pushtalarini oyoq osti qilar, mevali daraxtlarning po'stlog'ini kemirardi. Biror narsa noto'g'ri ketsa, uni Snoubolga to'nkash odat tusiga kirdi. Agar deraza sinsa yoki zovur to'lib qolsa, kimdir albatta buni Snoubol kechasi kelib qildi, derdi, omborxona kaliti yo'qolganda esa butun ferma Snoubol uni quduqqa tashlab yuborganiga amin bo'ldi. Qizig'i shundaki, yo'qolgan kalit un qopi ostidan topilgandan keyin ham ular bunga ishonishda davom etishdi. Sigirlar bir ovozdan Snoubol qo'ralariga o'rmalab kirib, ularni uyqularida sog'ib ketishini aytishdi. O'sha qishda bezovta qilib kelgan kalamushlar ham Snoubol bilan til biriktirgan, deyishardi.

paras.en: Napoleon decreed that there should be a full investigation into Snowball's activities. With his dogs in attendance he set out and made a careful tour of inspection of the farm buildings, the other animals following at a respectful distance. At every few steps Napoleon stopped and snuffed the ground for traces of Snowball's footsteps, which, he said, he could detect by the smell. He snuffed in every corner, in the barn, in the cowshed, in the henhouses, in the vegetable garden, and found traces of Snowball almost everywhere. He would put his snout to the ground, give several deep sniffs and exclaim in a terrible voice, ‘Snowball! He has been here! I can smell him distinctly!’ and at the word ‘Snowball’ all the dogs let out blood-curdling growls and showed their side teeth.
paras.uz: Napoleon Snoubolning faoliyatini to'liq tekshirish haqida farmon chiqardi. Itlari hamrohligida u yo'lga chiqib, ferma binolarini sinchkovlik bilan ko'zdan kechirdi, boshqa hayvonlar esa hurmat masofasida orqasidan ergashishdi. Har bir necha qadamda Napoleon to'xtab, Snoubolning izlarini topish uchun yerni hidlardi — uning aytishicha, u ularni hididan aniqlay olardi. U har bir burchakni — molxonada, sigirxonada, tovuqxonalarda, sabzavot bog'ida — hidlab chiqdi va deyarli hamma joyda Snoubolning izlarini topdi. U tumshug'ini yerga tutib, bir necha marta chuqur hidlab, dahshatli ovozda: «Snoubol! U shu yerda bo'lgan! Uning hidini aniq sezyapman!» deb xitob qilardi, «Snoubol» so'zi aytilishi bilan esa barcha itlar qonni muzlatuvchi irillash chiqarib, qoziq tishlarini ko'rsatishardi.

paras.en: The animals were thoroughly frightened. It seemed to them as though Snowball were some kind of invisible influence, pervading the air about them and menacing them with all kinds of dangers. In the evening Squealer called them together, and with an alarmed expression on his face told them that he had some serious news to report.
paras.uz: Hayvonlar butunlay qo'rqib ketishdi. Ularga Snoubol atrofdagi havoni qamrab olgan va ularga har xil xavflar bilan tahdid solayotgan qandaydir ko'rinmas kuchdek tuyuldi. Kechqurun Skviler ularni yig'di va yuzida xavotirli ifoda bilan ularga jiddiy xabar aytmoqchi ekanini bildirdi.

paras.en: ‘Comrades!’ cried Squealer, making little nervous skips, ‘a most terrible thing has been discovered. Snowball has sold himself to Frederick of Pinchfield Farm, who is even now plotting to attack us and take our farm away from us! Snowball is to act as his guide when the attack begins. But there is worse than that. We had thought that Snowball's rebellion was caused simply by his vanity and ambition. But we were wrong, comrades. Do you know what the real reason was? Snowball was in league with Jones from the very start! He was Jones's secret agent all the time. It has all been proved by documents which he left behind him and which we have only just discovered. To my mind this explains a great deal, comrades. Did we not see for ourselves how he attempted – fortunately without success – to get us defeated and destroyed at the Battle of the Cowshed?’
paras.uz: «O'rtoqlar! — deb qichqirdi Skviler asabiy sakrab. — Eng dahshatli narsa aniqlandi. Snoubol o'zini Pinchfild fermasining egasi Frederikka sotibdi, u esa hozir ham bizga hujum qilib, fermamizni tortib olishni rejalashtirmoqda! Hujum boshlanganda Snoubol uning yo'lboshchisi bo'lishi kerak. Lekin bundan ham yomoni bor. Biz Snoubolning isyoni shunchaki uning manmanligi va shuhratparastligi tufayli bo'lgan deb o'ylagan edik. Lekin adashgan ekanmiz, o'rtoqlar. Haqiqiy sababi nima bo'lganini bilasizlarmi? Snoubol boshidanoq Jons bilan til biriktirgan ekan! U butun vaqt davomida Jonsning maxfiy agenti bo'lgan. Bularning hammasi u qoldirib ketgan va biz endigina topgan hujjatlar bilan isbotlandi. Menimcha, bu ko'p narsani tushuntiradi, o'rtoqlar. Uning Molxona jangida bizni mag'lub qilib, yo'q qilishga — xayriyatki, muvaffaqiyatsiz — urinishini o'z ko'zimiz bilan ko'rmaganmidik?»

paras.en: The animals were stupefied. This was a wickedness far outdoing Snowball's destruction of the windmill. But it was some minutes before they could fully take it in. They all remembered, or thought they remembered, how they had seen Snowball charging ahead of them at the Battle of the Cowshed, how he had rallied and encouraged them at every turn, and how he had not paused for an instant even when the pellets from Jones's gun had wounded his back. At first it was a little difficult to see how this fitted in with his being on Jones's side. Even Boxer, who seldom asked questions, was puzzled. He lay down, tucked his fore hoofs beneath him, shut his eyes, and with a hard effort managed to formulate his thoughts.
paras.uz: Hayvonlar karaxt bo'lib qolishdi. Bu Snoubolning shamol tegirmonini buzganidan ancha o'tib tushadigan yovuzlik edi. Lekin buni to'liq anglab yetishlari uchun bir necha daqiqa kerak bo'ldi. Hammalari Molxona jangida Snoubolning ulardan oldinda hujumga tashlanganini, har qadamda ularni qanday ruhlantirib, dalda berganini, hatto Jons miltig'idan otilgan sochma o'qlar uning orqasini yaralaganda ham bir lahza to'xtamaganini eslashardi yoki eslaymiz, deb o'ylashardi. Dastlab bu uning Jons tomonida bo'lganiga qanday mos kelishini tushunish biroz qiyin edi. Hatto kamdan-kam savol beradigan Bokser ham dovdirab qoldi. U yotib, oldingi tuyoqlarini tagiga yig'di, ko'zlarini yumdi va qattiq urinib, fikrlarini ifoda etishga muvaffaq bo'ldi.

paras.en: ‘I do not believe that,’ he said. ‘Snowball fought bravely at the Battle of the Cowshed. I saw him myself. Did we not give him “Animal Hero, First Class” immediately afterwards?’
paras.uz: «Men bunga ishonmayman, — dedi u. — Snoubol Molxona jangida jasorat bilan jang qildi. Buni o'zim ko'rganman. Darhol shundan keyin unga «Birinchi darajali Hayvon Qahramoni» unvonini bermaganmidik?»

paras.en: ‘That was our mistake, comrade. For we know now – it is all written down in the secret documents that we have found – that in reality he was trying to lure us to our doom.’
paras.uz: «Bu bizning xatoyimiz edi, o'rtoq. Chunki endi bilamiz — bularning hammasi biz topgan maxfiy hujjatlarda yozilgan — u aslida bizni halokatga boshlamoqchi bo'lgan.»

paras.en: ‘But he was wounded,’ said Boxer. ‘We all saw him running with blood.’
paras.uz: «Lekin u yaralangan edi-ku, — dedi Bokser. — Hammamiz uning qonga belanib chopganini ko'rdik.»

paras.en: ‘That was part of the arrangement!’ cried Squealer. ‘Jones's shot only grazed him. I could show you this in his own writing, if you were able to read it. The plot was for Snowball, at the critical moment, to give the signal for flight and leave the field to the enemy. And he very nearly succeeded – I will even say, comrades, he would have succeeded if it had not been for our heroic Leader, Comrade Napoleon. Do you not remember how, just at the moment when Jones and his men had got inside the yard, Snowball suddenly turned and fled, and many animals followed him? And do you not remember, too, that it was just at that moment, when panic was spreading and all seemed lost, that Comrade Napoleon sprang forward with a cry of “Death to Humanity!” and sank his teeth in Jones's leg? Surely you remember that, comrades?’ exclaimed Squealer, frisking from side to side.
paras.uz: «Bu kelishuvning bir qismi edi! — deb qichqirdi Skviler. — Jonsning o'qi uni faqat qirib o'tgan. Agar o'qiy olganingizda, buni sizga uning o'z qo'li bilan yozilgan holda ko'rsatishim mumkin edi. Fitna shunday edi: hal qiluvchi lahzada Snoubol qochish ishorasini berib, maydonni dushmanga qoldirishi kerak edi. Va u deyarli muvaffaqiyatga erishdi — hatto aytaman, o'rtoqlar, agar qahramon Dohiyimiz O'rtoq Napoleon bo'lmaganida, u muvaffaqiyatga erishgan bo'lardi. Jons va uning odamlari hovliga kirgan o'sha lahzada Snoubol birdan orqaga o'girilib qochganini va ko'p hayvonlar uning ortidan ergashganini eslamaysizmi? Va yana aynan o'sha lahzada, vahima tarqalib, hammasi boy berilgandek tuyulganda, O'rtoq Napoleon «Insoniyatga o'lim!» deb hayqirib oldinga otilganini va tishlarini Jonsning oyog'iga botirganini eslamaysizmi? Buni eslaysiz-ku, o'rtoqlar?» — deb xitob qildi Skviler, u yoqdan-bu yoqqa o'ynoqlab.

paras.en: Now when Squealer described the scene so graphically, it seemed to the animals that they did remember it. At any rate, they remembered that at the critical moment of the battle Snowball had turned to flee. But Boxer was still a little uneasy.
paras.uz: Endi Skviler bu manzarani shunchalik jonli tasvirlagach, hayvonlarga go'yo buni eslaydigandek tuyuldi. Har holda, ular jangning hal qiluvchi lahzasida Snoubol qochish uchun orqaga o'girilganini eslashdi. Lekin Bokser hali ham biroz bezovta edi.

paras.en: ‘I do not believe that Snowball was a traitor at the beginning’ he said finally. ‘What he has done since is different. But I believe that at the Battle of the Cowshed he was a good comrade.’
paras.uz: «Men Snoubol boshida xoin bo'lganiga ishonmayman, — dedi u nihoyat. — Keyin qilgan ishlari boshqa gap. Lekin ishonamanki, Molxona jangida u yaxshi o'rtoq edi.»

paras.en: ‘Our Leader, Comrade Napoleon,’ announced Squealer, speaking very slowly and firmly, ‘has stated categorically – categorically, comrade – that Snowball was Jones's agent from the very beginning – yes, and from long before the Rebellion was ever thought of.’
paras.uz: «Dohiyimiz O'rtoq Napoleon, — deb e'lon qildi Skviler juda sekin va qat'iy gapirib, — qat'iyan — qat'iyan, o'rtoq — Snoubol boshidanoq Jonsning agenti bo'lganini aytdi, — ha, hatto Qo'zg'olon haqida o'ylanmasdan ancha oldin ham.»

paras.en: ‘Ah, that is different!’ said Boxer. ‘If Comrade Napoleon says it, it must be right.’
paras.uz: «Ha, bu boshqa gap! — dedi Bokser. — Agar O'rtoq Napoleon shunday desa, demak to'g'ri.»

paras.en: ‘That is the true spirit, comrade!’ cried Squealer, but it was noticed he cast a very ugly look at Boxer with his little twinkling eyes. He turned to go, then paused and added impressively: ‘I warn every animal on this farm to keep his eyes very wide open. For we have reason to think that some of Snowball's secret agents are lurking among us at this moment!’
paras.uz: «Mana haqiqiy ruh, o'rtoq!» — deb qichqirdi Skviler, lekin u kichkina chaqnab turgan ko'zlari bilan Bokserga juda xunuk qarab qo'ygani payqaldi. U ketish uchun o'girildi, keyin to'xtab, salobat bilan qo'shib qo'ydi: «Bu fermadagi har bir hayvonni ko'zini katta ochib yurishga ogohlantiraman. Chunki hozir ham oramizda Snoubolning ba'zi maxfiy agentlari yashirinib yurgan deb o'ylashimizga asos bor!»

paras.en: Four days later, in the late afternoon, Napoleon ordered all the animals to assemble in the yard. When they were all gathered together Napoleon emerged from the farmhouse, wearing both his medals (for he had recently awarded himself ‘Animal Hero, First Class’ and ‘Animal Hero, Second Class’), with his nine huge dogs frisking round him and uttering growls that sent shivers down all the animals’ spines. They all cowered silently in their places, seeming to know in advance that some terrible thing was about to happen.
paras.uz: To'rt kundan keyin, kech tushga yaqin, Napoleon barcha hayvonlarga hovliga yig'ilishni buyurdi. Hammalari yig'ilgach, Napoleon ferma uyidan ikkala medalini taqib chiqdi (chunki yaqinda u o'ziga «Birinchi darajali Hayvon Qahramoni» va «Ikkinchi darajali Hayvon Qahramoni» unvonlarini bergan edi), atrofida to'qqizta ulkan iti o'ynoqlab, barcha hayvonlarning umurtqasini titratadigan irillash chiqarardi. Hammalari jimgina o'z joylarida qisinib o'tirishdi, go'yo qandaydir dahshatli narsa sodir bo'lishini oldindan bilgandek edilar.

paras.en: Napoleon stood sternly surveying his audience; then he uttered a high-pitched whimper. Immediately the dogs bounded forward, seized four of the pigs by the ear and dragged them, squealing with pain and terror, to Napoleon's feet. The pigs’ ears were bleeding, the dogs had tasted blood, and for a few moments they appeared to go quite mad. To the amazement of everybody three of them flung themselves upon Boxer. Boxer saw them coming and put out his great hoof, caught a dog in mid-air and pinned him to the ground. The dog shrieked for mercy and the other two fled with their tails between their legs. Boxer looked at Napoleon to know whether he should crush the dog to death or let it go. Napoleon appeared to change countenance, and sharply ordered Boxer to let the dog go, whereat Boxer lifted his hoof, and the dog slunk away, bruised and howling.
paras.uz: Napoleon tinglovchilarini qattiq nigoh bilan ko'zdan kechirib turdi; keyin ingichka chiyilladi. Darhol itlar oldinga sakrab, to'rtta cho'chqani qulog'idan tishlab olishdi va og'riq va dahshatdan chinqirayotgan holda ularni Napoleonning oyoqlari ostiga sudrab kelishdi. Cho'chqalarning quloqlari qonardi, itlar qon ta'mini totib ko'rgan edi va bir necha lahza ular butunlay aqldan ozgandek bo'lishdi. Hammani hayratga solib, ulardan uchtasi Bokserga tashlandi. Bokser ularning kelayotganini ko'rib, ulkan tuyog'ini uzatdi, bir itni havodayoq tutib, yerga bosib oldi. It rahm so'rab chinqirdi, qolgan ikkitasi esa dumlarini qisib qochishdi. Bokser itni ezib o'ldirish yoki qo'yib yuborishni bilish uchun Napoleonga qaradi. Napoleonning chehrasi o'zgargandek bo'ldi va u Bokserga itni qo'yib yuborishni keskin buyurdi, shundan keyin Bokser tuyog'ini ko'tardi va it ezilgan va uvillagan holda sudralib ketdi.

paras.en: Presently the tumult died down. The four pigs waited, trembling, with guilt written on every line of their countenances. Napoleon now called upon them to confess their crimes. They were the same four pigs as had protested when Napoleon abolished the Sunday Meetings. Without any further prompting they confessed that they had been secretly in touch with Snowball ever since his expulsion, that they had collaborated with him in destroying the windmill, and that they had entered into an agreement with him to hand over Animal Farm to Mr Frederick. They added that Snowball had privately admitted to them that he had been Jones's secret agent for years past. When they had finished their confession the dogs promptly tore their throats out, and in a terrible voice Napoleon demanded whether any other animal had anything to confess.
paras.uz: Ko'p o'tmay shovqin tindi. To'rtta cho'chqa chehrasining har bir chizig'ida ayb yozilgan holda titrab kutib turishdi. Endi Napoleon ularni jinoyatlarini tan olishga chaqirdi. Bular Napoleon yakshanba Yig'ilishlarini bekor qilganda norozilik bildirgan o'sha to'rtta cho'chqa edi. Boshqa hech qanday turtkisiz ular Snoubol haydalganidan beri u bilan yashirincha aloqada bo'lganliklarini, shamol tegirmonini buzishda u bilan hamkorlik qilganliklarini va Hayvonlar fermasini janob Frederikka topshirish haqida u bilan kelishuvga kirishganliklarini tan olishdi. Ular yana Snoubol xufyona ularga ko'p yillardan beri Jonsning maxfiy agenti bo'lganini tan olganini qo'shishdi. Ular e'tiroflarini tugatishlari bilanoq itlar darhol ularning bo'g'zini yulib tashlashdi va Napoleon dahshatli ovozda yana biror hayvonning tan oladigan narsasi bormi, deb talab qildi.

paras.en: The three hens who had been the ringleaders in the attempted rebellion over the eggs now came forward and stated that Snowball had appeared to them in a dream and incited them to disobey Napoleon's orders. They too were slaughtered. Then a goose came forward and confessed to having secreted six ears of corn during the last year's harvest and eaten them in the night. Then a sheep confessed to having urinated in the drinking pool – urged to do this, so she said, by Snowball – and two other sheep confessed to having murdered an old ram, an especially devoted follower of Napoleon, by chasing him round and round a bonfire when he was suffering from a cough. They were all slain on the spot. And so the tale of confessions and executions went on, until there was a pile of corpses lying before Napoleon's feet and the air was heavy with the smell of blood, which had been unknown there since the expulsion of Jones.
paras.uz: Tuxumlar ustidan bo'lgan isyon urinishining boshida turgan uchta tovuq endi oldinga chiqib, Snoubol ularga tushlarida ko'rinib, ularni Napoleonning buyruqlariga bo'ysunmaslikka undaganini aytishdi. Ular ham so'yildi. Keyin bir g'oz oldinga chiqib, o'tgan yilgi hosil paytida oltita boshoqni yashirib, kechasi yeb qo'yganini tan oldi. Keyin bir qo'y sug'orish hovuziga siyganini tan oldi — uning aytishicha, bunga uni Snoubol undagan ekan — yana ikkita qo'y yo'tal bilan og'rib yurgan, Napoleonning ayniqsa sodiq tarafdori bo'lgan keksa qo'chqorni gulxan atrofida aylantirib quvib, o'ldirganliklarini tan olishdi. Ularning hammasi joyida o'ldirildi. Shunday qilib e'tiroflar va qatllar zanjiri davom etdi, toki Napoleonning oyoqlari ostida jasadlar uyumi yotib qolmaguncha va havo Jons haydalganidan beri u yerda noma'lum bo'lgan qon hidiga to'lmaguncha.

paras.en: When it was all over, the remaining animals, except for the pigs and dogs, crept away in a body. They were shaken and miserable. They did not know which was more shocking – the treachery of the animals who had leagued themselves with Snowball, or the cruel retribution they had just witnessed. In the old days there had often been scenes of bloodshed equally terrible, but it seemed to all of them that it was far worse now that it was happening among themselves. Since Jones had left the farm, until today, no animal had killed another animal. Not even a rat had been killed.
paras.uz: Hammasi tugagach, cho'chqalar va itlardan tashqari qolgan hayvonlar to'da bo'lib sudralib ketishdi. Ular larzaga tushgan va baxtsiz edi. Ular qaysi biri dahshatliroq ekanini bilishmasdi — Snoubol bilan til biriktirgan hayvonlarning xiyonatimi yoki hozirgina guvoh bo'lgan shafqatsiz jazomi. Eski kunlarda ham ko'pincha xuddi shunday dahshatli qon to'kish manzaralari bo'lgan, lekin hammasiga bu endi o'z oralarida sodir bo'layotgani uchun ancha yomonroq tuyuldi. Jons fermani tark etganidan beri, bugungi kungacha, hech bir hayvon boshqa hayvonni o'ldirmagan edi. Hatto biror kalamush ham o'ldirilmagan edi.

paras.en: They had made their way onto the little knoll where the half-finished windmill stood, and with one accord they all lay down as though huddling together for warmth – Clover, Muriel, Benjamin, the cows, the sheep and a whole flock of geese and hens – every one, indeed, except the cat, who had suddenly disappeared just before Napoleon ordered the animals to assemble. For some time nobody spoke. Only Boxer remained on his feet. He fidgeted to and fro, swishing his long black tail against his sides and occasionally uttering a little whinny of surprise. Finally he said:
paras.uz: Ular yarim qurilgan shamol tegirmoni turgan kichik tepalikka chiqib olishdi va bir ovozdan, go'yo isinish uchun bir-biriga qisilgandek yotishdi — Klover, Muriel, Benjamin, sigirlar, qo'ylar va bir gala g'oz va tovuqlar — aslida hamma, faqat Napoleon hayvonlarga yig'ilishni buyurishidan sal oldin birdan g'oyib bo'lgan mushukdan tashqari. Bir muddat hech kim gapirmadi. Faqat Bokser oyoqda qoldi. U u yoqdan-bu yoqqa bezovta yurar, uzun qora dumini biqinlariga urar va vaqti-vaqti bilan hayratdan ohista kishnab qo'yardi. Nihoyat u dedi:

paras.en: ‘I do not understand it. I would not have believed that such things could happen on our farm. It must be due to some fault in ourselves. The solution, as I see it, is to work harder. From now onwards I shall get up a full hour earlier in the mornings.’ And he moved off at his lumbering trot and made for the quarry. Having got there he collected two successive loads of stone and dragged them down to the windmill before retiring for the night.
paras.uz: «Men buni tushunmayapman. Fermamizda bunday narsalar sodir bo'lishi mumkinligiga ishonmagan bo'lardim. Bu o'zimizdagi qandaydir nuqson tufayli bo'lsa kerak. Menimcha, yechim — ko'proq ishlash. Bundan buyon ertalab butun bir soat oldin turaman.» Va u og'ir yo'rtig'ida yo'lga tushib, konga yo'naldi. U yerga yetib borib, ketma-ket ikki yuk tosh yig'di va tunashga ketishdan oldin ularni shamol tegirmoniga sudrab olib bordi.

paras.en: The animals huddled about Clover, not speaking. The knoll where they were lying gave them a wide prospect across the countryside. Most of Animal Farm was within their view – the long pasture stretching down to the main road, the hayfield, the spinney, the drinking pool, the ploughed fields where the young wheat was thick and green, and the red roofs of the farm buildings with the smoke curling from the chimneys. It was a clear spring evening. The grass and the bursting hedges were gilded by the level rays of the sun. Never had the farm – and with a kind of surprise they remembered that it was their own farm, every inch of it their own property – appeared to the animals so desirable a place. As Clover looked down the hillside her eyes filled with tears.
paras.uz: Hayvonlar gapirmasdan Kloverning atrofiga to'planishdi. Ular yotgan tepalikdan qishloq bo'ylab keng manzara ochilardi. Hayvonlar fermasining katta qismi ko'z oldida edi — katta yo'lgacha cho'zilgan uzun yaylov, pichanzor, butazor, sug'orish hovuzi, yosh bug'doy qalin va yam-yashil o'sib turgan haydalgan dalalar va mo'rilaridan buralib tutun chiqayotgan ferma binolarining qizil tomlari. Tiniq bahor oqshomi edi. O't va kurtak yozayotgan to'siqlar quyoshning yotiq nurlarida oltindek tovlanardi. Ferma hayvonlarga hech qachon — va ular qandaydir hayrat bilan uning o'z fermalari, har bir qarichi o'z mulklari ekanini esladilar — bunchalik orzu qilingan joy bo'lib ko'rinmagan edi. Klover tepalik yonbag'riga qararkan, ko'zlari yoshga to'ldi.

paras.en: If she could have spoken her thoughts, it would have been to say that this was not what they had aimed at when they had set themselves years ago to work for the overthrow of the human race. These scenes of terror and slaughter were not what they had looked forward to on that night when old Major first stirred them to rebellion. If she herself had had any picture of the future, it had been of a society of animals set free from hunger and the whip, all equal, each working according to his capacity, the strong protecting the weak, as she had protected the lost brood of ducklings with her foreleg on the night of Major's speech.
paras.uz: Agar u fikrlarini aytib bera olganida, bu ular yillar oldin inson zotini ag'darish uchun ishlashga kirishganlarida ko'zlagan narsa emasligini aytgan bo'lardi. Bu dahshat va qirg'in manzaralari keksa Mayor ularni birinchi marta qo'zg'olonga undagan o'sha kechada intiqib kutgan narsalari emas edi. Agar uning o'zida kelajak haqida biror tasavvur bo'lgan bo'lsa, u ochlik va qamchidan ozod bo'lgan, hammasi teng, har biri qobiliyatiga yarasha ishlaydigan, kuchli zaifni himoya qiladigan hayvonlar jamiyati edi — xuddi Mayor nutq so'zlagan kechada u adashib qolgan o'rdakchalarni oldingi oyog'i bilan himoya qilgani kabi.

paras.en: Instead – she did not know why – they had come to a time when no one dared speak his mind, when fierce, growling dogs roamed everywhere, and when you had to watch your comrades torn to pieces after confessing to shocking crimes. There was no thought of rebellion or disobedience in her mind. She knew that even as things were they were far better off than they had been in the days of Jones, and that before all else it was needful to prevent the return of the human beings. Whatever happened she would remain faithful, work hard, carry out the orders that were given to her, and accept the leadership of Napoleon. But still, it was not for this that she and all the other animals had hoped and toiled. It was not for this that they had built the windmill and faced the pellets of Jones's gun. Such were her thoughts, though she lacked the words to express them.
paras.uz: Buning o'rniga — u nega ekanini bilmasdi — ular hech kim fikrini aytishga jur'at etmaydigan, hamma joyda yovuz, irillaydigan itlar izg'ib yuradigan va dahshatli jinoyatlarni tan olgandan keyin o'rtoqlaringning parchalab tashlanishini tomosha qilish kerak bo'lgan zamonga kelib qolishgan edi. Uning xayolida isyon yoki bo'ysunmaslik haqida hech qanday fikr yo'q edi. U hatto hozirgi ahvolda ham Jons davridagidan ancha yaxshi yashashlarini va hamma narsadan oldin insonlarning qaytishiga yo'l qo'ymaslik zarurligini bilardi. Nima bo'lmasin, u sodiq qoladi, qattiq ishlaydi, unga berilgan buyruqlarni bajaradi va Napoleonning rahbarligini qabul qiladi. Lekin baribir, u va boshqa barcha hayvonlar shuning uchun umid qilib, mehnat qilishmagan edi. Ular shamol tegirmonini qurib, Jons miltig'ining o'qlariga ko'kragini tutganlari shuning uchun emas edi. Uning fikrlari shunday edi, garchi ularni ifoda etish uchun so'zlari yetishmasa ham.

paras.en: At last, feeling this to be in some way a substitute for the words she was unable to find, she began to sing ‘Beasts of England’. The other animals sitting round her took it up, and they sang it three times over – very tunefully, but slowly and mournfully, in a way they had never sung it before.
paras.uz: Nihoyat, buni qandaydir yo'l bilan topa olmagan so'zlari o'rnini bosadi, deb his qilib, u «Angliya hayvonlari»ni kuylay boshladi. Atrofida o'tirgan boshqa hayvonlar unga qo'shilishdi va ular uni uch marta kuylashdi — juda ohangdor, lekin ilgari hech qachon kuylamagan tarzda sekin va g'amgin.

paras.en: They had just finished singing it for the third time when Squealer, attended by two dogs, approached them with the air of having something important to say. He announced that, by a special decree of Comrade Napoleon, ‘Beasts of England’ had been abolished. From now onwards it was forbidden to sing it.
paras.uz: Ular uni uchinchi marta endigina kuylab bo'lishganda, ikki it hamrohligida Skviler muhim gapi bordek qiyofada ularga yaqinlashdi. U O'rtoq Napoleonning maxsus farmoni bilan «Angliya hayvonlari» bekor qilinganini e'lon qildi. Bundan buyon uni kuylash taqiqlandi.

paras.en: The animals were taken aback.
paras.uz: Hayvonlar dovdirab qolishdi.

paras.en: ‘Why?’ cried Muriel.
paras.uz: «Nega?» — deb qichqirdi Muriel.

paras.en: ‘It is no longer needed, comrade,’ said Squealer stiffly. ‘“Beasts of England” was the song of the Rebellion. But the Rebellion is now completed. The execution of the traitors this afternoon was the final act. The enemy both external and internal has been defeated. In “Beasts of England” we expressed our longing for a better society in days to come. But that society has now been established. Clearly this song has no longer any purpose.’
paras.uz: «U endi kerak emas, o'rtoq, — dedi Skviler qat'iy ohangda. — «Angliya hayvonlari» Qo'zg'olon qo'shig'i edi. Lekin Qo'zg'olon endi yakunlandi. Bugun tushdan keyin xoinlarning qatl etilishi uning so'nggi pardasi bo'ldi. Tashqi ham, ichki ham dushman mag'lub etildi. «Angliya hayvonlari»da biz kelajakdagi yaxshiroq jamiyatga intilishimizni ifoda etgan edik. Lekin u jamiyat endi barpo etildi. Ravshanki, bu qo'shiqning endi hech qanday maqsadi qolmadi.»

paras.en: Frightened though they were, some of the animals might possibly have protested, but at this moment the sheep set up their usual bleating of ‘Four legs good, two legs bad’, which went on for several minutes and put an end to the discussion.
paras.uz: Qo'rqib turishgan bo'lsa ham, ba'zi hayvonlar balki norozilik bildirishi mumkin edi, lekin shu lahzada qo'ylar odatdagi «To'rt oyoq — yaxshi, ikki oyoq — yomon» ma'rashini boshlashdi, bu bir necha daqiqa davom etib, muhokamaga chek qo'ydi.

paras.en: So ‘Beasts of England’ was heard no more. In its place Minimus, the poet, had composed another song which began:
paras.uz: Shunday qilib «Angliya hayvonlari» boshqa eshitilmadi. Uning o'rniga shoir Minimus quyidagicha boshlanadigan boshqa qo'shiq to'qigan edi:

paras.en: Animal Farm, Animal Farm, / Never through me shalt thou come to harm!
paras.uz: Hayvonlar fermasi, Hayvonlar fermasi, / Mendan senga hech qachon yetmas zarar!

paras.en: and this was sung every Sunday morning after the hoisting of the flag. But somehow neither the words nor the tune ever seemed to the animals to come up to ‘Beasts of England’.
paras.uz: va bu har yakshanba ertalab bayroq ko'tarilgandan keyin kuylanardi. Lekin negadir hayvonlarga na so'zlari, na kuyi hech qachon «Angliya hayvonlari»ga yetadigandek tuyulmadi.

gloss.ex: One Sunday morning Squealer announced that the hens, who had just come in to lay again, must surrender their eggs. Napoleon had accepted,…
…on every line of their countenances. Napoleon now called upon them to confess their crimes. They were the same four pigs as had protested when Napoleon abolishe…
…. They were all slain on the spot. And so the tale of confessions and executions went on, until there was a pile of corpses lying before Napoleon's feet and the…
…four of the pigs by the ear and dragged them, squealing with pain and terror, to Napoleon's feet. The pigs’ ears were bleeding, the dogs had tasted blood, and f…
…needed, comrade,’ said Squealer stiffly. ‘“Beasts of England” was the song of the Rebellion. But the Rebellion is now completed. The execution of the traitors t…

quiz.q: Why is 'Beasts of England' abolished?
o: Squealer says the Rebellion is completed
quiz.why_uz: Qo'shiq kelajakdagi jamiyat orzusi edi — endi u «barpo etilgan».

quiz.q: What does Clover realise on the knoll?
o: This was not what they had worked for
quiz.why_uz: U fikrini so'z bilan ifoda eta olmaydi.

chapters.recap_uz: Qahraton qishda ochlik boshlanadi, buni Uimperdan yashirishadi. Tovuqlar isyoni bostiriladi. Hamma yomonlik Snoubolga to'nkaladi. Hayvonlar «xiyonatni» tan oladi va itlar ularni o'ldiradi. Klover yig'laydi; «Angliya hayvonlari» taqiqlanadi.

chapters.title: The Battle of the Windmill

paras.en: A few days later, when the terror caused by the executions had died down, some of the animals remembered – or thought they remembered – that the Sixth Commandment decreed: ‘No animal shall kill any other animal.’ And though no one cared to mention it in the hearing of the pigs or the dogs, it was felt that the killings which had taken place did not square with this. Clover asked Benjamin to read her the Sixth Commandment, and when Benjamin, as usual, said that he refused to meddle in such matters, she fetched Muriel. Muriel read the Commandment for her. It ran: ‘No animal shall kill any other animal without cause.’ Somehow or other the last two words had slipped out of the animals’ memory. But they saw now that the Commandment had not been violated; for clearly there was good reason for killing the traitors who had leagued themselves with Snowball.
paras.uz: Bir necha kundan keyin, qatllar keltirib chiqargan dahshat bosilgach, ba'zi hayvonlar Oltinchi Amrda «Hech bir hayvon boshqa hayvonni o'ldirmaydi» deyilganini esladilar — yoki eslaymiz, deb o'yladilar. Garchi hech kim buni cho'chqalar yoki itlar eshitadigan joyda tilga olishni istamasa ham, sodir bo'lgan qotilliklar bunga to'g'ri kelmasligi his qilinardi. Klover Benjamindan unga Oltinchi Amrni o'qib berishni so'radi, Benjamin esa odatdagidek bunday ishlarga aralashishdan bosh tortganini aytgach, Murielni olib keldi. Muriel unga Amrni o'qib berdi. Unda shunday deyilgan edi: «Hech bir hayvon boshqa hayvonni sababsiz o'ldirmaydi.» Qandaydir tarzda oxirgi so'z hayvonlarning xotirasidan chiqib ketgan edi. Lekin endi ular Amr buzilmaganini ko'rishdi; chunki Snoubol bilan til biriktirgan xoinlarni o'ldirish uchun yaxshi sabab borligi ravshan edi.

paras.en: Throughout that year the animals worked even harder than they had worked in the previous year. To rebuild the windmill, with walls twice as thick as before, and to finish it by the appointed date, together with the regular work of the farm, was a tremendous labour. There were times when it seemed to the animals that they worked longer hours and fed no better than they had done in Jones's day. On Sunday mornings Squealer, holding down a long strip of paper with his trotter, would read out to them lists of figures proving that the production of every class of foodstuff had increased by two hundred per cent, three hundred per cent, or five hundred per cent, as the case might be. The animals saw no reason to disbelieve him, especially as they could no longer remember very clearly what conditions had been like before the Rebellion. All the same, there were days when they felt that they would sooner have had less figures and more food.
paras.uz: O'sha yil bo'yi hayvonlar o'tgan yilgidan ham ko'proq ishlashdi. Shamol tegirmonini devorlarini avvalgidan ikki baravar qalin qilib qayta qurish va uni fermaning odatiy ishlari bilan birga belgilangan muddatda tugatish ulkan mehnat edi. Ba'zan hayvonlarga ular Jons davridagidan ko'proq soat ishlab, undan yaxshiroq ovqatlanmayotgandek tuyulardi. Yakshanba ertalablari Skviler uzun qog'oz tasmasini tuyog'i bilan bosib turib, ularga har bir turdagi oziq-ovqat ishlab chiqarish holatga qarab ikki yuz foiz, uch yuz foiz yoki besh yuz foizga oshganini isbotlovchi raqamlar ro'yxatini o'qib berardi. Hayvonlar unga ishonmaslik uchun hech qanday sabab ko'rmasdi, ayniqsa Qo'zg'olondan oldin sharoit qanday bo'lganini endi unchalik aniq eslay olmasdilar. Shunga qaramay, ba'zi kunlari ular raqamlar kamroq, ovqat esa ko'proq bo'lishini afzal ko'rishlarini his qilishardi.

paras.en: All orders were now issued through Squealer or one of the other pigs. Napoleon himself was not seen in public as often as once in a fortnight. When he did appear he was attended not only by his retinue of dogs but by a black cockerel who marched in front of him and acted as a kind of trumpeter, letting out a loud ‘cock-a-doodle-doo’ before Napoleon spoke. Even in the farmhouse, it was said, Napoleon inhabited separate apartments from the others. He took his meals alone, with two dogs to wait upon him, and always ate from the Crown Derby dinner service which had been in the glass cupboard in the drawing-room. It was also announced that the gun would be fired every year on Napoleon's birthday, as well as on the other two anniversaries.
paras.uz: Endi barcha buyruqlar Skviler yoki boshqa cho'chqalardan biri orqali berilardi. Napoleonning o'zi ikki haftada bir marta ham ko'pchilik oldida ko'rinmasdi. U ko'ringanda nafaqat itlar mulozimligida, balki oldida qadam tashlab boradigan va qandaydir karnaychi vazifasini bajaradigan qora xo'roz hamrohligida chiqardi — xo'roz Napoleon gapirishidan oldin baland ovozda «qu-qu-qu!» deb qichqirardi. Aytishlaricha, hatto ferma uyida ham Napoleon boshqalardan alohida xonalarda yasharkan. U yolg'iz, ikki it xizmatida ovqatlanar va doim mehmonxonadagi oynali shkafda turgan «Kroun Derbi» chinni idishlaridan yerdi. Shuningdek, miltiq har yili boshqa ikki yillik bilan bir qatorda Napoleonning tug'ilgan kunida ham otilishi e'lon qilindi.

paras.en: Napoleon was now never spoken of simply as ‘Napoleon’. He was always referred to in formal style as ‘our Leader, Comrade Napoleon’, and the pigs liked to invent for him such titles as Father of All Animals, Terror of Mankind, Protector of the Sheepfold, Ducklings’ Friend, and the like. In his speeches Squealer would talk with the tears rolling down his cheeks of Napoleon's wisdom, the goodness of his heart, and the deep love he bore to all animals everywhere, even and especially the unhappy animals who still lived in ignorance and slavery on other farms. It had become usual to give Napoleon the credit for every successful achievement and every stroke of good fortune. You would often hear one hen remark to another, ‘Under the guidance of our Leader, Comrade Napoleon, I have laid five eggs in six days’; or two cows, enjoying a drink at the pool, would exclaim, ‘Thanks to the leadership of Comrade Napoleon, how excellent this water tastes!’ The general feeling on the farm was expressed in a poem entitled ‘Comrade Napoleon’, which was composed by Minimus and which ran as follows:
paras.uz: Endi Napoleon haqida hech qachon shunchaki «Napoleon» deb gapirilmasdi. Uni doim rasmiy uslubda «Dohiyimiz, O'rtoq Napoleon» deb atashardi, cho'chqalar esa unga Barcha Hayvonlar Otasi, Insoniyat Dahshati, Qo'yxona Himoyachisi, O'rdakchalar Do'sti va shunga o'xshash unvonlar o'ylab topishni yaxshi ko'rishardi. Skviler nutqlarida yonoqlaridan yosh oqizib Napoleonning donoligi, yuragining ezguligi va hamma joydagi barcha hayvonlarga, hatto, ayniqsa, boshqa fermalarda hali ham jaholat va qullikda yashayotgan baxtsiz hayvonlarga bo'lgan chuqur muhabbati haqida gapirardi. Har bir muvaffaqiyatli yutuq va har bir omadni Napoleonga nisbat berish odat tusiga kirgan edi. Ko'pincha bir tovuqning boshqasiga «Dohiyimiz O'rtoq Napoleonning rahbarligi ostida olti kunda beshta tuxum qo'ydim» deganini, yoki hovuzda suv ichib huzur qilayotgan ikki sigirning «O'rtoq Napoleonning rahbarligi tufayli bu suv qanchalik mazali!» deb xitob qilganini eshitish mumkin edi. Fermadagi umumiy kayfiyat Minimus to'qigan «O'rtoq Napoleon» nomli she'rda ifodalangan edi, u quyidagicha edi:

paras.en: Friend of the fatherless! / Fountain of happiness! / Lord of the swill-bucket! Oh, how my soul is on / Fire when I gaze at thy / Calm and commanding eye, / Like the sun in the sky, / Comrade Napoleon!
paras.uz: Yetimlar do'sti! / Baxt bulog'i! / Yemish chelagining xo'jasi! Oh, qalbim qanday / Yonadi, qarasam / Sokin, amr etuvchi ko'zingga, / Osmondagi quyoshdek, / O'rtoq Napoleon!

paras.en: Thou art the giver of / All that thy creatures love, / Full belly twice a day, clean straw to roll upon; / Every beast great or small / Sleeps at peace in his stall, / Thou watchest over all, / Comrade Napoleon!
paras.uz: Sensan beruvchi / Jonzotlaring sevgan har narsani, / Kuniga ikki mahal to'q qorin, ag'nashga toza somonni; / Har bir hayvon, katta-kichik, / Qo'rasida tinch uxlar, / Hammani sen kuzatasan, / O'rtoq Napoleon!

paras.en: Had I a sucking-pig, / Ere he had grown as big / Even as a pint bottle or as a rolling-pin, / He should have learned to be / Faithful and true to thee, / Yes, his first squeak should be / ‘Comrade Napoleon!’
paras.uz: Bo'lsaydi emizikli cho'chqacham, / U bir pint shishadek / Yoki xamir o'qlog'idek bo'lmasdan turib, / O'rganardi bo'lishni / Senga sodiq va vafodor, / Ha, uning ilk chiyillashi / «O'rtoq Napoleon!» bo'lardi.

paras.en: Napoleon approved of this poem and caused it to be inscribed on the wall of the big barn, at the opposite end from the Seven Commandments. It was surmounted by a portrait of Napoleon, in profile, executed by Squealer in white paint.
paras.uz: Napoleon bu she'rni ma'qulladi va uni katta molxonaning devoriga, Yetti Amrning qarama-qarshi tomoniga yozdirib qo'ydi. Uning tepasida Skviler oq bo'yoq bilan chizgan Napoleonning yon tomondan portreti bor edi.

paras.en: Meanwhile, through the agency of Whymper, Napoleon was engaged in complicated negotiations with Frederick and Pilkington. The pile of timber was still unsold. Of the two, Frederick was the more anxious to get hold of it, but he would not offer a reasonable price. At the same time there were renewed rumours that Frederick and his men were plotting to attack Animal Farm and to destroy the windmill, the building of which had aroused furious jealousy in him. Snowball was known to be still skulking on Pinchfield Farm. In the middle of the summer the animals were alarmed to hear that three hens had come forward and confessed that, inspired by Snowball, they had entered into a plot to murder Napoleon. They were executed immediately, and fresh precautions for Napoleon's safety were taken. Four dogs guarded his bed at night, one at each corner, and a young pig named Pinkeye was given the task of tasting all his food before he ate it, lest it should be poisoned.
paras.uz: Bu orada Uimper vositachiligida Napoleon Frederik va Pilkington bilan murakkab muzokaralar olib borardi. Yog'och g'arami hali ham sotilmagan edi. Ikkovidan Frederik uni qo'lga kiritishni ko'proq xohlardi, lekin u munosib narx taklif qilmasdi. Ayni paytda Frederik va uning odamlari Hayvonlar fermasiga hujum qilib, uning qurilishi Frederikda qattiq hasad uyg'otgan shamol tegirmonini buzishni rejalashtirayotgani haqida yangi mish-mishlar tarqaldi. Snoubol hali ham Pinchfild fermasida yashirinib yurgani ma'lum edi. Yoz o'rtasida hayvonlar uchta tovuq o'zi kelib, Snoubolning ilhomi bilan Napoleonni o'ldirish fitnasiga kirishganliklarini tan olganini eshitib, xavotirga tushishdi. Ular darhol qatl etildi va Napoleonning xavfsizligi uchun yangi choralar ko'rildi. Kechalari uning karavotini to'rtta it — har bir burchakda bittadan — qo'riqlardi, Pinkay ismli yosh cho'chqaga esa zaharlanmasligi uchun uning barcha ovqatini u yeyishidan oldin tatib ko'rish vazifasi topshirildi.

paras.en: At about the same time it was given out that Napoleon had arranged to sell the pile of timber to Mr Pilkington; he was also going to enter into a regular agreement for the exchange of certain products between Animal Farm and Foxwood. The relations between Napoleon and Pilkington, though they were only conducted through Whymper, were now almost friendly. The animals distrusted Pilkington, as a human being, but greatly preferred him to Frederick, whom they both feared and hated. As the summer wore on, and the windmill neared completion, the rumours of an impending treacherous attack grew stronger and stronger. Frederick, it was said, intended to bring against them twenty men all armed with guns, and he had already bribed the magistrates and police, so that if he could once get hold of the title-deeds of Animal Farm they would ask no questions.
paras.uz: Taxminan shu vaqtda Napoleon yog'och g'aramini janob Pilkingtonga sotishga kelishgani e'lon qilindi; u yana Hayvonlar fermasi va Foksvud o'rtasida ba'zi mahsulotlarni ayirboshlash bo'yicha muntazam kelishuvga kirishmoqchi edi. Napoleon va Pilkington o'rtasidagi munosabatlar, faqat Uimper orqali olib borilsa ham, endi deyarli do'stona edi. Hayvonlar Pilkingtonga inson sifatida ishonishmasdi, lekin uni ham qo'rqadigan, ham nafratlanadigan Frederikdan ancha afzal ko'rishardi. Yoz o'tib, shamol tegirmoni tugashga yaqinlashgani sari, yaqinlashib kelayotgan xoinona hujum haqidagi mish-mishlar tobora kuchaydi. Aytishlaricha, Frederik ularga qarshi hammasi miltiq bilan qurollangan yigirma kishini olib kelmoqchi ekan va allaqachon sudyalar va politsiyaga pora berib qo'ygan ekan, shuning uchun agar u bir marta Hayvonlar fermasining mulk hujjatlarini qo'lga kiritsa, ular hech qanday savol berishmaydi.

paras.en: Moreover terrible stories were leaking out from Pinchfield about the cruelties that Frederick practised upon his animals. He had flogged an old horse to death, he starved his cows, he had killed a dog by throwing it into the furnace, he amused himself in the evenings by making cocks fight with splinters of razor-blade tied to their spurs. The animals’ blood boiled with rage when they heard of these things being done to their comrades, and sometimes they clamoured to be allowed to go out in a body and attack Pinchfield Farm, drive out the humans and set the animals free. But Squealer counselled them to avoid rash actions and trust in Comrade Napoleon's strategy.
paras.uz: Bundan tashqari, Pinchfilddan Frederikning hayvonlariga qiladigan shafqatsizliklari haqida dahshatli hikoyalar sizib chiqardi. U keksa otni qamchilab o'ldirgan, sigirlarini och qoldirar, bir itni o'choqqa tashlab o'ldirgan, kechqurunlari xo'rozlarning shporlariga ustara parchalarini bog'lab, ularni urishtirib ko'ngil ochar ekan. O'rtoqlariga nisbatan bunday ishlar qilinayotganini eshitib, hayvonlarning qoni g'azabdan qaynab ketardi va ba'zan ular to'da bo'lib chiqib, Pinchfild fermasiga hujum qilish, insonlarni haydab, hayvonlarni ozod qilishga ruxsat berishlarini talab qilib shovqin ko'tarishardi. Lekin Skviler ularga shoshqaloq harakatlardan saqlanishni va O'rtoq Napoleonning strategiyasiga ishonishni maslahat berdi.

paras.en: Nevertheless feeling against Frederick continued to run high. One Sunday morning Napoleon appeared in the barn and explained that he had never at any time contemplated selling the pile of timber to Frederick; he considered it beneath his dignity, he said, to have dealings with scoundrels of that description. The pigeons who were still sent out to spread tidings of the Rebellion were forbidden to set foot anywhere on Foxwood, and were also ordered to drop their former slogan of ‘Death to Humanity’ in favour of ‘Death to Frederick’. In the late summer yet another of Snowball's machinations was laid bare. The wheat crop was full of weeds, and it was discovered that on one of his nocturnal visits Snowball had mixed weed seeds with the seed corn.
paras.uz: Shunga qaramay, Frederikka qarshi kayfiyat kuchliligicha qoldi. Bir yakshanba ertalab Napoleon molxonada paydo bo'lib, yog'och g'aramini Frederikka sotishni hech qachon o'ylamaganini tushuntirdi; u bunday toifadagi ablahlar bilan ish qilishni o'z qadr-qimmatiga nomunosib deb bilishini aytdi. Hali ham Qo'zg'olon xabarlarini tarqatish uchun yuborilayotgan kaptarlarga Foksvudning biror joyiga qadam bosish taqiqlandi, shuningdek ularga avvalgi «Insoniyatga o'lim» shiorini «Frederikka o'lim» shiori bilan almashtirish buyurildi. Yozning oxirida Snoubolning yana bir hiylasi fosh bo'ldi. Bug'doy hosilini begona o't bosib ketgan edi va Snoubol tungi tashriflaridan birida urug'lik donga begona o't urug'larini aralashtirgani aniqlandi.

paras.en: A gander who had been privy to the plot had confessed his guilt to Squealer and immediately committed suicide by swallowing deadly nightshade berries. The animals now also learned that Snowball had never – as many of them had believed hitherto – received the order of ‘Animal Hero, First Class’. This was merely a legend which had been spread some time after the Battle of the Cowshed by Snowball himself. So far from being decorated he had been censured for showing cowardice in the battle. Once again some of the animals heard this with a certain bewilderment, but Squealer was soon able to convince them that their memories had been at fault.
paras.uz: Fitnadan xabardor bo'lgan bir erkak g'oz Skvilerga aybini tan olgan va darhol zaharli itumshuq mevalarini yutib, o'zini o'ldirgan ekan. Endi hayvonlar Snoubol hech qachon — ularning ko'pchiligi shu paytgacha ishonganidek — «Birinchi darajali Hayvon Qahramoni» ordenini olmaganini ham bilib olishdi. Bu shunchaki Molxona jangidan bir muncha vaqt o'tgach Snoubolning o'zi tarqatgan afsona ekan. U mukofotlanish u yoqda tursin, jangda qo'rqoqlik ko'rsatgani uchun qoralangan ekan. Yana bir bor ba'zi hayvonlar buni qandaydir hayrat bilan eshitishdi, lekin Skviler tez orada ularni xotiralari aldaganiga ishontira oldi.

paras.en: In the autumn, by a tremendous, exhausting effort – for the harvest had to be gathered at almost the same time – the windmill was finished. The machinery had still to be installed, and Whymper was negotiating the purchase of it, but the structure was completed. In the teeth of every difficulty, in spite of inexperience, of primitive implements, of bad luck and of Snowball's treachery, the work had been finished punctually to the very day! Tired out but proud, the animals walked round and round their masterpiece, which appeared even more beautiful in their eyes than when it had been built the first time. Moreover the walls were twice as thick as before. Nothing short of explosives would lay them low this time!
paras.uz: Kuzda ulkan, holdan toydiruvchi harakat bilan — chunki hosilni ham deyarli bir vaqtda yig'ib olish kerak edi — shamol tegirmoni tugallandi. Mashinalarni hali o'rnatish kerak edi va Uimper ularni sotib olish bo'yicha muzokara olib borardi, lekin bino tayyor edi. Har qanday qiyinchiliklarga, tajribasizlikka, ibtidoiy asboblarga, omadsizlikka va Snoubolning xoinligiga qaramay, ish aynan belgilangan kunga tugallandi! Charchagan, lekin g'ururlangan hayvonlar o'z durdonalari atrofida aylanib yurishdi, u ularning ko'ziga birinchi marta qurilgandagidan ham chiroyliroq ko'rinardi. Bundan tashqari, devorlar avvalgidan ikki baravar qalin edi. Bu safar uni portlovchi moddadan boshqa hech narsa qulata olmasdi!

paras.en: And when they thought of how they had laboured, what discouragements they had overcome, and the enormous difference that would be made in their lives when the sails were turning and the dynamos running – when they thought of all this their tiredness forsook them and they gambolled round and round the windmill, uttering cries of triumph. Napoleon himself, attended by his dogs and his cockerel, came down to inspect the completed work; he personally congratulated the animals on their achievement, and announced that the mill would be named Napoleon Mill.
paras.uz: Va ular qanchalik mehnat qilganlarini, qanday tushkunliklarni yengib o'tganlarini, qanotlar aylanib, dinamolar ishlay boshlaganda hayotlarida qanday ulkan farq bo'lishini o'ylaganlarida — bularning hammasini o'ylaganlarida charchoqlari tarqab ketdi va ular g'alaba hayqiriqlarini chiqarib, shamol tegirmoni atrofida aylanib o'ynashdi. Itlari va xo'rozi hamrohligida Napoleonning o'zi tugallangan ishni ko'zdan kechirish uchun tushib keldi; u shaxsan hayvonlarni yutuqlari bilan tabrikladi va tegirmon «Napoleon tegirmoni» deb nomlanishini e'lon qildi.

paras.en: Two days later the animals were called together for a special meeting in the barn. They were struck dumb with surprise when Napoleon announced that he had sold the pile of timber to Frederick. Tomorrow Frederick's wagons would arrive and begin carting it away. Throughout the whole period of his seeming friendship with Pilkington, Napoleon had really been in secret agreement with Frederick.
paras.uz: Ikki kundan keyin hayvonlar molxonadagi maxsus yig'ilishga chaqirildi. Napoleon yog'och g'aramini Frederikka sotganini e'lon qilganda, ular hayratdan tilsiz qolishdi. Ertaga Frederikning aravalari kelib, uni tashib keta boshlaydi. Pilkington bilan go'yo do'stlashib yurgan butun davr mobaynida Napoleon aslida Frederik bilan yashirin kelishuvda bo'lgan ekan.

paras.en: All relations with Foxwood had been broken off; insulting messages had been sent to Pilkington. The pigeons had been told to avoid Pinchfield Farm and to alter their slogan from ‘Death to Frederick’ to ‘Death to Pilkington’. At the same time Napoleon assured the animals that the stories of an impending attack on Animal Farm were completely untrue, and that the tales about Frederick's cruelty to his own animals had been greatly exaggerated. All these rumours had probably originated with Snowball and his agents. It now appeared that Snowball was not, after all, hiding on Pinchfield Farm, and in fact had never been there in his life: he was living – in considerable luxury, so it was said – at Foxwood, and had in reality been a pensioner of Pilkington for years past.
paras.uz: Foksvud bilan barcha aloqalar uzildi; Pilkingtonga haqoratli xabarlar yuborildi. Kaptarlarga Pinchfild fermasidan uzoq yurish va shiorlarini «Frederikka o'lim»dan «Pilkingtonga o'lim»ga o'zgartirish aytildi. Ayni paytda Napoleon hayvonlarni Hayvonlar fermasiga yaqinlashib kelayotgan hujum haqidagi hikoyalar mutlaqo yolg'on ekaniga, Frederikning o'z hayvonlariga shafqatsizligi haqidagi gaplar esa juda bo'rttirilganiga ishontirdi. Bu mish-mishlarning hammasi, ehtimol, Snoubol va uning agentlaridan chiqqan. Endi ma'lum bo'lishicha, Snoubol, axir, Pinchfild fermasida yashirinmagan ekan, aslida u yerda umrida bo'lmagan ekan: u Foksvudda — aytishlaricha, ancha hashamatda — yashar va aslida ko'p yillardan beri Pilkingtonning nafaqaxo'ri ekan.

paras.en: The pigs were in ecstasies over Napoleon's cunning. By seeming to be friendly with Pilkington he had forced Frederick to raise his price by twelve pounds. But the superior quality of Napoleon's mind, said Squealer, was shown in the fact that he trusted nobody, not even Frederick. Frederick had wanted to pay for the timber with something called a cheque, which it seemed was a piece of paper with a promise to pay written upon it. But Napoleon was too clever for him. He had demanded payment in real five-pound notes, which were to be handed over before the timber was removed. Already Frederick had paid up; and the sum he had paid was just enough to buy the machinery for the windmill.
paras.uz: Cho'chqalar Napoleonning ayyorligidan vajdga tushishdi. Pilkington bilan do'stlashgandek ko'rinib, u Frederikni narxni o'n ikki funtga oshirishga majbur qilgan edi. Lekin Napoleon aqlining ustunligi, dedi Skviler, u hech kimga, hatto Frederikka ham ishonmaganida namoyon bo'ldi. Frederik yog'och uchun chek deb ataladigan narsa bilan to'lamoqchi bo'lgan ekan, bu esa, aftidan, ustiga to'lash va'dasi yozilgan bir parcha qog'oz ekan. Lekin Napoleon undan aqlliroq chiqdi. U yog'och olib ketilishidan oldin topshirilishi kerak bo'lgan haqiqiy besh funtlik banknotlar bilan to'lashni talab qilgan edi. Frederik allaqachon to'lab bo'lgan edi; va u to'lagan summa shamol tegirmoni uchun mashinalar sotib olishga aynan yetarli edi.

paras.en: Meanwhile the timber was being carted away at high speed. When it was all gone another special meeting was held in the barn for the animals to inspect Frederick's bank-notes. Smiling beatifically, and wearing both his decorations, Napoleon reposed on a bed of straw on the platform, with the money at his side, neatly piled on a china dish from the farmhouse kitchen. The animals filed slowly past, and each gazed his fill. And Boxer put out his nose to sniff at the bank-notes, and the flimsy white things stirred and rustled in his breath.
paras.uz: Bu orada yog'och katta tezlikda tashib ketilardi. Hammasi olib ketilgach, hayvonlar Frederikning banknotlarini ko'zdan kechirishlari uchun molxonada yana bir maxsus yig'ilish o'tkazildi. Saodat bilan jilmayib, ikkala nishonini taqqan Napoleon supadagi somon to'shakda yonboshlab yotar, yonida pul ferma uyi oshxonasidan olingan chinni likopchada tekis taxlab qo'yilgan edi. Hayvonlar sekin bir qatorda o'tishdi va har biri to'yguncha tomosha qildi. Bokser ham banknotlarni hidlash uchun burnini cho'zdi va o'sha yupqa oq narsalar uning nafasidan qimirlab, shitirlashdi.

paras.en: Three days later there was a terrible hullabaloo. Whymper, his face deadly pale, came racing up the path on his bicycle, flung it down in the yard and rushed straight into the farmhouse. The next moment a choking roar of rage sounded from Napoleon's apartments. The news of what had happened sped round the farm like wildfire. The bank-notes were forgeries! Frederick had got the timber for nothing!
paras.uz: Uch kundan keyin dahshatli to'polon ko'tarildi. Yuzi o'likdek oqarib ketgan Uimper velosipedida yo'lakdan uchib keldi, uni hovliga tashladi va to'g'ri ferma uyiga otildi. Keyingi lahzada Napoleonning xonalaridan bo'g'iq g'azab o'kirig'i eshitildi. Nima bo'lgani haqidagi xabar ferma bo'ylab yong'indek tarqaldi. Banknotlar soxta ekan! Frederik yog'ochni tekinga olib ketibdi!

paras.en: Napoleon called the animals together immediately and in a terrible voice pronounced the death sentence upon Frederick. When captured, he said, Frederick should be boiled alive. At the same time he warned them that after this treacherous deed the worst was to be expected. Frederick and his men might make their long-expected attack at any moment. Sentinels were placed at all the approaches to the farm. In addition, four pigeons were sent to Foxwood with a conciliatory message, which it was hoped might re-establish good relations with Pilkington.
paras.uz: Napoleon darhol hayvonlarni yig'di va dahshatli ovozda Frederikka o'lim hukmini e'lon qildi. Qo'lga tushganda, dedi u, Frederik tiriklay qaynatilishi kerak. Ayni paytda u ularni bu xoinona qilmishdan keyin eng yomonini kutish kerakligi haqida ogohlantirdi. Frederik va uning odamlari uzoq kutilgan hujumni istalgan lahzada boshlashi mumkin edi. Fermaga olib boradigan barcha yo'llarga soqchilar qo'yildi. Bundan tashqari, Pilkington bilan yaxshi munosabatlarni tiklashi mumkin deb umid qilingan yarashtiruvchi xabar bilan Foksvudga to'rtta kaptar yuborildi.

paras.en: The very next morning the attack came. The animals were at breakfast when the look-outs came racing in with the news that Frederick and his followers had already come through the five-barred gate. Boldly enough the animals sallied forth to meet them, but this time they did not have the easy victory that they had had in the Battle of the Cowshed. There were fifteen men, with half a dozen guns between them, and they opened fire as soon as they got within fifty yards. The animals could not face the terrible explosions and the stinging pellets, and in spite of the efforts of Napoleon and Boxer to rally them they were soon driven back. A number of them were already wounded. They took refuge in the farm buildings and peeped cautiously out from chinks and knot-holes.
paras.uz: Aynan ertasi kuni ertalab hujum boshlandi. Hayvonlar nonushta qilayotganda, kuzatuvchilar Frederik va uning odamlari allaqachon besh to'sinli darvozadan o'tganligi haqidagi xabar bilan chopib kelishdi. Hayvonlar ularni kutib olish uchun ancha dadil chiqishdi, lekin bu safar ular Molxona jangidagi kabi oson g'alabaga erisha olmadilar. O'n besh kishi bo'lib, ularda yarim o'nlab miltiq bor edi va ular ellik yardga yaqinlashishlari bilanoq o't ochishdi. Hayvonlar dahshatli portlashlar va achishtiruvchi sochma o'qlarga bardosh bera olmadilar va Napoleon va Bokserning ularni qayta to'plash urinishlariga qaramay, tez orada ortga surildilar. Ulardan bir nechtasi allaqachon yaralangan edi. Ular ferma binolariga panoh topishdi va yoriqlar va tugun teshiklaridan ehtiyotkorlik bilan mo'ralashdi.

paras.en: The whole of the big pasture, including the windmill, was in the hands of the enemy. For the moment even Napoleon seemed at a loss. He paced up and down without a word, his tail rigid and twitching. Wistful glances were sent in the direction of Foxwood. If Pilkington and his men would help them, the day might yet be won. But at this moment the four pigeons who had been sent out on the day before returned, one of them bearing a scrap of paper from Pilkington. On it was pencilled the words: ‘Serves you right.’
paras.uz: Shamol tegirmonini ham qo'shib, butun katta yaylov dushman qo'lida edi. Hozircha hatto Napoleon ham nima qilishini bilmayotgandek edi. U dumi qotib, tipirchilab, indamay u yoqdan-bu yoqqa yurardi. Foksvud tomonga umid bilan nigohlar tashlandi. Agar Pilkington va uning odamlari yordam berishsa, kunni hali yutib olish mumkin edi. Lekin shu lahzada kecha yuborilgan to'rtta kaptar qaytib keldi, ulardan biri Pilkingtondan bir parcha qog'oz olib kelgan edi. Unda qalam bilan shunday so'zlar yozilgan edi: «Haqingiz shu.»

paras.en: Meanwhile Frederick and his men had halted about the windmill. The animals watched them, and a murmur of dismay went round. Two of the men had produced a crowbar and a sledge hammer. They were going to knock the windmill down.
paras.uz: Bu orada Frederik va uning odamlari shamol tegirmoni yonida to'xtashgan edi. Hayvonlar ularni kuzatishdi va vahimali shivir-shivir tarqaldi. Odamlardan ikkitasi lom va kuvalda chiqarishgan edi. Ular shamol tegirmonini qulatmoqchi edi.

paras.en: ‘Impossible!’ cried Napoleon. ‘We have built the walls far too thick for that. They could not knock it down in a week. Courage, comrades!’
paras.uz: «Mumkin emas! — deb qichqirdi Napoleon. — Biz devorlarni buning uchun juda qalin qurganmiz. Ular uni bir haftada ham qulata olmaydi. Dadil bo'linglar, o'rtoqlar!»

paras.en: But Benjamin was watching the movements of the men intently. The two with the hammer and the crowbar were drilling a hole near the base of the windmill. Slowly, and with an air almost of amusement, Benjamin nodded his long muzzle.
paras.uz: Lekin Benjamin odamlarning harakatlarini diqqat bilan kuzatib turardi. Kuvalda va lom ko'targan ikkovi shamol tegirmonining tagiga yaqin joyda teshik o'yishayotgan edi. Sekin va deyarli kulgili qiyofada Benjamin uzun tumshug'ini irg'adi.

paras.en: ‘I thought so,’ he said. ‘Do you not see what they are doing? In another moment they are going to pack blasting powder into that hole.’
paras.uz: «Shunday deb o'ylagandim, — dedi u. — Nima qilishayotganini ko'rmayapsizlarmi? Hozir ular o'sha teshikka portlovchi porox tiqishadi.»

paras.en: Terrified, the animals waited. It was impossible now to venture out of the shelter of the buildings. After a few minutes the men were seen to be running in all directions. Then there was a deafening roar. The pigeons swirled into the air, and all the animals, except Napoleon, flung themselves flat on their bellies and hid their faces. When they got up again a huge cloud of black smoke was hanging where the windmill had been. Slowly the breeze drifted it away. The windmill had ceased to exist!
paras.uz: Dahshatga tushgan hayvonlar kutishdi. Endi binolar panohidan tashqariga chiqishga jur'at etib bo'lmasdi. Bir necha daqiqadan keyin odamlar har tomonga chopib ketayotgani ko'rindi. Keyin quloqni kar qiluvchi gumburlash eshitildi. Kaptarlar havoga girdob bo'lib ko'tarildi va Napoleondan tashqari barcha hayvonlar o'zlarini qorinlari bilan yerga tashlab, yuzlarini yashirishdi. Ular yana turishganda, shamol tegirmoni turgan joyda ulkan qora tutun buluti osilib turardi. Shabada uni sekin uchirib ketdi. Shamol tegirmoni yo'q bo'lgan edi!

paras.en: At this sight the animals’ courage returned to them. The fear and despair they had felt a moment earlier were drowned in their rage against this vile, contemptible act. A mighty cry for vengeance went up, and without waiting for further orders they charged forth in a body and made straight for the enemy. This time they did not heed the cruel pellets that swept over them like hail. It was a savage, bitter battle. The men fired again and again, and, when the animals got to close quarters, lashed out with their sticks and their heavy boots. A cow, three sheep and two geese were killed, and nearly everyone was wounded. Even Napoleon, who was directing operations from the rear, had the tip of his tail chipped by a pellet. But the men did not go unscathed either.
paras.uz: Bu manzarani ko'rib, hayvonlarga jasorat qaytdi. Bir lahza oldin his qilgan qo'rquv va umidsizliklari bu razil, jirkanch qilmishga qarshi g'azablariga g'arq bo'ldi. Qasos haqidagi kuchli hayqiriq ko'tarildi va boshqa buyruqlarni kutmasdan ular to'da bo'lib otilib chiqib, to'g'ri dushmanga tashlanishdi. Bu safar ular ustlaridan do'ldek yog'ilayotgan shafqatsiz sochma o'qlarga e'tibor berishmadi. Bu yovuz, achchiq jang edi. Odamlar qayta-qayta o'q uzishdi, hayvonlar yaqin kelganda esa tayoqlari va og'ir etiklari bilan urishdi. Bir sigir, uchta qo'y va ikkita g'oz o'ldirildi, deyarli hamma yaralandi. Hatto orqadan harakatlarni boshqarayotgan Napoleonning ham dumining uchini sochma o'q uzib ketdi. Lekin odamlar ham sog'-salomat qolmadi.

paras.en: Three of them had their heads broken by blows from Boxer's hoofs, another was gored in the belly by a cow's horn, another had his trousers nearly torn off by Jessie and Bluebell. And when the nine dogs of Napoleon's own bodyguard, whom he had instructed to make a detour under cover of the hedge, suddenly appeared on the men's flank, baying ferociously, panic overtook them. They saw that they were in danger of being surrounded. Frederick shouted to his men to get out while the going was good, and the next moment the cowardly enemy was running for dear life. The animals chased them right down to the bottom of the field, and got in some last kicks at them as they forced their way through the thorn hedge.
paras.uz: Ulardan uchtasining boshi Bokserning tuyoq zarbalaridan yorildi, yana birining qorniga sigir shoxi sanchildi, yana birining shimini Jessi va Blyubell deyarli yirtib olishdi. Napoleon to'siq panasida aylanib o'tishni buyurgan o'z shaxsiy qo'riqchilari — to'qqizta it birdan odamlarning yonboshida vahshiyona vovullab paydo bo'lganda, ularni vahima bosdi. Ular qurshovda qolish xavfi borligini ko'rishdi. Frederik odamlariga vaqt borida qochishni qichqirdi va keyingi lahzada qo'rqoq dushman jon holatda qochib borardi. Hayvonlar ularni dalaning eng chetigacha quvib borishdi va ular tikanli to'siqdan yorib o'tayotganda oxirgi tepkilarini ham tushirishdi.

paras.en: They had won, but they were weary and bleeding. Slowly they began to limp back towards the farm. The sight of their dead comrades stretched upon the grass moved some of them to tears. And for a little while they halted in sorrowful silence at the place where the windmill had once stood. Yes, it was gone, almost the last trace of their labour was gone! Even the foundations were partially destroyed. And in rebuilding it they could not this time, as before, make use of the fallen stones. This time the stones had vanished too. The force of the explosion had flung them to distances of hundreds of yards. It was as though the windmill had never been.
paras.uz: Ular g'alaba qozonishdi, lekin charchagan va qonga belangan edi. Ular sekin oqsoqlanib fermaga qaytib kela boshlashdi. O't ustida cho'zilib yotgan o'lik o'rtoqlarini ko'rish ba'zilarini yig'latdi. Bir muddat ular shamol tegirmoni bir vaqtlar turgan joyda g'amgin sukunatda to'xtab qolishdi. Ha, u yo'q edi, mehnatlarining deyarli so'nggi izi ham yo'q bo'lgan edi! Hatto poydevori ham qisman vayron qilingan edi. Uni qayta qurishda bu safar avvalgidek qulagan toshlardan foydalana olishmasdi. Bu safar toshlar ham g'oyib bo'lgan edi. Portlash kuchi ularni yuzlab yard masofaga uloqtirib yuborgan edi. Go'yo shamol tegirmoni hech qachon bo'lmagandek edi.

paras.en: As they approached the farm Squealer, who had unaccountably been absent during the fighting, came skipping towards them, whisking his tail and beaming with satisfaction. And the animals heard, from the direction of the farm buildings, the solemn booming of a gun.
paras.uz: Ular fermaga yaqinlashganda, jang paytida tushunarsiz tarzda yo'q bo'lib qolgan Skviler dumini silkitib, mamnuniyatdan yashnab, sakrab-sakrab ular tomon keldi. Va hayvonlar ferma binolari tomonidan miltiqning tantanali gumburlashini eshitishdi.

paras.en: ‘What is that gun firing for?’ said Boxer.
paras.uz: «Miltiq nima uchun otilyapti?» — dedi Bokser.

paras.en: ‘To celebrate our victory!’ cried Squealer.
paras.uz: «G'alabamizni nishonlash uchun!» — deb qichqirdi Skviler.

paras.en: ‘What victory?’ said Boxer. His knees were bleeding, he had lost a shoe and split his hoof, and a dozen pellets had lodged themselves in his hind leg.
paras.uz: «Qanaqa g'alaba?» — dedi Bokser. Uning tizzalari qonardi, bir taqasini yo'qotib, tuyog'ini yorib olgan edi, orqa oyog'iga esa o'nlab sochma o'q qadalib qolgan edi.

paras.en: ‘What victory, comrade? Have we not driven the enemy off our soil – the sacred soil of Animal Farm?’
paras.uz: «Qanaqa g'alaba, o'rtoq? Dushmanni yerimizdan — Hayvonlar fermasining muqaddas yeridan — haydab chiqarmadikmi?»

paras.en: ‘But they have destroyed the windmill. And we had worked on it for two years!’
paras.uz: «Lekin ular shamol tegirmonini vayron qilishdi. Biz esa uning ustida ikki yil ishlagan edik!»

paras.en: ‘What matter? We will build another windmill. We will build six windmills if we feel like it. You do not appreciate, comrade, the mighty thing that we have done. The enemy was in occupation of this very ground that we stand upon. And now – thanks to the leadership of Comrade Napoleon – we have won every inch of it back again!’
paras.uz: «Nima qipti? Boshqa shamol tegirmoni quramiz. Xohlasak, oltita shamol tegirmoni quramiz. Biz qilgan ulug' ishni qadrlamayapsan, o'rtoq. Dushman biz turgan aynan shu yerni egallab olgan edi. Endi esa — O'rtoq Napoleonning rahbarligi tufayli — uning har bir qarichini qaytarib oldik!»

paras.en: ‘Then we have won back what we had before,’ said Boxer.
paras.uz: «Demak, ilgari bizda bo'lgan narsani qaytarib oldik», — dedi Bokser.

paras.en: ‘That is our victory,’ said Squealer.
paras.uz: «Bizning g'alabamiz shu», — dedi Skviler.

paras.en: They limped into the yard. The pellets under the skin of Boxer's leg smarted painfully. He saw ahead of him the heavy labour of rebuilding the windmill from the foundations, and already in imagination he braced himself for the task. But for the first time it occurred to him that he was eleven years old and that perhaps his great muscles were not quite what they had once been.
paras.uz: Ular oqsoqlanib hovliga kirishdi. Bokserning oyog'i terisi ostidagi sochma o'qlar og'riqli achishardi. U oldinda shamol tegirmonini poydevoridan qayta qurishdek og'ir mehnatni ko'rdi va allaqachon xayolan bu vazifaga o'zini tayyorladi. Lekin birinchi marta uning xayoliga o'zi o'n bir yoshda ekani va balki ulkan mushaklari avvalgidek emasligi keldi.

paras.en: But when the animals saw the green flag flying, and heard the gun firing again – seven times it was fired in all – and heard the speech that Napoleon made, congratulating them on their conduct, it did seem to them after all that they had won a great victory. The animals slain in the battle were given a solemn funeral. Boxer and Clover pulled the wagon which served as a hearse, and Napoleon himself walked at the head of the procession. Two whole days were given over to celebrations. There were songs, speeches and more firing of the gun, and a special gift of an apple was bestowed on every animal, with two ounces of corn for each bird and three biscuits for each dog. It was announced that the battle would be called the Battle of the Windmill, and that Napoleon had created a new decoration, the Order of the Green Banner, which he had conferred upon himself. In the general rejoicings the unfortunate affair of the bank-notes was forgotten.
paras.uz: Lekin hayvonlar hilpirab turgan yashil bayroqni ko'rib, miltiqning yana otilganini eshitib — u jami yetti marta otildi — va Napoleonning ularni xatti-harakatlari bilan tabriklagan nutqini eshitgach, ularga axir haqiqatan ham buyuk g'alaba qozonishgandek tuyuldi. Jangda halok bo'lgan hayvonlar tantanali dafn etildi. Bokser va Klover tobut aravasi vazifasini o'tagan aravani tortishdi, Napoleonning o'zi esa marosim boshida yurdi. Butun ikki kun bayramga bag'ishlandi. Qo'shiqlar, nutqlar va yana miltiq otishlar bo'ldi, har bir hayvonga maxsus sovg'a sifatida bittadan olma, har bir qushga ikki untsiya don va har bir itga uchtadan pechenye berildi. Jang Shamol tegirmoni jangi deb atalishi va Napoleon yangi mukofot — Yashil Bayroq ordenini ta'sis etib, uni o'ziga topshirgani e'lon qilindi. Umumiy shodlik ichida banknotlar bilan bog'liq baxtsiz voqea unutildi.

paras.en: It was a few days later than this that the pigs came upon a case of whisky in the cellars of the farmhouse. It had been overlooked at the time when the house was first occupied. That night there came from the farmhouse the sound of loud singing, in which, to everyone's surprise, the strains of ‘Beasts of England’ were mixed up. At about half-past nine Napoleon, wearing an old bowler hat of Mr Jones's, was distinctly seen to emerge from the back door, gallop rapidly round the yard and disappear indoors again. But in the morning a deep silence hung over the farmhouse. Not a pig appeared to be stirring. It was nearly nine o'clock when Squealer made his appearance, walking slowly and dejectedly, his eyes dull, his tail hanging limply behind him, and with every appearance of being seriously ill. He called the animals together and told them that he had a terrible piece of news to impart. Comrade Napoleon was dying!
paras.uz: Bundan bir necha kun o'tib cho'chqalar ferma uyining yerto'lasidan bir quti viski topib olishdi. Uy birinchi marta egallanganda u e'tibordan chetda qolgan ekan. O'sha kechasi ferma uyidan baland qo'shiq ovozi eshitildi, unga hammani hayratga solib, «Angliya hayvonlari» kuyi ham aralashib ketgan edi. Taxminan to'qqiz yarimda janob Jonsning eski kotelok shlyapasini kiygan Napoleon orqa eshikdan chiqib, hovli atrofida tez chopib aylanib, yana ichkariga g'oyib bo'lgani aniq ko'rindi. Lekin ertalab ferma uyi ustida chuqur sukunat osilib turardi. Birorta cho'chqa qimirlayotganga o'xshamasdi. Soat to'qqizga yaqin Skviler ko'rindi — u sekin va ma'yus yurar, ko'zlari xira, dumi orqasida shalvirab osilib turar va har tomonlama jiddiy kasal ko'rinardi. U hayvonlarni yig'ib, ularga dahshatli xabar yetkazishi kerakligini aytdi. O'rtoq Napoleon jon berayotgan ekan!

paras.en: A cry of lamentation went up. Straw was laid down outside the doors of the farmhouse, and the animals walked on tiptoe. With tears in their eyes they asked one another what they should do if their Leader were taken away from them. A rumour went round that Snowball had after all contrived to introduce poison into Napoleon's food. At eleven o'clock Squealer came out to make another announcement. As his last act upon earth, Comrade Napoleon had pronounced a solemn decree: the drinking of alcohol was to be punished by death.
paras.uz: Nola ko'tarildi. Ferma uyi eshiklari oldiga somon to'shaldi va hayvonlar oyoq uchida yurishdi. Ko'zlarida yosh bilan ular bir-biridan, agar Dohiylari ulardan olib ketilsa, nima qilishlarini so'rashdi. Snoubol baribir Napoleonning ovqatiga zahar solishga muvaffaq bo'libdi, degan mish-mish tarqaldi. Soat o'n birda Skviler yana bir e'lon qilish uchun chiqdi. Yer yuzidagi so'nggi ishi sifatida O'rtoq Napoleon tantanali farmon chiqargan ekan: spirtli ichimlik ichish o'lim bilan jazolanadi.

paras.en: By the evening, however, Napoleon appeared to be somewhat better, and the following morning Squealer was able to tell them that he was well on the way to recovery. By the evening of that day Napoleon was back at work, and on the next day it was learned that he had instructed Whymper to purchase in Willingdon some booklets on brewing and distilling. A week later Napoleon gave orders that the small paddock beyond the orchard, which it had previously been intended to set aside as a grazing-ground for animals who were past work, was to be ploughed up. It was given out that the pasture was exhausted and needed re-seeding: but it soon became known that Napoleon intended to sow it with barley.
paras.uz: Biroq kechga yaqin Napoleon biroz yaxshilanganday bo'ldi va ertasi kuni ertalab Skviler ularga u tuzalish yo'lida ekanini ayta oldi. O'sha kuni kechqurun Napoleon yana ishga qaytdi, keyingi kuni esa u Uimperga Uillingdondan pivo pishirish va spirt haydash haqida bir nechta risola sotib olishni buyurgani ma'lum bo'ldi. Bir haftadan keyin Napoleon ilgari ishlashdan qolgan hayvonlar uchun yaylov sifatida ajratib qo'yish mo'ljallangan bog' ortidagi kichik o'tloqni haydashni buyurdi. Yaylov tugab qolgan va qayta ekishga muhtoj, deb e'lon qilindi: lekin tez orada Napoleon unga arpa ekmoqchi ekani ma'lum bo'ldi.

paras.en: About this time there occurred a strange incident which hardly anyone was able to understand. One night at about twelve o'clock there was a loud crash in the yard, and the animals rushed out of their stalls. It was a moonlit night.
