At the foot of the end wall of the big barn, where the Seven Commandments were written, there lay a ladder broken in two pieces. Squealer, temporarily stunned, was sprawling beside it, and near at hand there lay a lantern, a paintbrush and an overturned pot of white paint. The dogs immediately made a ring round Squealer, and escorted him back to the farmhouse as soon as he was able to walk. None of the animals could form any idea as to what this meant, except old Benjamin, who nodded his muzzle with a knowing air, and seemed to understand, but would say nothing.
paras.uz: Taxminan shu vaqtda deyarli hech kim tushuna olmagan g'alati voqea yuz berdi. Bir kechasi soat o'n ikkilarda hovlida qattiq gursillagan ovoz eshitildi va hayvonlar qo'ralaridan otilib chiqishdi. Oydin kecha edi. Yetti Amr yozilgan katta molxonaning yon devori tagida ikkiga bo'lingan narvon yotardi. Uning yonida vaqtincha hushidan ketgan Skviler cho'zilib yotar, yaqinida fonus, bo'yoq cho'tkasi va ag'darilgan oq bo'yoq idishi yotardi. Itlar darhol Skviler atrofida halqa hosil qilishdi va u yura olishi bilanoq uni ferma uyiga kuzatib borishdi. Hayvonlarning hech biri bu nimani anglatishini tasavvur qila olmadi, faqat keksa Benjamin bilag'onlik bilan tumshug'ini irg'adi va tushungandek bo'ldi, lekin hech narsa demadi.

paras.en: But a few days later Muriel, reading over the Seven Commandments to herself, noticed that there was yet another of them which the animals had remembered wrong. They had thought that the Fifth Commandment was ‘No animal shall drink alcohol’, but there were two words that they had forgotten. Actually the Commandment read: ‘No animal shall drink alcohol to excess.’
paras.uz: Lekin bir necha kundan keyin Muriel Yetti Amrni o'zicha qayta o'qib chiqib, hayvonlar noto'g'ri eslab qolgan yana bir amr borligini payqadi. Ular Beshinchi Amr «Hech bir hayvon spirtli ichimlik ichmaydi» deb o'ylashgan edi, lekin ular unutgan ikki so'z bor ekan. Aslida Amrda shunday deyilgan edi: «Hech bir hayvon spirtli ichimlikni me'yoridan ortiq ichmaydi.»

gloss.ex: A few days later, when the terror caused by the executions had died down, some of the animals remembered – or thought they r…
…t had happened sped round the farm like wildfire. The bank-notes were forgeries! Frederick had got the timber for nothing!
…not see what they are doing? In another moment they are going to pack blasting powder into that hole.’
…sallied forth to meet them, but this time they did not have the easy victory that they had had in the Battle of the Cowshed. There were fifteen men, with half…
…ten. Actually the Commandment read: ‘No animal shall drink alcohol to excess.’

quiz.q: What was wrong with Frederick's bank-notes?
What do the pigs add to the Fifth Commandment?
quiz.why_uz: «Hech bir hayvon spirtli ichimlikni me'yoridan ortiq ichmaydi».

chapters.recap_uz: «Hech bir hayvon boshqa hayvonni sababsiz o'ldirmaydi». Napoleon dohiyga aylanadi. U yog'ochni Frederikka sotadi — pul soxta chiqadi. Frederik hujum qilib, tegirmonni portlatadi; hayvonlar g'alaba qiladi, lekin qanchalik qimmatga! Cho'chqalar viski topadi va beshinchi Amr ham o'zgaradi.

chapters.title: Boxer's last journey

paras.en: Boxer's split hoof was a long time in healing. They had started the rebuilding of the windmill the day after the victory celebrations were ended. Boxer refused to take even a day off work, and made it a point of honour not to let it be seen that he was in pain. In the evenings he would admit privately to Clover that the hoof troubled him a great deal. Clover treated the hoof with poultices of herbs which she prepared by chewing them, and both she and Benjamin urged Boxer to work less hard. ‘A horse's lungs do not last for ever,’ she said to him. But Boxer would not listen. He had, he said, only one real ambition left – to see the windmill well under way before he reached the age for retirement.
paras.uz: Bokserning yorilgan tuyog'i uzoq bitmadi. G'alaba bayramlari tugaganining ertasi kuniyoq ular shamol tegirmonini qayta qurishni boshlashgan edi. Bokser hatto bir kun ham dam olishdan bosh tortdi va og'riq chekayotganini bildirmaslikni sharaf ishi qilib oldi. Kechqurunlari u Kloverga xufyona tuyog'i uni juda qiynayotganini tan olardi. Klover tuyoqni chaynab tayyorlagan o'tlardan qilingan malham bilan davoladi, u ham, Benjamin ham Bokserni kamroq ishlashga undashdi. «Otning o'pkasi abadiy chidamaydi», — dedi u unga. Lekin Bokser quloq solmadi. Uning aytishicha, unda faqat bitta haqiqiy orzu qolgan edi — nafaqa yoshiga yetishidan oldin shamol tegirmoni qurilishi yaxshi yo'lga tushganini ko'rish.

paras.en: At the beginning, when the laws of Animal Farm were first formulated, the retiring age had been fixed for horses and pigs at twelve, for cows at fourteen, for dogs at nine, for sheep at seven and for hens and geese at five. Liberal old-age pensions had been agreed upon. As yet no animal had actually retired on pension, but of late the subject had been discussed more and more. Now that the small field beyond the orchard had been set aside for barley, it was rumoured that a corner of the large pasture was to be fenced off and turned into a grazing-ground for superannuated animals. For a horse, it was said, the pension would be five pounds of corn a day and, in winter, fifteen pounds of hay, with a carrot or possibly an apple on public holidays. Boxer's twelfth birthday was due in the late summer of the following year.
paras.uz: Boshida, Hayvonlar fermasining qonunlari birinchi marta ishlab chiqilganda, nafaqa yoshi otlar va cho'chqalar uchun o'n ikki, sigirlar uchun o'n to'rt, itlar uchun to'qqiz, qo'ylar uchun yetti, tovuqlar va g'ozlar uchun besh yosh qilib belgilangan edi. Saxovatli qarilik nafaqalari kelishib olingan edi. Hozircha biror hayvon haqiqatan ham nafaqaga chiqmagan edi, lekin oxirgi paytlarda bu masala tobora ko'proq muhokama qilinardi. Endi bog' ortidagi kichik dala arpa uchun ajratilgach, katta yaylovning bir burchagi to'siq bilan o'ralib, keksa hayvonlar uchun yaylovga aylantirilarkan, degan mish-mish yurardi. Aytishlaricha, ot uchun nafaqa kuniga besh funt don, qishda esa o'n besh funt pichan bo'lib, bayram kunlari sabzi yoki ehtimol olma ham beriladi. Bokserning o'n ikki yoshga to'lishi keyingi yilning yoz oxiriga to'g'ri kelardi.

paras.en: Meanwhile life was hard. The winter was as cold as the last one had been, and food was even shorter. Once again all rations were reduced except those of the pigs and the dogs. A too-rigid equality in rations, Squealer explained, would have been contrary to the principles of Animalism. In any case he had no difficulty in proving to the other animals that they were not in reality short of food, whatever the appearances might be. For the time being, certainly, it had been found necessary to make a readjustment of rations (Squealer always spoke of it as a ‘readjustment’, never as a ‘reduction’), but in comparison with the days of Jones the improvement was enormous.
paras.uz: Bu orada hayot og'ir edi. Qish o'tgan qishdek sovuq bo'ldi, ovqat esa yana ham kam edi. Yana bir bor cho'chqalar va itlarnikidan tashqari barcha ulushlar kamaytirildi. Ulushlarda haddan tashqari qattiq tenglik, deb tushuntirdi Skviler, Hayvonizm tamoyillariga zid bo'lardi. Har holda u boshqa hayvonlarga, ko'rinish qanday bo'lmasin, aslida ovqat yetishmasligi yo'qligini isbotlashda hech qiynalmadi. Hozircha, albatta, ulushlarni qayta moslashtirish zarur bo'lgan edi (Skviler doim bu haqda «kamaytirish» emas, «qayta moslashtirish» deb gapirardi), lekin Jons davri bilan solishtirganda yaxshilanish ulkan edi.

paras.en: Reading out the figures in a shrill rapid voice, he proved to them in detail that they had more oats, more hay, more turnips than they had had in Jones's day, that they worked shorter hours, that their drinking water was of better quality, that they lived longer, that a larger proportion of their young ones survived infancy, and that they had more straw in their stalls and suffered less from fleas. The animals believed every word of it. Truth to tell, Jones and all he stood for had almost faded out of their memories. They knew that life nowadays was harsh and bare, that they were often hungry and often cold, and that they were usually working when they were not asleep. But doubtless it had been worse in the old days. They were glad to believe so. Besides, in those days they had been slaves and now they were free, and that made all the difference, as Squealer did not fail to point out.
paras.uz: Raqamlarni chiyildoq, tez ovozda o'qib berib, u ularga Jons davridagidan ko'proq suli, ko'proq pichan, ko'proq sholg'om borligini, kamroq soat ishlashlarini, ichimlik suvlari sifatliroq ekanini, uzoqroq yashashlarini, bolalarining kattaroq qismi go'daklikdan omon qolishini, qo'ralarida ko'proq somon borligini va burgalardan kamroq azob chekishlarini batafsil isbotlab berdi. Hayvonlar uning har bir so'ziga ishonishdi. Rostini aytganda, Jons va u ifodalagan hamma narsa ularning xotirasidan deyarli o'chib ketgan edi. Ular hozirgi hayot og'ir va qashshoq ekanini, ko'pincha och va ko'pincha sovuqda qolishlarini, uxlamagan paytlarida odatda ishlashlarini bilishardi. Lekin, shubhasiz, eski kunlarda bundan yomonroq bo'lgan. Ular shunga ishonishdan xursand edi. Bundan tashqari, o'sha kunlarda ular qul edi, endi esa ozod edi, va Skviler ta'kidlashni unutmaganidek, butun farq shunda edi.

paras.en: There were many more mouths to feed now. In the autumn the four sows had all littered about simultaneously, producing thirty-one young pigs between them. The young pigs were piebald, and as Napoleon was the only boar on the farm it was possible to guess at their parentage. It was announced that later, when bricks and timber had been purchased, a schoolroom would be built in the farmhouse garden. For the time being the young pigs were given their instruction by Napoleon himself in the farmhouse kitchen. They took their exercise in the garden, and were discouraged from playing with the other young animals. About this time, too, it was laid down as a rule that when a pig and any other animal met on the path, the other animal must stand aside: and also that all pigs, of whatever degree, were to have the privilege of wearing green ribbons on their tails on Sundays.
paras.uz: Endi boqiladigan og'izlar ancha ko'p edi. Kuzda to'rtta ona cho'chqaning hammasi deyarli bir vaqtda tug'ib, jami o'ttiz bitta cho'chqacha dunyoga keltirishdi. Cho'chqachalar ola-bula edi va Napoleon fermadagi yagona erkak cho'chqa bo'lgani uchun ularning otasi kimligini taxmin qilish mumkin edi. Keyinroq g'isht va yog'och sotib olingach, ferma uyi bog'ida maktab xonasi qurilishi e'lon qilindi. Hozircha cho'chqachalarga ferma uyi oshxonasida Napoleonning o'zi saboq berardi. Ular bog'da mashq qilishar va boshqa yosh hayvonlar bilan o'ynashga undalmasdi. Taxminan shu vaqtda yana bir qoida o'rnatildi: so'qmoqda cho'chqa va boshqa biror hayvon uchrashib qolsa, boshqa hayvon chetga chiqishi kerak; shuningdek, darajasidan qat'i nazar barcha cho'chqalar yakshanba kunlari dumlariga yashil lenta taqish imtiyoziga ega bo'lishi kerak.

paras.en: The farm had had a fairly successful year, but was still short of money. There were the bricks, sand and lime for the schoolroom to be purchased, and it would also be necessary to begin saving up again for the machinery for the windmill. Then there were lamp oil and candles for the house, sugar for Napoleon's own table (he forbade this to the other pigs, on the ground that it made them fat), and all the usual replacements such as tools, nails, string, coal, wire, scrap-iron and dog biscuits.
paras.uz: Ferma ancha muvaffaqiyatli yil o'tkazgan edi, lekin hali ham pul yetishmasdi. Maktab xonasi uchun g'isht, qum va ohak sotib olish kerak edi, shuningdek shamol tegirmoni mashinalari uchun yana jamg'arishni boshlash zarur edi. Keyin uy uchun chiroq moyi va shamlar, Napoleonning o'z dasturxoni uchun qand (u boshqa cho'chqalarga semirtiradi, degan bahona bilan buni taqiqlagan edi) va asboblar, mixlar, ip, ko'mir, sim, temir-tersak va it pechenyesi kabi barcha odatiy almashtiriladigan narsalar bor edi.

paras.en: A stack of hay and part of the potato crop were sold off, and the contract for eggs was increased to six hundred a week, so that that year the hens barely hatched enough chicks to keep their numbers at the same level. Rations, reduced in December, were reduced again in February, and lanterns in the stalls were forbidden to save oil. But the pigs seemed comfortable enough, and in fact were putting on weight if anything. One afternoon in late February a warm, rich, appetising scent, such as the animals had never smelt before, wafted itself across the yard from the little brew-house, which had been disused in Jones's time, and which stood beyond the kitchen. Someone said it was the smell of cooking barley. The animals sniffed the air hungrily and wondered whether a warm mash was being prepared for their supper.
paras.uz: Bir g'aram pichan va kartoshka hosilining bir qismi sotib yuborildi, tuxum shartnomasi esa haftasiga olti yuztagacha oshirildi, shuning uchun o'sha yili tovuqlar sonini bir xil darajada saqlash uchun zo'rg'a yetarli jo'ja ochirishdi. Dekabrda kamaytirilgan ulushlar fevralda yana kamaytirildi va moyni tejash uchun qo'ralarda fonuslar taqiqlandi. Lekin cho'chqalar ancha bemalol ko'rinardi va aslida, aksincha, semirib borardi. Fevral oxirida bir kuni tushdan keyin oshxona ortida turgan, Jons davrida ishlatilmagan kichik pivoxonadan hovli bo'ylab hayvonlar ilgari hech qachon hidlamagan iliq, to'yimli, ishtahani ochuvchi hid tarqaldi. Kimdir bu pishirilayotgan arpa hidi ekanini aytdi. Hayvonlar havoni ochko'zlik bilan hidlashib, kechki ovqatlari uchun iliq yem tayyorlanayotgan bo'lsa kerak, deb o'ylashdi.

paras.en: But no warm mash appeared, and on the following Sunday it was announced that from now onwards all barley would be reserved for the pigs. The field beyond the orchard had already been sown with barley. And the news soon leaked out that every pig was now receiving a ration of a pint of beer daily, with half a gallon for Napoleon himself, which was always served to him in the Crown Derby soup tureen.
paras.uz: Lekin hech qanday iliq yem paydo bo'lmadi va keyingi yakshanbada bundan buyon barcha arpa cho'chqalar uchun ajratib qo'yilishi e'lon qilindi. Bog' ortidagi dalaga allaqachon arpa ekilgan edi. Tez orada har bir cho'chqa endi har kuni bir pint pivo, Napoleonning o'zi esa yarim gallon olayotgani haqidagi xabar sizib chiqdi, unga pivo doim «Kroun Derbi» sho'rva idishida tortilardi.

paras.en: But if there were hardships to be borne, they were partly offset by the fact that life nowadays had a greater dignity than it had had before. There were more songs, more speeches, more processions. Napoleon had commanded that once a week there should be held something called a Spontaneous Demonstration, the object of which was to celebrate the struggles and triumphs of Animal Farm. At the appointed time the animals would leave their work and march round the precincts of the farm in military formation, with the pigs leading, then the horses, then the cows, then the sheep, and then the poultry. The dogs flanked the procession and at the head of all marched Napoleon's black cockerel. Boxer and Clover always carried between them a green banner marked with the hoof and the horn and the caption, ‘Long live Comrade Napoleon!’
paras.uz: Lekin agar bardosh berish kerak bo'lgan qiyinchiliklar bo'lsa, ular qisman hozirgi hayotning avvalgisidan ko'ra ko'proq qadr-qimmatga ega ekani bilan qoplanardi. Qo'shiqlar ham, nutqlar ham, namoyishlar ham ko'proq edi. Napoleon haftada bir marta Hayvonlar fermasining kurashlari va g'alabalarini nishonlash maqsadida Stixiyali Namoyish deb ataladigan narsa o'tkazilishini buyurgan edi. Belgilangan vaqtda hayvonlar ishlarini tashlab, harbiy saf tortib ferma hududi bo'ylab yurishardi — oldinda cho'chqalar, keyin otlar, keyin sigirlar, keyin qo'ylar, keyin parrandalar. Itlar safning ikki chetidan borar, hammadan oldinda Napoleonning qora xo'rozi qadam tashlardi. Bokser va Klover doim o'rtalarida tuyoq va shox tasviri hamda «Yashasin O'rtoq Napoleon!» yozuvi tushirilgan yashil bayroqni ko'tarib borishardi.

paras.en: Afterwards there were recitations of poems composed in Napoleon's honour, and a speech by Squealer giving particulars of the latest increases in the production of foodstuffs, and on occasion a shot was fired from the gun. The sheep were the greatest devotees of the Spontaneous Demonstrations, and if anyone complained (as a few animals sometimes did, when no pigs or dogs were near) that they wasted time and meant a lot of standing about in the cold, the sheep were sure to silence him with a tremendous bleating of ‘Four legs good, two legs bad!’ But by and large the animals enjoyed these celebrations. They found it comforting to be reminded that, after all, they were truly their own masters and that the work they did was for their own benefit.
paras.uz: Keyin Napoleon sharafiga to'qilgan she'rlar o'qilar, Skviler oziq-ovqat ishlab chiqarishdagi so'nggi o'sishlar tafsilotlari bilan nutq so'zlar, ba'zan esa miltiqdan bir marta o'q uzilardi. Qo'ylar Stixiyali Namoyishlarning eng ashaddiy muxlislari edi, va agar kimdir (ba'zi hayvonlar yaqin atrofda cho'chqa yoki itlar bo'lmaganda ba'zan shikoyat qilishardi) ular vaqtni behuda o'tkazadi va sovuqda ko'p tik turishga to'g'ri keladi, deb shikoyat qilsa, qo'ylar albatta «To'rt oyoq — yaxshi, ikki oyoq — yomon!» degan dahshatli ma'rash bilan uni jim qildirishardi. Lekin umuman olganda hayvonlar bu bayramlardan zavqlanishardi. Ular axir haqiqatan ham o'z xo'jayinlari ekanliklari va qilayotgan ishlari o'z manfaatlari uchun ekani eslatilishidan taskin topishardi.

paras.en: So that what with the songs, the processions, Squealer's lists of figures, the thunder of the gun, the crowing of the cockerel and the fluttering of the flag, they were able to forget that their bellies were empty, at least part of the time.
paras.uz: Shunday qilib, qo'shiqlar, namoyishlar, Skvilerning raqamlar ro'yxatlari, miltiqning gumburlashi, xo'rozning qichqirig'i va bayroqning hilpirashi bilan ular hech bo'lmasa vaqtning bir qismida qorinlari bo'shligini unuta olishardi.

paras.en: In April Animal Farm was proclaimed a Republic, and it became necessary to elect a President. There was only one candidate, Napoleon, who was elected unanimously. On the same day it was given out that fresh documents had been discovered which revealed further details about Snowball's complicity with Jones. It now appeared that Snowball had not, as the animals had previously imagined, merely attempted to lose the Battle of the Cowshed by means of a stratagem, but had been openly fighting on Jones's side. In fact it was he who had actually been the leader of the human forces, and had charged into battle with the words ‘Long live Humanity!’ on his lips. The wounds on Snowball's back, which a few of the animals still remembered to have seen, had been inflicted by Napoleon's teeth.
paras.uz: Aprelda Hayvonlar fermasi Respublika deb e'lon qilindi va Prezident saylash zarurati tug'ildi. Faqat bitta nomzod bor edi — Napoleon, u bir ovozdan saylandi. O'sha kuni Snoubolning Jons bilan sheriklik qilgani haqida qo'shimcha tafsilotlarni ochib bergan yangi hujjatlar topilgani e'lon qilindi. Endi ma'lum bo'lishicha, Snoubol, hayvonlar ilgari tasavvur qilganidek, shunchaki hiyla yordamida Molxona jangini yutqazishga urinmagan, balki ochiqchasiga Jons tomonida jang qilgan ekan. Aslida insonlar qo'shiniga sarkardalik qilgan uning o'zi bo'lgan va lablarida «Yashasin Insoniyat!» degan so'zlar bilan jangga tashlangan ekan. Ba'zi hayvonlar hali ham ko'rganlarini eslaydigan Snoubolning orqasidagi yaralar Napoleonning tishlari bilan yetkazilgan ekan.

paras.en: In the middle of the summer Moses the raven suddenly reappeared on the farm, after an absence of several years. He was quite unchanged, still did no work, and talked in the same strain as ever about Sugarcandy Mountain. He would perch on a stump, flap his black wings, and talk by the hour to anyone who would listen. ‘Up there, comrades,’ he would say solemnly, pointing to the sky with his large beak – ‘up there, just on the other side of that dark cloud that you can see – there it lies, Sugarcandy Mountain, that happy country where we poor animals shall rest for ever from our labours!’ He even claimed to have been there on one of his higher flights, and to have seen the everlasting fields of clover and the linseed cake and lump sugar growing on the hedges. Many of the animals believed him.
paras.uz: Yoz o'rtasida qarg'a Mozes bir necha yillik yo'qlikdan keyin birdan fermada yana paydo bo'ldi. U butunlay o'zgarmagan edi, hali ham hech ish qilmas va hamon Qandtog' haqida avvalgidek gapirardi. U to'nkaga qo'nib, qora qanotlarini qoqib, tinglashga rozi bo'lgan har kim bilan soatlab gaplashardi. «Ana u yoqda, o'rtoqlar, — derdi u tantanali ravishda, katta tumshug'i bilan osmonni ko'rsatib, — ana u yoqda, ko'rib turganingiz o'sha qora bulutning naq narigi tomonida — u yerda Qandtog' joylashgan, biz bechora hayvonlar mehnatlarimizdan abadiy dam oladigan o'sha baxtli mamlakat!» U hatto balandroq parvozlaridan birida u yerda bo'lganini va abadiy beda dalalarini, to'siqlarda o'sayotgan zig'ir kunjarasi va bo'lak qandni ko'rganini da'vo qildi. Ko'p hayvonlar unga ishonishdi.

paras.en: Their lives now, they reasoned, were hungry and laborious; was it not right and just that a better world should exist somewhere else? A thing that was difficult to determine was the attitude of the pigs towards Moses. They all declared contemptuously that his stories about Sugarcandy Mountain were lies, and yet they allowed him to remain on the farm, not working, with an allowance of a gill of beer a day.
paras.uz: Hozirgi hayotlari, deb mulohaza qilishardi ular, och va mashaqqatli; boshqa biror joyda yaxshiroq dunyo bo'lishi to'g'ri va adolatli emasmi? Aniqlash qiyin bo'lgan narsa cho'chqalarning Mozesga munosabati edi. Ularning hammasi uning Qandtog' haqidagi hikoyalari yolg'on ekanini nafrat bilan e'lon qilishardi, shunga qaramay ishlamaydigan Mozesga fermada qolishga ruxsat berishar va kuniga bir gill pivo ulush berishardi.

paras.en: After his hoof had healed up Boxer worked harder than ever. Indeed all the animals worked like slaves that year. Apart from the regular work of the farm, and the rebuilding of the windmill, there was the schoolhouse for the young pigs, which was started in March. Sometimes the long hours on insufficient food were hard to bear, but Boxer never faltered. In nothing that he said or did was there any sign that his strength was not what it had been. It was only his appearance that was a little altered; his hide was less shiny than it had used to be, and his great haunches seemed to have shrunken. The others said, ‘Boxer will pick up when the spring grass comes on’; but the spring grass came and Boxer grew no fatter.
paras.uz: Tuyog'i bitgandan keyin Bokser har qachongidan ham ko'proq ishladi. Aslida o'sha yili barcha hayvonlar quldek ishlashdi. Fermaning odatiy ishlari va shamol tegirmonini qayta qurishdan tashqari, martda boshlangan cho'chqachalar uchun maktab binosi ham bor edi. Ba'zan yetarli bo'lmagan ovqat bilan uzoq soatlar ishlashga chidash qiyin edi, lekin Bokser hech qachon ikkilanmadi. Uning gapirgan yoki qilgan biror narsasida kuchi avvalgidek emasligining biror belgisi yo'q edi. Faqat tashqi ko'rinishi biroz o'zgargan edi; terisi avvalgidan kamroq yaltirardi, ulkan sag'rilari esa kichrayib qolgandek edi. Boshqalar «Bahorgi o't chiqqanda Bokser o'ziga keladi», deyishardi; lekin bahorgi o't chiqdi, Bokser esa semirmadi.

paras.en: Sometimes on the slope leading to the top of the quarry, when he braced his muscles against the weight of some vast boulder, it seemed that nothing kept him on his feet except the will to continue. At such times his lips were seen to form the words ‘I will work harder’; he had no voice left. Once again Clover and Benjamin warned him to take care of his health, but Boxer paid no attention. His twelfth birthday was approaching. He did not care what happened so long as a good store of stone was accumulated before he went on pension.
paras.uz: Ba'zan kon tepasiga olib chiqadigan qiyalikda, u qandaydir ulkan xarsang og'irligiga qarshi mushaklarini taranglaganda, uni oyoqda faqat davom etish irodasi ushlab turgandek tuyulardi. Bunday paytlarda uning lablari «Men yanada ko'proq ishlayman» so'zlarini shakllantirayotgani ko'rinardi; ovozi qolmagan edi. Yana bir bor Klover va Benjamin uni sog'lig'iga ehtiyot bo'lishga ogohlantirishdi, lekin Bokser e'tibor bermadi. Uning o'n ikki yoshga to'lishi yaqinlashib qolgan edi. Nafaqaga chiqishidan oldin yaxshigina tosh zaxirasi to'plansa bas, nima bo'lishi unga farqi yo'q edi.

paras.en: Late one evening, in the summer, a sudden rumour ran round the farm that something had happened to Boxer. He had gone out alone to drag a load of stone down to the windmill. And sure enough, the rumour was true. A few minutes later two pigeons came racing in with the news:
paras.uz: Yozda bir kuni kech oqshom ferma bo'ylab Bokserga nimadir bo'libdi, degan to'satdan mish-mish tarqaldi. U shamol tegirmoniga bir yuk tosh sudrab borish uchun yolg'iz chiqib ketgan edi. Darhaqiqat, mish-mish rost chiqdi. Bir necha daqiqadan keyin ikkita kaptar xabar bilan uchib keldi:

paras.en: ‘Boxer has fallen! He is lying on his side and can't get up!’
paras.uz: «Bokser yiqildi! U yonboshlab yotibdi va turolmayapti!»

paras.en: About half the animals on the farm rushed out to the knoll where the windmill stood. There lay Boxer, between the shafts of the cart, his neck stretched out, unable even to raise his head. His eyes were glazed, his sides matted with sweat. A thin stream of blood had trickled out of his mouth. Clover dropped to her knees at his side.
paras.uz: Fermadagi hayvonlarning taxminan yarmi shamol tegirmoni turgan tepalikka yugurib chiqishdi. U yerda arava tortqilari orasida Bokser bo'ynini cho'zgan holda, hatto boshini ham ko'tara olmay yotardi. Uning ko'zlari xiralashgan, biqinlari terdan namiqib ketgan edi. Og'zidan ingichka qon izi oqib chiqqan edi. Klover uning yonida tiz cho'kdi.

paras.en: ‘Boxer!’ she cried, ‘how are you?’
paras.uz: «Bokser! — deb qichqirdi u. — Ahvoling qanday?»

paras.en: ‘It is my lung,’ said Boxer in a weak voice. ‘It does not matter. I think you will be able to finish the windmill without me. There is a pretty good store of stone accumulated. I had only another month to go in any case. To tell you the truth I had been looking forward to my retirement. And perhaps, as Benjamin is growing old too, they will let him retire at the same time and be a companion to me.’
paras.uz: «O'pkam, — dedi Bokser zaif ovozda. — Ahamiyati yo'q. Menimcha, shamol tegirmonini mensiz ham tugata olasizlar. Ancha yaxshigina tosh zaxirasi to'plangan. Baribir menga yana bir oy qolgan edi. Rostini aytsam, nafaqaga chiqishimni intiqib kutayotgan edim. Balki Benjamin ham qarib qolgani uchun uni ham men bilan bir vaqtda nafaqaga chiqarishar va u menga hamroh bo'lar.»

paras.en: ‘We must get help at once,’ said Clover. ‘Run, somebody, and tell Squealer what has happened.’
paras.uz: «Darhol yordam olishimiz kerak, — dedi Klover. — Kimdir chopib borib, Skvilerga nima bo'lganini aytsin.»

paras.en: All the other animals immediately raced back to the farmhouse to give Squealer the news. Only Clover remained, and Benjamin, who lay down at Boxer's side, and, without speaking, kept the flies off him with his long tail. After about a quarter of an hour Squealer appeared, full of sympathy and concern. He said that Comrade Napoleon had learned with the very deepest distress of this misfortune to one of the most loyal workers on the farm, and was already making arrangements to send Boxer to be treated in the hospital at Willingdon. The animals felt a little uneasy at this. Except for Mollie and Snowball no other animal had ever left the farm, and they did not like to think of their sick comrade in the hands of human beings. However, Squealer easily convinced them that the veterinary surgeon in Willingdon could treat Boxer's case more satisfactorily than could be done on the farm. And about half an hour later, when Boxer had somewhat recovered, he was with difficulty got onto his feet, and managed to limp back to his stall, where Clover and Benjamin had prepared a good bed of straw for him.
paras.uz: Qolgan barcha hayvonlar darhol Skvilerga xabar berish uchun ferma uyiga yugurishdi. Faqat Klover va Bokserning yoniga yotib, indamay uzun dumi bilan undan pashshalarni haydab turgan Benjamin qolishdi. Chorak soatcha o'tgach, hamdardlik va tashvishga to'la Skviler paydo bo'ldi. U O'rtoq Napoleon fermadagi eng sodiq mehnatkashlardan birining boshiga tushgan bu baxtsizlikdan eng chuqur qayg'u bilan xabar topganini va allaqachon Bokserni Uillingdondagi kasalxonaga davolanishga jo'natish choralarini ko'rayotganini aytdi. Hayvonlar bundan biroz bezovtalanishdi. Molli va Snouboldan tashqari hech bir hayvon hech qachon fermani tark etmagan edi va ular kasal o'rtoqlarining insonlar qo'lida bo'lishini o'ylashni yoqtirishmadi. Biroq Skviler ularni Uillingdondagi veterinar Bokserni fermada qilish mumkin bo'lganidan ko'ra yaxshiroq davolay olishiga osongina ishontirdi. Taxminan yarim soatdan keyin, Bokser biroz o'ziga kelgach, uni qiyinchilik bilan oyoqqa turg'izishdi va u Klover va Benjamin unga yaxshi somon to'shak tayyorlab qo'ygan qo'rasiga oqsoqlanib qaytishga muvaffaq bo'ldi.

paras.en: For the next two days Boxer remained in his stall. The pigs had sent out a large bottle of pink medicine which they had found in the medicine chest in the bathroom, and Clover administered it to Boxer twice a day after meals. In the evenings she lay in his stall and talked to him, while Benjamin kept the flies off him. Boxer professed not to be sorry for what had happened. If he made a good recovery he might expect to live another three years, and he looked forward to the peaceful days that he would spend in the corner of the big pasture. It would be the first time that he had had leisure to study and improve his mind. He intended, he said, to devote the rest of his life to learning the remaining twenty-two letters of the alphabet.
paras.uz: Keyingi ikki kun Bokser qo'rasida qoldi. Cho'chqalar hammomdagi dori qutisidan topgan katta shisha pushti dorini yuborishgan edi va Klover uni Bokserga kuniga ikki marta ovqatdan keyin ichirdi. Kechqurunlari u uning qo'rasida yotib, u bilan gaplashar, Benjamin esa undan pashshalarni haydab turardi. Bokser bo'lgan voqeadan afsuslanmayotganini aytardi. Agar yaxshi tuzalsa, yana uch yil yashashini kutishi mumkin edi va u katta yaylovning burchagida o'tkazadigan osoyishta kunlarni intiqib kutardi. Bu uning birinchi marta o'qish va aqlini o'stirish uchun bo'sh vaqti bo'lishi edi. U qolgan umrini alifboning qolgan yigirma ikki harfini o'rganishga bag'ishlamoqchi ekanini aytdi.

paras.en: However, Benjamin and Clover could only be with Boxer after working hours, and it was in the middle of the day when the van came to take him away. The animals were all at work weeding turnips under the supervision of a pig, when they were astonished to see Benjamin come galloping from the direction of the farm buildings, braying at the top of his voice. It was the first time that they had ever seen Benjamin excited – indeed, it was the first time that anyone had ever seen him gallop. ‘Quick, quick!’ he shouted. ‘Come at once! They're taking Boxer away!’ Without waiting for orders from the pig, the animals broke off work and raced back to the farm buildings. Sure enough, there in the yard was a large closed van, drawn by two horses, with lettering on its side and a sly-looking man in a low-crowned bowler hat sitting on the driver's seat. And Boxer's stall was empty.
paras.uz: Biroq Benjamin va Klover Bokser bilan faqat ish vaqtidan keyin birga bo'la olishardi, furgon esa uni olib ketish uchun kunning o'rtasida keldi. Hayvonlar hammasi bir cho'chqa nazorati ostida sholg'om o'tayotgan edi, shunda ular Benjaminning butun ovozi bilan hangrab, ferma binolari tomondan chopib kelayotganini ko'rib hayratda qolishdi. Ular Benjaminni hayajonlangan holda birinchi marta ko'rishayotgan edi — aslida, uning chopganini ham hech kim birinchi marta ko'rayotgan edi. «Tez, tez! — deb qichqirdi u. — Darhol kelinglar! Ular Bokserni olib ketishyapti!» Cho'chqadan buyruq kutmasdan hayvonlar ishni tashlab, ferma binolariga yugurib qaytishdi. Darhaqiqat, hovlida ikki ot qo'shilgan, yon tomoniga yozuv tushirilgan katta yopiq furgon turardi, haydovchi o'rindig'ida esa past gardishli kotelok shlyapa kiygan ayyor ko'rinishli bir odam o'tirardi. Bokserning qo'rasi esa bo'sh edi.

paras.en: The animals crowded round the van. ‘Good-bye, Boxer!’ they chorused, ‘good-bye!’
paras.uz: Hayvonlar furgon atrofiga to'planishdi. «Xayr, Bokser! — deyishdi ular jo'r bo'lib. — Xayr!»

paras.en: ‘Fools! Fools!’ shouted Benjamin, prancing round them and stamping the earth with his small hoofs. ‘Fools! Do you not see what is written on the side of that van?’
paras.uz: «Ahmoqlar! Ahmoqlar! — deb qichqirdi Benjamin, ularning atrofida sakrab, kichkina tuyoqlari bilan yerni tepib. — Ahmoqlar! O'sha furgonning yoniga nima yozilganini ko'rmayapsizlarmi?»

paras.en: That gave the animals pause, and there was a hush. Muriel began to spell out the words. But Benjamin pushed her aside and in the midst of a deadly silence he read:
paras.uz: Bu hayvonlarni to'xtatib qo'ydi va jimlik cho'kdi. Muriel so'zlarni hijjalab o'qiy boshladi. Lekin Benjamin uni chetga itarib, o'lik sukunat ichida o'qidi:

paras.en: ‘“Alfred Simmonds, Horse Slaughterer and Glue Boiler, Willingdon. Dealer in Hides and Bone-Meal. Kennels Supplied.” Do you not understand what that means? They are taking Boxer to the knacker's!’
paras.uz: «Alfred Simmonds, Uillingdon. Ot so'yuvchi va yelim qaynatuvchi. Teri va suyak uni savdosi. Itxonalar ta'minlanadi.» Bu nimani anglatishini tushunmayapsizlarmi? Ular Bokserni o'lakso qassobiga olib ketishyapti!»

paras.en: A cry of horror burst from all the animals. At this moment the man on the box whipped up his horses and the van moved out of the yard at a smart trot. All the animals followed, crying out at the tops of their voices. Clover forced her way to the front. The van began to gather speed. Clover tried to stir her stout limbs to a gallop, and achieved a canter. ‘Boxer!’ she cried. ‘Boxer! Boxer! Boxer!’ And just at this moment, as though he had heard the uproar outside, Boxer's face, with the white stripe down his nose, appeared at the small window at the back of the van.
paras.uz: Barcha hayvonlardan dahshat faryodi otilib chiqdi. Shu lahzada o'rindiqdagi odam otlarini qamchiladi va furgon chaqqon yo'rtib hovlidan chiqib ketdi. Barcha hayvonlar baland ovozda qichqirgancha ortidan ergashishdi. Klover oldinga yorib o'tdi. Furgon tezlasha boshladi. Klover to'la oyoqlarini chopishga majburlashga urinib, yo'rg'alashga erishdi. «Bokser! — deb qichqirdi u. — Bokser! Bokser! Bokser!» Va aynan shu lahzada, go'yo tashqaridagi shovqinni eshitgandek, furgonning orqasidagi kichik derazada burni bo'ylab oq chiziq tushgan Bokserning yuzi paydo bo'ldi.

paras.en: ‘Boxer!’ cried Clover in a terrible voice. ‘Boxer! Get out! Get out quickly! They are taking you to your death!’
paras.uz: «Bokser! — deb qichqirdi Klover dahshatli ovozda. — Bokser! Chiq! Tezroq chiq! Ular seni o'limga olib ketishyapti!»

paras.en: All the animals took up the cry of ‘Get out, Boxer, get out!’ But the van was already gathering speed and drawing away from them. It was uncertain whether Boxer had understood what Clover had said. But a moment later his face disappeared from the window and there was the sound of a tremendous drumming of hoofs inside the van. He was trying to kick his way out. The time had been when a few kicks from Boxer's hoofs would have smashed the van to matchwood. But alas! his strength had left him; and in a few moments the sound of drumming hoofs grew fainter and died away. In desperation the animals began appealing to the two horses which drew the van to stop. ‘Comrades, comrades!’ they shouted. ‘Don't take your own brother to his death!’ But the stupid brutes, too ignorant to realise what was happening, merely set back their ears and quickened their pace. Boxer's face did not reappear at the window. Too late, someone thought of racing ahead and shutting the five-barred gate; but in another moment the van was through it and rapidly disappearing down the road. Boxer was never seen again.
paras.uz: Barcha hayvonlar «Chiq, Bokser, chiq!» degan hayqiriqni ilib ketishdi. Lekin furgon allaqachon tezlik olib, ulardan uzoqlashib borardi. Bokser Klover aytgan gapni tushundimi-yo'qmi, noma'lum edi. Lekin bir lahzadan keyin uning yuzi derazadan g'oyib bo'ldi va furgon ichidan dahshatli tuyoq dupurlashi eshitildi. U tepib, yorib chiqishga urinayotgan edi. Bir vaqtlar Bokser tuyoqlarining bir necha tepkisi furgonni chil-chil qilib yuborgan bo'lardi. Lekin afsus! kuchi uni tark etgan edi; va bir necha lahzadan keyin dupurlayotgan tuyoqlar ovozi zaiflashib, tinib qoldi. Umidsizlikda hayvonlar furgonni tortib borayotgan ikki otga to'xtashni so'rab yolvora boshlashdi. «O'rtoqlar, o'rtoqlar! — deb qichqirishdi ular. — O'z birodaringizni o'limga olib bormanglar!» Lekin nima bo'layotganini anglashga juda nodon bo'lgan ahmoq jonivorlar shunchaki quloqlarini qayirib, qadamlarini tezlatishdi. Bokserning yuzi derazada boshqa ko'rinmadi. Kimningdir xayoliga oldinga chopib, besh to'sinli darvozani yopish fikri juda kech keldi; keyingi lahzada furgon undan o'tib, yo'l bo'ylab tezda ko'zdan g'oyib bo'ldi. Bokserni boshqa hech kim ko'rmadi.

paras.en: Three days later it was announced that he had died in the hospital at Willingdon, in spite of receiving every attention a horse could have. Squealer came to announce the news to the others. He had, he said, been present during Boxer's last hours.
paras.uz: Uch kundan keyin u Uillingdondagi kasalxonada, otga ko'rsatilishi mumkin bo'lgan barcha g'amxo'rlikka qaramay, vafot etgani e'lon qilindi. Xabarni boshqalarga Skviler kelib aytdi. Uning aytishicha, u Bokserning so'nggi soatlarida yonida bo'lgan ekan.

paras.en: ‘It was the most affecting sight I have ever seen!’ said Squealer, lifting his trotter and wiping away a tear. ‘I was at his bedside at the very last. And at the end, almost too weak to speak, he whispered in my ear that his sole sorrow was to have passed on before the windmill was finished. “Forward, comrades!” he whispered. “Forward in the name of the Rebellion. Long live Animal Farm! Long live Comrade Napoleon! Napoleon is always right.” Those were his very last words, comrades.’
paras.uz: «Bu umrimda ko'rgan eng ta'sirli manzara edi! — dedi Skviler tuyog'ini ko'tarib, ko'z yoshini artib. — Men eng oxirgi lahzada uning boshida edim. Va oxirida, gapirishga deyarli holi qolmagan holda, u qulog'imga shivirlab, yagona qayg'usi shamol tegirmoni tugallanmasdan oldin dunyodan o'tib ketayotgani ekanini aytdi. «Oldinga, o'rtoqlar! — deb shivirladi u. — Qo'zg'olon nomi bilan oldinga. Yashasin Hayvonlar fermasi! Yashasin O'rtoq Napoleon! Napoleon har doim haq.» Bular uning eng so'nggi so'zlari edi, o'rtoqlar.»

paras.en: Here Squealer's demeanour suddenly changed. He fell silent for a moment, and his little eyes darted suspicious glances from side to side before he proceeded.
paras.uz: Shu yerda Skvilerning qiyofasi birdan o'zgardi. U bir lahza jim qoldi va davom etishdan oldin kichkina ko'zlari gumonli nigohlar bilan u yoqdan-bu yoqqa yugurdi.

paras.en: It had come to his knowledge, he said, that a foolish and wicked rumour had been circulated at the time of Boxer's removal. Some of the animals had noticed that the van which took Boxer away was marked ‘Horse Slaughterer’, and had actually jumped to the conclusion that Boxer was being sent to the knacker's. It was almost unbelievable, said Squealer, that any animal could be so stupid. Surely, he cried indignantly, whisking his tail and skipping from side to side, surely they knew their beloved Leader, Comrade Napoleon, better than that? But the explanation was really very simple. The van had previously been the property of the knacker, and had been bought by the veterinary surgeon, who had not yet painted the old name out. That was how the mistake had arisen.
paras.uz: Uning aytishicha, Bokser olib ketilgan paytda ahmoqona va yovuz mish-mish tarqatilganidan xabar topgan ekan. Ba'zi hayvonlar Bokserni olib ketgan furgonga «Ot so'yuvchi» deb yozilganini payqab, haqiqatan ham Bokserni o'lakso qassobiga jo'natishyapti, degan xulosaga shoshilishgan ekan. Biror hayvon shunchalik ahmoq bo'lishi deyarli aql bovar qilmas narsa, dedi Skviler. Axir, deb qichqirdi u g'azab bilan, dumini silkitib va u yoqdan-bu yoqqa sakrab, axir ular sevimli Dohiylari O'rtoq Napoleonni bundan yaxshiroq bilishadi-ku? Lekin izohi juda oddiy edi. Furgon ilgari o'lakso qassobining mulki bo'lgan va uni veterinar sotib olgan, u esa eski nomni hali bo'yab tashlamagan ekan. Xato shundan kelib chiqqan.

paras.en: The animals were enormously relieved to hear this. And when Squealer went on to give further graphic details of Boxer's death-bed, the admirable care he had received and the expensive medicines for which Napoleon had paid without a thought as to the cost, their last doubts disappeared and the sorrow that they felt for their comrade's death was tempered by the thought that at least he had died happy.
paras.uz: Hayvonlar buni eshitib, juda yengil tortishdi. Skviler Bokserning o'lim to'shagi, u ko'rgan ajoyib g'amxo'rlik va Napoleon narxini o'ylamay to'lagan qimmatbaho dorilar haqida yana jonli tafsilotlar bera boshlagach, ularning so'nggi shubhalari ham yo'qoldi va o'rtoqlarining o'limidan his qilgan qayg'ulari hech bo'lmasa u baxtli o'lgani haqidagi fikr bilan yengillashdi.

paras.en: Napoleon himself appeared at the meeting on the following Sunday morning and pronounced a short oration in Boxer's honour. It had not been possible, he said, to bring back their lamented comrade's remains for interment on the farm, but he had ordered a large wreath to be made from the laurels in the farmhouse garden and sent down to be placed on Boxer's grave. And in a few days’ time the pigs intended to hold a memorial banquet in Boxer's honour. Napoleon ended his speech with a reminder of Boxer's two favourite maxims, ‘I will work harder’ and ‘Comrade Napoleon is always right’ – maxims, he said, which every animal would do well to adopt as his own.
paras.uz: Keyingi yakshanba ertalab yig'ilishda Napoleonning o'zi paydo bo'lib, Bokser sharafiga qisqa nutq so'zladi. Marhum o'rtoqlarining jasadini fermaga dafn etish uchun qaytarib olib kelishning iloji bo'lmadi, dedi u, lekin u ferma uyi bog'idagi dafnalardan katta gulchambar yasab, Bokserning qabriga qo'yish uchun jo'natishni buyurgan ekan. Bir necha kundan keyin esa cho'chqalar Bokser sharafiga xotira ziyofati o'tkazmoqchi ekan. Napoleon nutqini Bokserning ikki sevimli hikmati — «Men yanada ko'proq ishlayman» va «O'rtoq Napoleon har doim haq» — haqidagi eslatma bilan tugatdi; uning aytishicha, har bir hayvon bu hikmatlarni o'ziniki qilib olsa yaxshi bo'lardi.

paras.en: On the day appointed for the banquet a grocer's van drove up from Willingdon and delivered a large wooden crate at the farmhouse. That night there was the sound of uproarious singing, which was followed by what sounded like a violent quarrel and ended at about eleven o'clock with a tremendous crash of glass. No one stirred in the farmhouse before noon on the following day. And the word went round that from somewhere or other the pigs had acquired the money to buy themselves another case of whisky.
paras.uz: Ziyofat uchun belgilangan kuni Uillingdondan baqqolning furgoni kelib, ferma uyiga katta yog'och quti tashlab ketdi. O'sha kechasi shov-shuvli qo'shiq ovozi eshitildi, undan keyin qattiq janjalga o'xshash narsa bo'ldi va soat o'n birlarda dahshatli shisha sinishi bilan tugadi. Ertasi kuni tushgacha ferma uyida hech kim qimirlamadi. Cho'chqalar qayerdandir o'zlariga yana bir quti viski sotib olish uchun pul topishgani haqida gap tarqaldi.
