chapters.recap_uz: Ulushlar «qayta moslashtiriladi», Napoleon Prezident bo'ladi, Mozes qaytib keladi. Kuchdan qolgan Bokser yiqiladi. Uni «kasalxonaga» olib ketayotgan furgonda «Ot so'yuvchi» deb yozilgan bo'ladi. Skviler buni ham oqlaydi, cho'chqalar esa yana viski sotib oladi.

chapters.title: More equal than others

paras.en: Years passed. The seasons came and went, the short animal lives fled by. A time came when there was no one who remembered the old days before the Rebellion, except Clover, Benjamin, Moses the raven, and a number of the pigs.
paras.uz: Yillar o'tdi. Fasllar kelib-ketdi, hayvonlarning qisqa umrlari o'tib ketdi. Shunday vaqt keldiki, Klover, Benjamin, qarg'a Mozes va bir nechta cho'chqadan boshqa Qo'zg'olondan oldingi eski kunlarni eslaydigan hech kim qolmadi.

paras.en: Muriel was dead. Bluebell, Jessie and Pincher were dead. Jones too was dead – he had died in an inebriates’ home in another part of the country. Snowball was forgotten. Boxer was forgotten, except by the few who had known him. Clover was an old stout mare now, stiff in the joints and with a tendency to rheumy eyes. She was two years past the retiring age, but in fact no animal had ever actually retired. The talk of setting aside a corner of the pasture for superannuated animals had long since been dropped. Napoleon was now a mature boar of twenty-four stone. Squealer was so fat that he could with difficulty see out of his eyes. Only old Benjamin was much the same as ever, except for being a little greyer about the muzzle, and, since Boxer's death, more morose and taciturn than ever.
paras.uz: Muriel o'lgan edi. Blyubell, Jessi va Pincher o'lgan edi. Jons ham o'lgan edi — u mamlakatning boshqa bir joyidagi ichkilikbozlar uyida vafot etgan edi. Snoubol unutilgan edi. Bokser ham, uni tanigan bir nechtasidan tashqari, unutilgan edi. Klover endi bo'g'imlari qotib qolgan, ko'zlari yoshlanib turadigan keksa, to'la biya edi. U nafaqa yoshidan ikki yil o'tib ketgan edi, lekin aslida biror hayvon hech qachon nafaqaga chiqmagan edi. Yaylovning bir burchagini keksa hayvonlar uchun ajratish haqidagi gaplar allaqachon to'xtagan edi. Napoleon endi yigirma to'rt stounlik yetuk erkak cho'chqa edi. Skviler shunchalik semirib ketgan ediki, ko'zlari bilan zo'rg'a ko'ra olardi. Faqat keksa Benjamin tumshug'i atrofi biroz oqarganini va Bokser o'limidan beri har qachongidan ham xo'mraygan va kamgap bo'lib qolganini hisobga olmaganda, avvalgidek edi.

paras.en: There were many more creatures on the farm now, though the increase was not so great as had been expected in earlier years. Many animals had been born to whom the Rebellion was only a dim tradition, passed on by word of mouth, and others had been bought who had never heard mention of such a thing before their arrival. The farm possessed three horses now besides Clover. They were fine upstanding beasts, willing workers and good comrades, but very stupid. None of them proved able to learn the alphabet beyond the letter B. They accepted everything that they were told about the Rebellion and the principles of Animalism, especially from Clover, for whom they had an almost filial respect; but it was doubtful whether they understood very much of it.
paras.uz: Endi fermada ancha ko'p jonivorlar bor edi, garchi o'sish oldingi yillarda kutilganidek katta bo'lmasa ham. Qo'zg'olon ular uchun og'izdan-og'izga o'tadigan xira rivoyat bo'lgan ko'p hayvonlar tug'ilgan, kelishlaridan oldin bunday narsa haqida hech eshitmagan boshqalari esa sotib olingan edi. Endi fermada Kloverdan tashqari yana uchta ot bor edi. Ular kelishgan, qaddi-qomatli jonivorlar, ishga tayyor mehnatkashlar va yaxshi o'rtoqlar edi, lekin juda ahmoq edi. Ularning hech biri alifboni B harfidan nariga o'rgana olmadi. Ular Qo'zg'olon va Hayvonizm tamoyillari haqida aytilgan hamma narsani, ayniqsa deyarli farzandlarcha hurmat qiladigan Kloverdan eshitganlarini qabul qilishardi; lekin ulardan ko'p narsani tushunishlari shubhali edi.

paras.en: The farm was more prosperous now, and better organised; it had even been enlarged by two fields which had been bought from Mr Pilkington. The windmill had been successfully completed at last, and the farm possessed a threshing machine and a hay elevator of its own, and various new buildings had been added to it. Whymper had bought himself a dogcart. The windmill, however, had not after all been used for generating electrical power. It was used for milling corn, and brought in a handsome money profit. The animals were hard at work building yet another windmill: when that one was finished, so it was said, the dynamos would be installed. But the luxuries of which Snowball had once taught the animals to dream, the stalls with electric light and hot and cold water, and the three-day week, were no longer talked about. Napoleon had denounced such ideas as contrary to the spirit of Animalism. The truest happiness, he said, lay in working hard and living frugally.
paras.uz: Ferma endi gullab-yashnagan va yaxshiroq tashkil etilgan edi; u hatto janob Pilkingtondan sotib olingan ikki dala hisobiga kengaytirilgan edi. Shamol tegirmoni nihoyat muvaffaqiyatli qurib bitkazilgan edi, fermaning o'z xirmon mashinasi va pichan ko'targichi bor edi, unga turli yangi binolar qo'shilgan edi. Uimper o'ziga ikki g'ildirakli arava sotib olgan edi. Biroq shamol tegirmoni, axir, elektr energiyasi ishlab chiqarish uchun ishlatilmadi. U don tortish uchun ishlatilar va yaxshigina pul foyda keltirardi. Hayvonlar yana bir shamol tegirmonini qurish bilan band edi: aytishlaricha, u tugagach, dinamolar o'rnatilar ekan. Lekin bir vaqtlar Snoubol hayvonlarga orzu qilishni o'rgatgan hashamatlar — elektr chiroqli, issiq va sovuq suvli qo'ralar va uch kunlik ish haftasi haqida endi gapirilmasdi. Napoleon bunday g'oyalarni Hayvonizm ruhiga zid deb qoralagan edi. Eng haqiqiy baxt, dedi u, qattiq mehnat qilish va kamtarona yashashda.

paras.en: Somehow it seemed as though the farm had grown richer without making the animals themselves any richer -except, of course, for the pigs and the dogs. Perhaps this was partly because there were so many pigs and so many dogs. It was not that these creatures did not work, after their fashion. There was, as Squealer was never tired of explaining, endless work in the supervision and organisation of the farm. Much of this work was of a kind that the other animals were too ignorant to understand. For example. Squealer told them that the pigs had to expend enormous labours every day upon mysterious things called ‘files’, ‘reports’, ‘minutes’ and ‘memoranda’. These were large sheets of paper which had to be closely covered with writing, and as soon as they were so covered they were burnt in the furnace. This was of the highest importance for the welfare of the farm, Squealer said. But still, neither pigs nor dogs produced any food by their own labour; and there were very many of them, and their appetites were always good.
paras.uz: Negadir ferma boyib ketgandek, lekin hayvonlarning o'zlari boyimagandek tuyulardi — albatta, cho'chqalar va itlardan tashqari. Ehtimol, bu qisman cho'chqalar ham, itlar ham juda ko'p bo'lgani uchundir. Bu jonivorlar o'zlaricha ishlamas edi, degan gap emas. Skviler tushuntirishdan hech charchamaganidek, fermani nazorat qilish va tashkil etishda tugamas ish bor edi. Bu ishning ko'p qismi boshqa hayvonlar tushunishi uchun juda nodon bo'lgan turdagi ish edi. Masalan, Skviler ularga cho'chqalar har kuni «papkalar», «hisobotlar», «bayonnomalar» va «memorandumlar» deb ataladigan sirli narsalarga ulkan mehnat sarflashlari kerakligini aytdi. Bular zich yozuv bilan to'ldirilishi kerak bo'lgan katta qog'oz varaqlari edi va ular shunday to'ldirilishi bilanoq o'choqda yoqib yuborilardi. Bu ferma farovonligi uchun eng muhim ahamiyatga ega, dedi Skviler. Lekin baribir na cho'chqalar, na itlar o'z mehnati bilan hech qanday oziq-ovqat ishlab chiqarmasdi; ular esa juda ko'p edi va ishtahalari doim yaxshi edi.

paras.en: As for the others, their life, so far as they knew, was as it had always been. They were generally hungry, they slept on straw, they drank from the pool, they laboured in the fields; in winter they were troubled by the cold, and in summer by the flies. Sometimes the older ones among them racked their dim memories and tried to determine whether in the early days of the Rebellion, when Jones's expulsion was still recent, things had been better or worse than now. They could not remember. There was nothing with which they could compare their present lives: they had nothing to go upon except Squealer's lists of figures, which invariably demonstrated that everything was getting better and better. The animals found the problem insoluble; in any case they had little time for speculating on such things now. Only old Benjamin professed to remember every detail of his long life and to know that things never had been, nor ever could be, much better or much worse – hunger, hardship and disappointment being, so he said, the unalterable law of life.
paras.uz: Boshqalarga kelsak, ularning hayoti, ular bilishicha, doim qanday bo'lsa, shunday edi. Ular odatda och edilar, somonda uxlashar, hovuzdan suv ichishar, dalalarda mehnat qilishardi; qishda ularni sovuq, yozda esa pashshalar qiynardi. Ba'zan ularning keksaroqlari xira xotiralarini titkilab, Qo'zg'olonning dastlabki kunlarida, Jons haydalganiga hali ko'p bo'lmaganda, ahvol hozirgidan yaxshiroq yoki yomonroq bo'lganini aniqlashga urinishardi. Ular eslay olishmasdi. Hozirgi hayotlarini solishtiradigan hech narsa yo'q edi: ularning Skvilerning raqamlar ro'yxatlaridan boshqa tayanadigan narsasi yo'q edi, ular esa har doim hamma narsa tobora yaxshilanib borayotganini ko'rsatardi. Hayvonlar bu muammoni yechib bo'lmas deb topishdi; har holda endi bunday narsalar haqida mulohaza yuritishga vaqtlari kam edi. Faqat keksa Benjamin uzoq umrining har bir tafsilotini eslashini va narsalar hech qachon ancha yaxshi yoki ancha yomon bo'lmaganini va bo'lishi ham mumkin emasligini bilishini aytardi — uning aytishicha, ochlik, mashaqqat va umidsizlik hayotning o'zgarmas qonuni edi.

paras.en: And yet the animals never gave up hope. More, they never lost, even for an instant, their sense of honour and privilege in being members of Animal Farm. They were still the only farm in the whole county – in all England! – owned and operated by animals. Not one of them, not even the youngest, not even the newcomers who had been brought from farms ten or twenty miles away, ever ceased to marvel at that. And when they heard the gun booming and saw the green flag fluttering at the masthead, their hearts swelled with imperishable pride, and the talk turned always towards the old heroic days, the expulsion of Jones, the writing of the Seven Commandments, the great battles in which the human invaders had been defeated. None of the old dreams had been abandoned.
paras.uz: Shunga qaramay hayvonlar hech qachon umidlarini uzishmadi. Bundan ham ko'proq, ular hatto bir lahza ham Hayvonlar fermasi a'zolari bo'lishdan sharaf va imtiyoz tuyg'usini yo'qotishmadi. Ular hali ham butun grafligidagi — butun Angliyadagi! — hayvonlarga tegishli va ular boshqaradigan yagona ferma edi. Ularning birortasi ham, hatto eng yoshi ham, hatto o'n yoki yigirma mil uzoqdagi fermalardan olib kelingan yangi kelganlar ham bundan hayratlanishni hech qachon to'xtatmasdi. Miltiqning gumburlaganini eshitib, ustun boshida hilpirab turgan yashil bayroqni ko'rganlarida esa, yuraklari so'nmas g'urur bilan to'lib ketar va suhbat doim eski qahramonlik kunlariga — Jonsning haydalishiga, Yetti Amrning yozilishiga, inson bosqinchilari mag'lub etilgan buyuk janglarga burilardi. Eski orzulardan birortasi ham tashlab yuborilmagan edi.

paras.en: The Republic of the Animals which Major had foretold, when the green fields of England should be untrodden by human feet, was still believed in. Some day it was coming: it might not be soon, it might not be within the lifetime of any animal now living, but still it was coming. Even the tune of ‘Beasts of England’ was perhaps hummed secretly here and there: at any rate it was a fact that every animal on the farm knew it, though no one would have dared to sing it aloud. It might be that their lives were hard and that not all of their hopes had been fulfilled; but they were conscious that they were not as other animals. If they went hungry, it was not from feeding tyrannical human beings; if they worked hard, at least they worked for themselves. No creature among them went upon two legs. No creature called any other creature ‘Master’. All animals were equal.
paras.uz: Mayor bashorat qilgan, Angliyaning yashil dalalarini inson oyog'i bosmaydigan Hayvonlar Respublikasiga hali ham ishonishardi. Bir kun u keladi: tez orada bo'lmasligi mumkin, hozir tirik bo'lgan biror hayvonning umrida bo'lmasligi mumkin, lekin baribir keladi. Hatto «Angliya hayvonlari»ning kuyi ham balki u yer-bu yerda yashirincha xirgoyi qilinardi: har holda fermadagi har bir hayvon uni bilishi haqiqat edi, garchi hech kim uni ovoz chiqarib kuylashga jur'at etmasa ham. Ehtimol, ularning hayoti og'ir bo'lgandir va umidlarining hammasi ham ro'yobga chiqmagandir; lekin ular boshqa hayvonlarga o'xshamasliklarini anglashardi. Agar och qolishsa, bu zolim insonlarni boqqani uchun emas edi; agar qattiq ishlashsa, hech bo'lmasa o'zlari uchun ishlashardi. Oralarida ikki oyoqda yuradigan biror jonzot yo'q edi. Hech bir jonzot boshqa jonzotni «Xo'jayin» deb atamasdi. Barcha hayvonlar teng edi.

paras.en: One day in early summer Squealer ordered the sheep to follow him and led them out to a piece of waste ground at the other end of the farm, which had become overgrown with birch saplings. The sheep spent the whole day there browsing at the leaves under Squealer's supervision. In the evening he returned to the farmhouse himself, but, as it was warm weather, told the sheep to stay where they were. It ended by their remaining there for a whole week, during which time the other animals saw nothing of them. Squealer was with them for the greater part of every day. He was, he said, teaching them to sing a new song, for which privacy was needed.
paras.uz: Yoz boshida bir kuni Skviler qo'ylarga orqasidan ergashishni buyurdi va ularni fermaning narigi chetidagi qayin nihollari bosib ketgan bo'sh yerga olib bordi. Qo'ylar kun bo'yi u yerda Skviler nazorati ostida barglarni yeb o'tkazishdi. Kechqurun u o'zi ferma uyiga qaytdi, lekin havo iliq bo'lgani uchun qo'ylarga o'sha yerda qolishni aytdi. Oxir-oqibat ular u yerda butun bir hafta qolishdi va bu vaqt davomida boshqa hayvonlar ularni umuman ko'rishmadi. Skviler har kuni ko'p vaqtini ular bilan o'tkazardi. Uning aytishicha, u ularga yangi qo'shiq kuylashni o'rgatayotgan edi va buning uchun xilvat joy kerak edi.

paras.en: It was just after the sheep had returned, on a pleasant evening when the animals had finished work and were making their way back to the farm buildings, that the terrified neighing of a horse sounded from the yard. Startled, the animals stopped in their tracks. It was Clover's voice. She neighed again, and all the animals broke into a gallop and rushed into the yard. Then they saw what Clover had seen.
paras.uz: Qo'ylar qaytib kelganidan keyin, hayvonlar ishni tugatib, ferma binolariga qaytib kelayotgan yoqimli bir oqshomda hovlidan otning dahshatga tushgan kishnashi eshitildi. Cho'chib ketgan hayvonlar joylarida to'xtab qolishdi. Bu Kloverning ovozi edi. U yana kishnadi va barcha hayvonlar chopib hovliga otilishdi. Shunda ular Klover ko'rgan narsani ko'rishdi.

paras.en: It was a pig walking on his hind legs.
paras.uz: Bu orqa oyoqlarida yurib kelayotgan cho'chqa edi.

paras.en: Yes, it was Squealer. A little awkwardly, as though not quite used to supporting his considerable bulk in that position, but with perfect balance, he was strolling across the yard. And a moment later, out from the door of the farmhouse came a long file of pigs, all walking on their hind legs. Some did it better than others, one or two were even a trifle unsteady and looked as though they would have liked the support of a stick, but every one of them made his way right round the yard successfully. And finally there was a tremendous baying of dogs and a shrill crowing from the black cockerel, and out came Napoleon himself, majestically upright, casting haughty glances from side to side, and with his dogs gambolling round him.
paras.uz: Ha, bu Skviler edi. Biroz noqulay, go'yo o'zining ancha katta gavdasini bu holatda ko'tarishga hali to'liq o'rganmagandek, lekin mukammal muvozanat bilan u hovli bo'ylab sayr qilib yurardi. Bir lahzadan keyin ferma uyi eshigidan hammasi orqa oyoqlarida yurayotgan uzun qator cho'chqalar chiqib keldi. Ba'zilari buni boshqalardan yaxshiroq qilardi, bir-ikkitasi hatto biroz gandiraklar va go'yo hassaga suyanishni xohlagandek ko'rinardi, lekin ularning har biri hovlini muvaffaqiyatli aylanib chiqdi. Va nihoyat itlarning dahshatli vovullashi va qora xo'rozning chiyildoq qichqirig'i yangradi va ulug'vor tik turgan, u yoqdan-bu yoqqa mag'rur nigoh tashlagan, atrofida itlari o'ynoqlagan Napoleonning o'zi chiqib keldi.

paras.en: He carried a whip in his trotter.
paras.uz: Uning tuyog'ida qamchi bor edi.

paras.en: There was a deadly silence. Amazed, terrified, huddling together, the animals watched the long line of pigs march slowly round the yard. It was as though the world had turned upside-down. Then there came a moment when the first shock had worn off and when in spite of everything – in spite of their terror of the dogs, and of the habit, developed through long years, of never complaining, never criticising, no matter what happened – they might have uttered some word of protest. But just at that moment, as though at a signal, all the sheep burst out into a tremendous bleating of —
paras.uz: O'lik sukunat cho'kdi. Hayratda, dahshatda, bir-biriga qisilgan hayvonlar uzun cho'chqalar qatorining hovli bo'ylab sekin aylanib yurishini kuzatishdi. Go'yo dunyo ostin-ustun bo'lgandek edi. Keyin birinchi zarba o'tib ketgan va hamma narsaga qaramay — itlardan qo'rquvlariga va uzoq yillar davomida shakllangan, nima bo'lmasin hech qachon shikoyat qilmaslik, hech qachon tanqid qilmaslik odatiga qaramay — ular biror norozilik so'zini aytishlari mumkin bo'lgan lahza keldi. Lekin aynan shu lahzada, go'yo ishora bilan, barcha qo'ylar dahshatli ovozda ma'rab yuborishdi —

paras.en: ‘Four legs good, two legs better! Four legs good, two legs better! Four legs good, two legs better!’
paras.uz: «To'rt oyoq — yaxshi, ikki oyoq — yaxshiroq! To'rt oyoq — yaxshi, ikki oyoq — yaxshiroq! To'rt oyoq — yaxshi, ikki oyoq — yaxshiroq!»

paras.en: It went on for five minutes without stopping. And by the time the sheep had quieted down the chance to utter any protest had passed, for the pigs had marched back into the farmhouse.
paras.uz: Bu besh daqiqa to'xtovsiz davom etdi. Qo'ylar tinchlanganda esa biror norozilik bildirish imkoniyati o'tib ketgan edi, chunki cho'chqalar saf tortib ferma uyiga qaytib kirib ketishgan edi.

paras.en: Benjamin felt a nose nuzzling at his shoulder. He looked round. It was Clover. Her old eyes looked dimmer than ever. Without saying anything she tugged gently at his mane and led him round to the end of the big barn, where the Seven Commandments were written. For a minute or two they stood gazing at the tarred wall with its white lettering.
paras.uz: Benjamin yelkasiga kimningdir burni tekkanini sezdi. U atrofga qaradi. Bu Klover edi. Uning keksa ko'zlari har qachongidan ham xira ko'rinardi. Hech narsa demasdan u yolidan ohista tortib, uni Yetti Amr yozilgan katta molxonaning yon devoriga olib bordi. Bir-ikki daqiqa ular oq harfli qatron surtilgan devorga tikilib turishdi.

paras.en: ‘My sight is failing,’ she said finally. ‘Even when I was young I could not have read what was written there. But it appears to me that that wall looks different. Are the Seven Commandments the same as they used to be, Benjamin?’
paras.uz: «Ko'zim xiralashib qolyapti, — dedi u nihoyat. — Hatto yoshligimda ham u yerda yozilganini o'qiy olmasdim. Lekin menga o'sha devor boshqacha ko'rinayotgandek. Yetti Amr avvalgidekmi, Benjamin?»

paras.en: For once Benjamin consented to break his rule, and he read out to her what was written on the wall. There was nothing there now except a single Commandment. It ran:
paras.uz: Bir marta Benjamin o'z qoidasini buzishga rozi bo'ldi va devorda yozilganini unga o'qib berdi. U yerda endi bitta Amrdan boshqa hech narsa yo'q edi. Unda shunday deyilgan edi:

paras.en: ALL ANIMALS ARE EQUAL BUT SOME ANIMALS ARE MORE EQUAL THAN OTHERS.
paras.uz: BARCHA HAYVONLAR TENG, LEKIN BA'ZI HAYVONLAR BOSHQALARIDAN KO'RA TENGROQ.

paras.en: After that it did not seem strange when next day the pigs who were supervising the work of the farm all carried whips in their trotters. It did not seem strange to learn that the pigs had bought themselves a wireless set, were arranging to install a telephone, and had taken out subscriptions to John Bull, Tit-Bits and the Daily Mirror. It did not seem strange when Napoleon was seen strolling in the farmhouse garden with a pipe in his mouth – no, not even when the pigs took Mr Jones's clothes out of the wardrobes and put them on, Napoleon himself appearing in a black coat, ratcatcher breeches and leather leggings, while his favourite sow appeared in the watered silk dress which Mrs Jones had been used to wear on Sundays.
paras.uz: Shundan keyin ertasi kuni ferma ishini nazorat qilayotgan cho'chqalarning hammasi tuyoqlarida qamchi ko'tarib yurgani g'alati tuyulmadi. Cho'chqalar o'zlariga radio sotib olgani, telefon o'rnatishga tayyorgarlik ko'rayotgani va «Jon Bull», «Tit-Bits» va «Daily Mirror»ga obuna bo'lganini bilish ham g'alati tuyulmadi. Napoleon ferma uyi bog'ida og'zida trubka bilan sayr qilib yurganini ko'rish ham g'alati tuyulmadi — yo'q, hatto cho'chqalar janob Jonsning kiyimlarini shkaflardan olib kiyib olganlarida ham, Napoleonning o'zi qora kamzul, ovchi shim va charm gamashlarda, sevimli ona cho'chqasi esa Jons xonim yakshanba kunlari kiyadigan tovlanuvchi ipak ko'ylakda paydo bo'lganda ham.

paras.en: A week later, in the afternoon, a number of dogcarts drove up to the farm. A deputation of neighbouring farmers had been invited to make a tour of inspection. They were shown all over the farm, and expressed great admiration for everything they saw, especially the windmill. The animals were weeding the turnip field. They worked diligently, hardly raising their faces from the ground, and not knowing whether to be more frightened of the pigs or of the human visitors.
paras.uz: Bir haftadan keyin tushdan keyin fermaga bir nechta ikki g'ildirakli arava kelib to'xtadi. Qo'shni fermerlar delegatsiyasi ko'zdan kechirish uchun taklif qilingan edi. Ularga butun ferma ko'rsatildi va ular ko'rgan hamma narsaga, ayniqsa shamol tegirmoniga katta qoyil qolishlarini bildirishdi. Hayvonlar sholg'om dalasida o'toq qilishayotgan edi. Ular yuzlarini yerdan zo'rg'a ko'tarib, tirishqoqlik bilan ishlashar va cho'chqalardan ko'proq qo'rqish kerakmi yoki inson mehmonlardanmi, bilishmasdi.

paras.en: That evening loud laughter and bursts of singing came from the farmhouse. And suddenly, at the sound of the mingled voices, the animals were stricken with curiosity. What could be happening in there, now that for the first time animals and human beings were meeting on terms of equality? With one accord they began to creep as quietly as possible into the farmhouse garden.
paras.uz: O'sha kuni kechqurun ferma uyidan baland kulgi va qo'shiq sadolari eshitildi. Va birdan aralash ovozlarni eshitib, hayvonlarni qiziqish chulg'ab oldi. Birinchi marta hayvonlar va insonlar teng sharoitda uchrashayotgan bir paytda u yerda nima bo'layotgan bo'lishi mumkin? Bir ovozdan ular iloji boricha jimgina ferma uyi bog'iga o'rmalab kira boshlashdi.

paras.en: At the gate they paused, half frightened to go on, but Clover led the way in. They tiptoed up to the house, and such animals as were tall enough peered in at the dining-room window. There, round the long table, sat half a dozen farmers and half a dozen of the more eminent pigs, Napoleon himself occupying the seat of honour at the head of the table. The pigs appeared completely at ease in their chairs. The company had been enjoying a game of cards, but had broken off for the moment, evidently in order to drink a toast. A large jug was circulating, and the mugs were being refilled with beer. No one noticed the wondering faces of the animals that gazed in at the window.
paras.uz: Darvoza oldida ular davom etishga yarim qo'rqib to'xtashdi, lekin Klover ichkariga boshlab bordi. Ular oyoq uchida uyga yaqinlashishdi va bo'yi yetarli bo'lgan hayvonlar ovqat xonasi derazasidan ichkariga mo'ralashdi. U yerda uzun stol atrofida yarim o'nlab fermerlar va yarim o'nlab eng obro'li cho'chqalar o'tirar, stolning boshidagi sharafli o'rinni Napoleonning o'zi egallagan edi. Cho'chqalar kursilarida butunlay bemalol ko'rinardi. Davra karta o'yinidan zavqlanayotgan edi, lekin ular hozircha o'yinni to'xtatishgan edi, aftidan, qadah ko'tarish uchun. Katta ko'za aylanib yurar va krujkalarga yana pivo quyilardi. Hech kim derazadan qarab turgan hayvonlarning hayratlangan yuzlarini payqamadi.

paras.en: Mr Pilkington, of Foxwood, had stood up, his mug in his hand. In a moment, he said, he would ask the present company to drink a toast. But before doing so there were a few words that he felt it incumbent upon him to say.
paras.uz: Foksvudlik janob Pilkington qo'lida krujka bilan o'rnidan turdi. Bir lahzadan keyin, dedi u, hozir bo'lganlardan qadah ko'tarishni so'raydi. Lekin buni qilishdan oldin aytishni o'z burchi deb bilgan bir necha so'zi bor ekan.

paras.en: It was a source of great satisfaction to him, he said – and, he was sure, to all others present – to feel that a long period of mistrust and misunderstanding had now come to an end. There had been a time – not that he, or any of the present company, had shared such sentiments – but there had been a time when the respected proprietors of Animal Farm had been regarded, he would not say with hostility, but perhaps with a certain measure of misgiving, by their human neighbours. Unfortunate incidents had occurred, mistaken ideas had been current. It had been felt that the existence of a farm owned and operated by pigs was somehow abnormal and was liable to have an unsettling effect in the neighbourhood. Too many farmers had assumed, without due enquiry, that on such a farm a spirit of licence and indiscipline would prevail.
paras.uz: Uzoq davom etgan ishonchsizlik va tushunmovchilik davri endi tugaganini his qilish, dedi u, uning uchun — va, ishonchi komilki, hozir bo'lgan boshqa barcha uchun ham — katta mamnuniyat manbai ekan. Shunday vaqt bo'lgan — u yoki hozir bo'lganlardan birortasi bunday his-tuyg'ularni baham ko'rgani yo'q — lekin shunday vaqt bo'lganki, Hayvonlar fermasining hurmatli egalariga ularning inson qo'shnilari dushmanlik bilan demay qo'ya qolay, lekin balki ma'lum darajada xavotir bilan qarashgan. Baxtsiz voqealar sodir bo'lgan, noto'g'ri g'oyalar yurgan. Cho'chqalarga tegishli va ular boshqaradigan fermaning mavjudligi qandaydir g'ayritabiiy va atrofda bezovtalik keltirib chiqarishi mumkin deb hisoblangan. Juda ko'p fermerlar tegishli tekshiruvsiz bunday fermada o'zboshimchalik va intizomsizlik ruhi hukm suradi, deb taxmin qilishgan.

paras.en: They had been nervous about the effects upon their own animals, or even upon their human employees. But all such doubts were now dispelled. Today he and his friends had visited Animal Farm and inspected every inch of it with their own eyes, and what did they find? Not only the most up-to-date methods, but a discipline and an orderliness which should be an example to all farmers everywhere. He believed that he was right in saying that the lower animals on Animal Farm did more work and received less food than any animals in the county. Indeed he and his fellow-visitors today had observed many features which they intended to introduce on their own farms immediately.
paras.uz: Ular o'z hayvonlariga, hatto o'zlarining inson xizmatchilariga ta'siri haqida xavotirlanishgan. Lekin endi bunday shubhalarning hammasi tarqab ketdi. Bugun u va do'stlari Hayvonlar fermasiga tashrif buyurib, uning har bir qarichini o'z ko'zlari bilan ko'zdan kechirishdi, va nimani topishdi? Nafaqat eng zamonaviy usullarni, balki hamma joydagi barcha fermerlarga namuna bo'lishi kerak bo'lgan intizom va tartiblilikni. Ishonamanki, dedi u, Hayvonlar fermasidagi quyi hayvonlar grafligidagi har qanday hayvondan ko'proq ishlaydi va kamroq ovqat oladi desam, to'g'ri aytgan bo'laman. Haqiqatan ham u va boshqa mehmonlar bugun o'z fermalarida darhol joriy etmoqchi bo'lgan ko'p xususiyatlarni kuzatishgan.

paras.en: He would end his remarks, he said, by emphasising once again the friendly feelings that subsisted, and ought to subsist, between Animal Farm and its neighbours. Between pigs and human beings there was not and there need not be any clash of interests whatever. Their struggles and their difficulties were one. Was not the labour problem the same everywhere? Here it became apparent that Mr Pilkington was about to spring some carefully-prepared witticism on the company, but for a moment he was too overcome by amusement to be able to utter it. After much choking, during which his various chins turned purple, he managed to get it out: ‘If you have your lower animals to contend with,’ he said, ‘we have our lower classes!’ This bon mot set the table in a roar; and Mr Pilkington once again congratulated the pigs on the low rations, the long working-hours and the general absence of pampering which he had observed on Animal Farm.
paras.uz: U so'zini, dedi u, Hayvonlar fermasi va uning qo'shnilari o'rtasida mavjud bo'lgan va mavjud bo'lishi kerak bo'lgan do'stona tuyg'ularni yana bir bor ta'kidlash bilan tugatmoqchi. Cho'chqalar va insonlar o'rtasida hech qanday manfaatlar to'qnashuvi yo'q va bo'lishi ham shart emas. Ularning kurashlari va qiyinchiliklari bir. Mehnat muammosi hamma joyda bir xil emasmi? Shu yerda janob Pilkington davraga puxta tayyorlangan qandaydir hazilni aytmoqchi ekani ayon bo'ldi, lekin bir lahza u kulgidan uni aytolmay qoldi. Uzoq bo'g'ilib, uning bir nechta iyagi binafsha rangga kirgandan keyin u nihoyat uni aytib berdi: «Agar sizlar quyi hayvonlaringiz bilan kurashishga majbur bo'lsangiz, — dedi u, — bizda quyi tabaqalarimiz bor!» Bu bon mot — o'tkir so'z stol atrofidagilarni qah-qah urib kuldirdi; va janob Pilkington yana bir bor cho'chqalarni Hayvonlar fermasida kuzatgan kam ulushlar, uzoq ish soatlari va umuman erkalashning yo'qligi bilan tabrikladi.

paras.en: And now, he said finally, he would ask the company to rise to their feet and make certain that their glasses were full. ‘Gentlemen,’ concluded Mr Pilkington, ‘gentlemen, I give you a toast: To the prosperity of Animal Farm!’
paras.uz: Va endi, dedi u nihoyat, u davradan o'rnidan turishni va qadahlari to'la ekaniga ishonch hosil qilishni so'raydi. «Janoblar, — deb so'zini yakunladi janob Pilkington, — janoblar, sizlarga qadah ko'taraman: Hayvonlar fermasining farovonligi uchun!»

paras.en: There was enthusiastic cheering and stamping of feet. Napoleon was so gratified that he left his place and came round the table to clink his mug against Mr Pilkington's before emptying it. When the cheering had died down, Napoleon, who had remained on his feet, intimated that he too had a few words to say.
paras.uz: Ishtiyoqli olqishlar va oyoq dupurlatishlar yangradi. Napoleon shunchalik mamnun bo'ldiki, joyidan turib, stolni aylanib o'tib, krujkasini bo'shatishdan oldin janob Pilkingtonning krujkasiga urishtirdi. Olqishlar tingach, oyoqda qolgan Napoleon uning ham aytadigan bir necha so'zi borligini bildirdi.

paras.en: Like all of Napoleon's speeches, it was short and to the point. He too, he said, was happy that the period of misunderstanding was at an end. For a long time there had been rumours – circulated, he had reason to think, by some malignant enemy – that there was something subversive and even revolutionary in the outlook of himself and his colleagues. They had been credited with attempting to stir up rebellion among the animals on neighbouring farms. Nothing could be further from the truth! Their sole wish, now and in the past, was to live at peace and in normal business relations with their neighbours. This farm which he had the honour to control, he added, was a co-operative enterprise. The title-deeds, which were in his own possession, were owned by the pigs jointly.
paras.uz: Napoleonning barcha nutqlari singari bu ham qisqa va lo'nda edi. U ham, dedi u, tushunmovchilik davri tugaganidan xursand. Uzoq vaqt davomida — u o'ylashga asosi bor ediki, qandaydir yovuz dushman tarqatgan — uning va hamkasblarining dunyoqarashida qandaydir buzg'unchi va hatto inqilobiy narsa bor, degan mish-mishlar yurgan. Ularni qo'shni fermalardagi hayvonlar orasida qo'zg'olon ko'tarishga urinishda ayblashgan. Haqiqatdan bundan uzoq narsa bo'lishi mumkin emas! Ularning yagona istagi, hozir ham, o'tmishda ham, qo'shnilari bilan tinch va oddiy ish munosabatlarida yashash. Boshqarish sharafiga muyassar bo'lgan bu ferma, deb qo'shimcha qildi u, kooperativ korxona. Uning o'z qo'lida bo'lgan mulk hujjatlari cho'chqalarga birgalikda tegishli.

paras.en: He did not believe, he said, that any of the old suspicions still lingered, but certain changes had been made recently in the routine of the farm which should have the effect of promoting confidence still further. Hitherto the animals on the farm had had a rather foolish custom of addressing one another as ‘Comrade’. This was to be suppressed. There had also been a very strange custom, whose origin was unknown, of marching every Sunday morning past a boar's skull which was nailed to a post in the garden. This too would be suppressed, and the skull had already been buried. His visitors might have observed, too, the green flag which flew from the masthead. If so, they would perhaps have noted that the white hoof and horn with which it had previously been marked had now been removed. It would be a plain green flag from now onwards.
paras.uz: Uning aytishicha, u eski gumonlarning birortasi hali ham qolgan deb ishonmaydi, lekin yaqinda fermaning kundalik tartibida ishonchni yana ham mustahkamlashi kerak bo'lgan ba'zi o'zgarishlar kiritildi. Hozirgacha fermadagi hayvonlarning bir-biriga «O'rtoq» deb murojaat qilishdek ancha ahmoqona odati bor edi. Bu bekor qilinadi. Shuningdek, kelib chiqishi noma'lum bo'lgan juda g'alati odat — har yakshanba ertalab bog'dagi ustunga mixlab qo'yilgan erkak cho'chqa bosh suyagi yonidan saf tortib o'tish odati bor edi. Bu ham bekor qilinadi, bosh suyagi esa allaqachon ko'mib qo'yildi. Mehmonlar, ehtimol, ustun boshida hilpirab turgan yashil bayroqni ham ko'rishgandir. Agar shunday bo'lsa, ular unda ilgari tasvirlangan oq tuyoq va shox endi olib tashlanganini payqashgandir. Bundan buyon u oddiy yashil bayroq bo'ladi.

paras.en: He had only one criticism, he said, to make of Mr Pilkington's excellent and neighbourly speech. Mr Pilkington had referred throughout to ‘Animal Farm’. He could not of course know – for he, Napoleon, was only now for the first time announcing it – that the name ‘Animal Farm’ had been abolished. Henceforward the farm was to be known as ‘The Manor Farm’ – which, he believed, was its correct and original name.
paras.uz: Uning aytishicha, janob Pilkingtonning ajoyib va qo'shnichilikka xos nutqiga faqat bitta tanqidiy fikri bor ekan. Janob Pilkington butun nutqi davomida «Hayvonlar fermasi» deb gapirdi. U, albatta, bila olmasdi — chunki u, Napoleon, buni hozirgina birinchi marta e'lon qilmoqda — «Hayvonlar fermasi» nomi bekor qilingan. Bundan buyon ferma «Manor fermasi» deb ataladi — uning ishonishicha, bu uning to'g'ri va asl nomi.

paras.en: ‘Gentlemen,’ concluded Napoleon, ‘I will give you the same toast as before, but in a different form. Fill your glasses to the brim. Gentlemen, here is my toast: To the prosperity of The Manor Farm!’
paras.uz: «Janoblar, — deb so'zini yakunladi Napoleon, — sizlarga avvalgi qadahni ko'taraman, lekin boshqacha shaklda. Qadahlaringizni lim-lim to'ldiring. Janoblar, mana mening qadahim: «Manor fermasi»ning farovonligi uchun!»

paras.en: There was the same hearty cheering as before, and the mugs were emptied to the dregs. But as the animals outside gazed at the scene, it seemed to them that some strange thing was happening. What was it that had altered in the faces of the pigs? Clover's old dim eyes flitted from one face to another. Some of them had five chins, some had four, some had three. But what was it that seemed to be melting and changing? Then, the applause having come to an end, the company took up their cards and continued the game that had been interrupted, and the animals crept silently away.
paras.uz: Avvalgidek samimiy olqishlar yangradi va krujkalar tagigacha bo'shatildi. Lekin tashqaridagi hayvonlar bu manzarani tomosha qilarkan, ularga qandaydir g'alati narsa sodir bo'layotgandek tuyuldi. Cho'chqalarning yuzlarida nima o'zgardi? Kloverning keksa, xira ko'zlari bir yuzdan boshqasiga yugurdi. Ba'zilarining beshta iyagi, ba'zilarining to'rtta, ba'zilarining uchta iyagi bor edi. Lekin erib, o'zgarib borayotgandek tuyulgan narsa nima edi? Keyin olqishlar tugagach, davra kartalarini olib, to'xtatilgan o'yinni davom ettirdi, hayvonlar esa jimgina sudralib ketishdi.

paras.en: But they had not gone twenty yards when they stopped short. An uproar of voices was coming from the farmhouse. They rushed back and looked through the window again. Yes, a violent quarrel was in progress. There were shoutings, bangings on the table, sharp suspicious glances, furious denials. The source of the trouble appeared to be that Napoleon and Mr Pilkington had each played an ace of spades simultaneously.
paras.uz: Lekin ular yigirma yard ham yurmasdan to'xtab qolishdi. Ferma uyidan ovozlar shovqini kelayotgan edi. Ular yugurib qaytib, yana derazadan qarashdi. Ha, qattiq janjal ketayotgan edi. Baqiriqlar, stolga mushtlar, o'tkir gumonli nigohlar, g'azabli inkorlar. Janjalning manbai Napoleon va janob Pilkington bir vaqtda bittadan qarg'a tuzini tashlaganga o'xshardi.

paras.en: Twelve voices were shouting in anger, and they were all alike. No question, now, what had happened to the faces of the pigs. The creatures outside looked from pig to man, and from man to pig, and from pig to man again: but already it was impossible to say which was which.
paras.uz: O'n ikki ovoz g'azab bilan baqirardi va ularning hammasi bir xil edi. Endi cho'chqalarning yuzlariga nima bo'lgani haqida savol qolmadi. Tashqaridagi jonzotlar cho'chqadan odamga, odamdan cho'chqaga, va yana cho'chqadan odamga qarashardi: lekin qaysi biri qaysi ekanini aytish allaqachon imkonsiz edi.

quiz.q: What is the single Commandment left on the wall?
o: All animals are equal but some animals are more equal than others

quiz.q: What do the animals see at the end?
o: That they cannot tell pig from man

chapters.recap_uz: Yillar o'tadi; Qo'zg'olonni deyarli hech kim eslamaydi. Cho'chqalar orqa oyoqlarida yurib, qamchi ko'taradi. Yetti Amr o'rnida bitta qoida qoladi. Napoleon fermani yana «Manor» deb ataydi, va oxirida hayvonlar cho'chqa va odamni bir-biridan farqlay olmay qoladi.
